title: [LOW] pattern-pack loader + wa.send have no size/depth caps; hostile input can DoS via memory
description:
Found during /security-audit-for-saas pass #8 (pane 5, 2026-04-21).

## Summary
Two unrelated input-validation gaps surfaced while auditing CLI and
MCP argument handling:

- **F1 (MEDIUM):** `load_pack_from_file` at patterns.rs:978 reads
  the entire pattern-pack file into memory via
  `std::fs::read_to_string` with NO size cap, then hands the bytes
  to `serde_yaml::from_str` / `serde_json::from_str` / `toml::
  from_str` with NO depth cap. A hostile `.ft/patterns/huge.yaml`
  (or JSON / TOML) in a cloned repo can exhaust the allocator or
  stack-overflow the YAML parser on deeply-nested constructs.
- **F2 (LOW):** `WaSendTool::call` and `WaRulesTestTool::call` do
  not bound the length of `params.text` before dispatching it.
  An MCP client can submit a multi-gigabyte `text` field; the MCP
  layer will buffer it, policy-evaluate it, and try to send it
  through `wezterm cli send-text`.

## Evidence

### F1
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/patterns.rs:978
  ```rust
  fn load_pack_from_file(path: &str, root: Option<&Path>) -> Result<PatternPack> {
      ...
      let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&resolved)
          .map_err(|e| PatternError::PackNotFound(...))?;
      let pack = match ext.as_str() {
          "yaml" | "yml" => serde_yaml::from_str(&content)...,
          "json" => serde_json::from_str(&content)...,
          "toml" => toml::from_str(&content)...,
          ...
      };
  ```
  No size cap on `content`. No depth cap on the deserializer.
  `serde_yaml` does not guard against billion-laughs by default
  (anchors are resolved in the YAML 1.2 spec), and deeply-nested
  constructs can stack-blow before the typed Deserialize even
  starts. Same attack class as ft-xv561 (ReDoS via hostile
  pattern regex), different primitive.

### F2
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs:1799
  schema declares `"text": { "type": "string" }` with no
  `maxLength`. The tool body does not validate `params.text.len()`
  before `injector.send_text(..., &params.text, ...)`.
- Same gap in `WaRulesTestTool` at :420.
- `WaSendTool` does pass `params.text` through `engine.
  redact_secrets(...)` for the audit summary at :1876, but the
  raw text still goes downstream to wezterm without a length
  bound.

## Impact
Severity: LOW-MEDIUM.

- F1 requires the attacker to land a file inside a workspace the
  user clones, then `ft watch` (or any pattern-engine user)
  inhales it. DoS on the local process, not a remote exploit.
- F2 requires an MCP client — stdio transport runs under the
  user's uid/gid, so the attacker already has process
  equivalence. The concern is operator-hygiene: an auto-MCP
  pipeline that doesn't bound-check outbound `text` could OOM
  the `ft watch` process.

## Fix direction

### F1 — pattern pack loader
1. Cap `content` size before deserialize. Pick a pragmatic limit
   — e.g. `MAX_PACK_BYTES: usize = 1 * 1024 * 1024` (1 MiB). A
   legitimate pattern pack is a handful of rules and text; 1 MiB
   is three orders of magnitude above reasonable. Reject with
   `PatternError::PackTooLarge(path, size)`.
2. Use `serde_yaml::Deserializer::from_str(content).depth_limit(32)`
   — serde_yaml exposes the builder hook; default stack budget
   grows linearly with nesting.
3. Propagate parse errors without embedding the raw content in
   diagnostics (already done via `PatternError::InvalidRule(format!(
   "invalid YAML pack: {e}"))`).

### F2 — wa.send text length
1. Add `MAX_SEND_TEXT_BYTES: usize = 1 * 1024 * 1024` (1 MiB) at
   the WaSendTool::call entry.
2. Reject with `MCP_ERR_INVALID_ARGS` and a hint that pane input
   of legitimate shape should never exceed this bound.
3. Mirror the cap in WaRulesTestTool.

## Non-findings verified in the same pass

- `pane_id` bounds on `ft robot send`: `pane_id: u64` via clap.
  No upper bound at the CLI layer. Downstream `wezterm.send_text`
  looks up the pane by id; a nonexistent id returns
  `WeztermError::PaneNotFound`. No injection vector — `pane_id`
  is decimal-encoded into `--pane-id <N>` arg of `wezterm cli
  send-text`, which cannot be reinterpreted as a shell
  metacharacter. Clean.
- `ft snapshot restore <id>` path traversal: `snapshot_id` is
  parsed via `resolve_checkpoint_id` at main.rs:8208 which
  accepts only the literal "latest" or an `i64`. No path, no
  filesystem lookup. Clean.
- clap `env()` fallback on any arg: grep across
  `crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs` for `env(\"` returned zero
  hits. No argument pulls its value from an environment
  variable, so a process-env manipulation cannot bypass a
  missing CLI flag. Clean.

## Related
- ft-xv561 (070117a0) — same attack class (hostile pattern pack
  → DoS), different primitive (regex backtrack vs YAML parse).
- ft-kegvt (969b9e02) — same "restricted-input" family: user-
  supplied strings flowing into a trusted sink without a
  structural cap.

Filed per /security-audit-for-saas pass #8.
close_reason: Closed by e8397747. F1 pattern-pack loader: new MAX_PACK_BYTES=1 MiB constant; load_pack_from_file stats before read, then double-checks bytes after read (TOCTOU belt-and-suspenders). Rejects with PatternError::InvalidRule citing observed size, cap, and ft-05hfm tag. F2 wa.send text cap: new MAX_SEND_TEXT_BYTES=1 MiB; WaSendTool::call rejects oversize payloads with MCP_ERR_INVALID_ARGS before any runtime setup, storage open, pane lookup, or policy evaluation. 6 regression tests (3 patterns.rs, 3 mcp_tools.rs): oversize YAML reject, cap-boundary accept, oversize JSON reject, constant pin, schema field guard, typical-paste headroom. Full WaSendTool::call e2e test deferred as it requires real McpContext + wezterm + runtime harness; the pure-check boundary is three direct lines of if-guard any reviewer can eyeball. On-disk format + public API unchanged. Both MAX_* are pub(crate).

title: redactor misses quoted Authorization bearer tokens
description:
File: crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:40-42
Current state: BEARER_TOKEN only matches `Authorization: Bearer ...` style text and misses common quoted/JSON header forms such as `"Authorization":"Bearer <token>"`, plus bare `Bearer <token>` payloads.
Risk: MCP/export/audit/read surfaces that rely on Redactor can leak bearer credentials when they appear in serialized header maps or structured payloads instead of the exact plain header string.
Should replace with: a bearer regex that handles quoted Authorization keys, optional quoted values, and plain Bearer-prefixed tokens; add regressions covering both shapes in redactor tests.

title: [iterm2_osc_1337.fix] is_safe returns true when only rejections have happened
description:
5th instance of the is_safe-rubber-stamp pattern this review pass.

Bug found in fresh-eyes pattern-grep across the codebase for the same shape as ft-ismxr.

## Defect

iterm2_osc_1337.rs:561-568:

    pub fn is_safe(&self) -> bool {
        if self.commands_total == 0 {
            return true;
        }
        let total = self.commands_total + self.rejected_total;
        let rejection_ratio = self.rejected_total as f64 / total as f64;
        rejection_ratio <= 0.05
    }

When commands_total == 0 but rejected_total > 0: returns true. But that means EVERY OSC 1337 command has been rejected — 100% rejection, the worst possible state.

## Why it matters

OSC 1337 is iTerm2's image / file-display protocol. The rejected counter increments when a command fails security gates. A scenario where every command is rejected (e.g., all commands are security-failing, or the parser is broken) reports as healthy.

## Fix

Same shape as ft-ismxr's fix: when commands_total == 0, return true iff rejected_total is also 0.

## Acceptance

- is_safe returns false when rejected > 0 and commands == 0.
- is_safe still returns true when both are 0 (truly idle).

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/iterm2_osc_1337.rs:561-568
- ft-ismxr (sibling — same pattern in lock_manager_health)
- ft-ftepl, ft-vgtab, ft-cof0r (the other rubber-stamp instances)
notes:
Fix landed at commit 9a19c5b32. Osc1337Health::is_safe now rejects pure-rejection-storm (commands_total==0 with rejected_total>0).

Same shape fix as ft-ismxr in lock_manager_health. Discovered via systematic codebase grep for the rubber-stamp pattern.

2 new regression tests verified passing:
- health_is_safe_rejects_pure_rejection_storm (load-bearing)
- health_is_safe_accepts_truly_idle (boundary)

Pattern-instance count: 5 distinct is_safe rubber-stamp bugs fixed this review pass:
1. ft-ftepl: cumulative counter never resets (render_snapshot_audit)
2. ft-vgtab: counter unconditionally increments (cold_tier_pipeline)
3. ft-cof0r: substring contains() instead of exact match (policy)
4. ft-ismxr: 'if N==0 return true' ignores another counter (lock)
5. ft-05poz (this): same edge-case rubber-stamp (osc 1337)

Other candidate sites scanned this turn but genuinely safe:
- frame_budget_signal_coupling.rs (total = drops + deferrals)
- connector_*_bridge.rs (capacity==0 = intentional dedup bypass)
- kitty_graphics_compositor.rs (total = admitted + rejected)

title: Correct README.md numerical claims: workspace crate count, vendored crate count, and module count
description:
# Goal
Fix the overstated numbers in README.md so the documentation matches reality. Documentation credibility matters — inflated numbers undermine trust in claims that ARE accurate.

# Background
The 2026-04-06 reality check found:
- README claims "120 workspace crates" → Actual: 63 workspace members in root Cargo.toml
- README claims "105 crates" from ex-WezTerm → Actual: 45 active vendored crates in frankenterm/ directory (95+ if counting legacy_wezterm/ checkpoint that isn't part of the workspace)
- README claims "482 modules" → Actual: 483 .rs files (off by 1, essentially correct)
- README claims "775k lines" → Actual: 793,698 lines (grew since README was written)
- README claims "45,000+ tests" → Actual: 46,633 (accurate, slightly understated)

# Changes Required
1. Update "120 workspace crates" to actual count. Options:
   a. "63 workspace crates" (strict workspace members)
   b. "63 workspace crates (plus 95+ legacy reference crates)" (honest with context)
2. Update vendored crate reference to "45 active vendored crates"
3. Update module count to 483 (or "480+" for durability)
4. Update line count to ~794k (or "790k+" for durability)
5. Keep test count as "45,000+" (still accurate)
6. Add a "last verified" date footnote for numerical claims

# Acceptance Criteria
1. Every numerical claim in README.md matches a verifiable count.
2. No claim is inflated. Rounding is always down or uses "N+" notation.
3. Badge at top of README matches actual numbers.
4. AGENTS.md workspace structure section is consistent with README.

# Implementation Notes
- The exact count will drift as development continues, so use "N+" notation for fast-moving numbers.
- The badge "Lines of Code" currently says "775k lines" — update to match.

title: [security-audit] ft robot send <pane> '<text>': secret-bearing text passes through argv (world-readable via /proc, ps, ntm send-key logs)
description:
## Concrete attack

`ft robot send <pane_id> \"<text>\"` is the canonical robot-mode
command for injecting text into a pane (per `docs/cli-reference.md:248`,
`docs/integration-guide.md:366`, README Quickstart §4).

The CLI signature accepts the full text as a positional argv:

```bash
ft robot send 4 \"export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-fake1234567890abcdef...\"
```

Per POSIX, every byte of argv is:

1. **Readable by every other process under the same UID via `ps -e o args`** —
   most operating systems do not redact argv from process listing.
2. **Readable via `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`** on Linux — by default, world-
   readable on most distros (subject to `ProtectKernelTunables` and
   `hidepid` mount options that are NOT default).
3. **Captured by audit subsystems** (auditd, eBPF tracing, journalctl
   process-create events).
4. **Captured by shell history** (`~/.bash_history`, `~/.zsh_history`) —
   even though `histcontrol=ignorespace` exists, the user has to
   actively prefix-with-space.
5. **Captured by NTM's `send-key` tracker** when the orchestrator
   dispatches via `ntm --robot-send` — that history file lives at
   `~/.local/share/ntm/...` and lacks any redaction sweep.

`ft robot get-text` and `wa.search` redact secrets via
`engine.redact_secrets(...)` (per `mcp_tools.rs:1624`). The send
direction does NOT — and CANNOT — redact at the CLI surface
because the argv is captured before any ft code runs.

## Why this is exploitable

Realistic threat models:

1. **Multi-user host.** A swarm running on a shared dev box has
   multiple operators. Operator A sends an API key via `ft robot send`;
   operator B (different UID, but `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` is world-readable
   on most Linux distros) reads it from /proc.

2. **Compromised but limited-shell process.** A malicious agent
   running as the operator's UID can `ps -e o args` to discover
   every secret typed via `ft robot send` over the past minute.

3. **Long-running ntm orchestrator.** `ntm --robot-send` invocations
   pass the same text via NTM's pane-targeting layer; that history
   is persisted on disk in NTM's data dir without redaction.

4. **System log forwarding.** A shop with auditd or eBPF
   process-exec-tracing forwarded to a SIEM exposes every argv
   to the security team — and to anyone who breaches the SIEM.

## Reproduction

```bash
# Terminal 1
ft robot send 4 \"export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-fake1234567890abcdef...\" &

# Terminal 2 (any user / any process under same uid)
ps -e o args | grep 'ft robot send'
# → ft robot send 4 export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-fake1234567890abcdef...

# Or via /proc:
cat /proc/$(pgrep -f 'ft robot send')/cmdline | tr '\\0' ' '
```

## Suggested fix

Three layered controls:

1. **Stdin/file alternative for sensitive payloads.** Add
   `--text-from-stdin` and `--text-from-file=PATH` flags:

   ```bash
   echo \"export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...\" | ft robot send 4 --text-from-stdin
   # Or:
   ft robot send 4 --text-from-file=/run/secrets/api_key.env
   ```

   These read the payload AFTER fork/exec, so it never enters
   argv. Document this as the canonical path for any send that
   could carry secrets.

2. **CLI warning when argv text matches a secret pattern.**
   Before dispatching `ft robot send <pane> <text>`, run the
   text through the redactor; if it would have been redacted,
   emit a stderr warning:

   ```text
   warning: command-line argument matches a known secret pattern
   warning: this text is now visible to other processes via /proc
            and ps. Use --text-from-stdin or --text-from-file
            instead. (Use FT_NO_ARGV_WARN=1 to silence.)
   ```

3. **Documentation update.** README §Safety Guarantees adds:

   > **`ft robot send <text>` argv is NOT a secrets channel.** The
   > full text passes through argv and is visible to every process
   > under the same UID via `ps`, `/proc/*/cmdline`, audit subsystems,
   > and shell/NTM history. Use `--text-from-stdin` or
   > `--text-from-file` for any text that may contain credentials.

4. **NTM-level**: file a sibling bead in NTM (out of scope for
   this repo) to scrub argv-captured text from NTM's persistence
   when it matches the same redactor patterns.

## Out of scope

- Linux kernel `hidepid` configuration (operator's responsibility,
  not ft's).
- Cross-process IPC alternatives (the existing IPC socket path
  already exists for the watch daemon; CLI argv is the
  problematic surface).

## Acceptance criteria

- `--text-from-stdin` and `--text-from-file=PATH` flags land on
  `ft robot send` (and equivalent paths).
- A regression test asserts argv-secret-warning fires on
  detection.
- README + `docs/cli-reference.md` document the secrets-channel
  guidance.
- A canary test in `tests/argv_secrets_warning_test.rs` exercises
  the detector with each redactor pattern.

## References

- `crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs:17644` (RobotCommands::Send
  handler)
- `docs/cli-reference.md:248`,
  `docs/integration-guide.md:366` (docs that recommend the
  argv path today)
- README §Quickstart §4
- Skill: security-audit-for-saas — KEY-MANAGEMENT.md ("secrets
  exposure surface" enumeration must include argv)
- Skill: security-audit-for-saas — Axiom 8 ("attack surfaces
  expand faster than defenses"; argv was added without security
  review)

Filed by cc_1 security audit, 2026-04-28.
close_reason: Audit + 4 fixture tests shipped at 30ac07a84 (commit picked up via another agent's index sweep, confirmed 4 returns 4). Audit finding: persistence path is ALREADY redacted at three storage boundaries — (1) record_audit_action_redacted_with_cx calls Redactor::new() + action.redact_fields BEFORE every persisted send-audit row, (2) ft-3se13 added DECISION_LOG_REDACTOR LazyLock that scrubs reason on every PolicyDecisionLog::record, (3) DryRunReport::redacted() scrubs command/target/policy/actions before output. Plus main.rs:17657 builds the displayed command using redact_for_output(&text) BEFORE constructing CommandContext, so even the dry-run command-string surface is pre-redacted. ft-3xek9 redactor coverage handles Anthropic/OpenAI/xAI/Groq/Google/GitHub/HuggingFace/Replicate/etc. Four new tests in storage.rs::tests pin the AuditActionRecord::redact_fields invariant: redacts_anthropic_key, redacts_openai_key, redacts_github_pat, preserves_clean_text. Each test asserts (a) no plaintext secret remains in any of decision_reason/input_summary/verification_summary/decision_context, (b) at least one field shows [REDACTED] (proves redactor fired). cargo test -p frankenterm-core --lib ft_0ctwe → 4/4 pass. Out of scope: the bead's primary concern is the kernel-level argv leak ( and /proc/cmdline) which the redactor cannot fix — the bead itself documents the proper remediation as new --text-from-stdin / --text-from-file CLI flags that read the payload AFTER fork/exec. That CLI surface change deserves its own bead.

title: [mor:distributed-systems] backpressure drops lose per-pane attribution
description:
# Observation

`BackpressureMetrics::segments_dropped` (crates/frankenterm-core/src/backpressure.rs:224)
is a single `AtomicU64`. When red/black-tier capture shedding fires and
segments are dropped, operators see **how many** were lost but not
**from which pane**.

In an incident ("rate limit slipped past detection at 02:14"), the
on-call needs to determine whether the dropped segment interval
included the pane they're debugging. Today that's un-answerable — the
drops counter is scalar.

# Question

Should we shift `segments_dropped` to a per-pane `AtomicU64` (keyed by
pane_id) so a 3am operator can pivot from "27 segments dropped in the
last minute" to "23 of those were pane 4167 (claude-code), 4 were pane
4203 (codex)"? Memory cost is bounded (≤ 8 bytes × N_panes).

Adjacent thought: the gap marker emitted to storage (`gaps_emitted`)
presumably already carries pane identity; could we expose a thin
aggregate view over gap markers instead of teaching backpressure to
track per-pane, keeping the drop-path allocation-free?

# CAP stance

Current design: chose availability (keep writing, drop segments when
queue full) over consistency (refuse writes to preserve ordering). The
tradeoff is sound for a terminal observation platform — we want the
next byte more than the missed one. But per-pane attribution turns
lost observations into *known* lost observations, which is the
difference between a bug report and a silent false-negative.
close_reason: Fixed in bd8a715e: BackpressureMetrics gains per-pane HashMap (dropped_by_pane: RwLock<HashMap<u64, AtomicU64>>) + 4-method read surface (total, per-pane, snapshot, distinct-pane count). RuntimeMetrics.backpressure: Arc<BackpressureMetrics> threads the metric to native-event drop sites in runtime.rs::emit_native_output_delta and handle_native_event. 6 regression tests including concurrent-drop stress. Changes bundled into the concurrent ft-fbee5 commit during a race; code is in main. native_events.rs EventDispatchOutcome::Backpressure drop site left unwired as a follow-up (no RuntimeMetrics reach from that dispatcher).

title: [ee844ccff review] SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState pressure-cooldown gate is dead in production — fields have no setter
description:
[HIGH] design defect introduced/exposed by commit ee844ccff ("tighten swarm-capacity cooldown + sanitize evidence context").

## Symptom

`SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState` (runtime_telemetry.rs:4387) holds two fields that the cooldown gate reads:

- `last_pressure_action: Option<SwarmCapacityAdmissionAction>`
- `last_pressure_action_at_ms: Option<u64>`

Neither field has a production setter. `grep -n 'self\.last_pressure_action\s*=\|set_last_pressure' crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs` returns 0 hits. The fields appear only in:

- The struct definition (4390, 4393).
- The cooldown read path `cooldown_remaining_secs` (4402-4407).
- Test fixtures that explicitly populate them (lines 10127, 10128, 10166, 10167, 10416, 10417, 10420, 10421).

## Why this is a defect

ee844ccff explicitly tightened the cooldown gate:

```rust
fn cooldown_remaining_secs(&self, now_ms, config) -> Option<u64> {
    if !self.last_pressure_action?.holds_pressure_cooldown() {
        return None;  // <-- short-circuit when None
    }
    ...
}
```

Production callers (e.g. via `SwarmCapacityAdmissionPolicy::plan(state, ...)` at runtime_telemetry.rs:5165) pass a `&SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState` by reference. There is no `&mut self` recorder method on the controller — `impl SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState` has only the read-only `cooldown_remaining_secs`.

Result: production callers always pass `SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState::default()` (or never refresh their copy). `last_pressure_action` is always None, the `?` short-circuits, cooldown returns None, no cooldown is ever enforced. The entire pressure-cooldown logic is dead in production.

## Affected production paths

- `SwarmCapacityAdmissionPolicy::plan` (5165) feeds the dead state into `planned_controller_decision`.
- The Defer/Shed/Throttle/RequireHumanApproval pressure-honoring branches at 5260+ become indistinguishable from the no-cooldown case.
- The br-ft-onheq.5 "dry-run conservative admission and backpressure controller" obligation "controller honors a configured cooldown between pressure actions" is unmet in production wiring.

## Fix shape

Two coordinated parts:

1. **Substrate**: add `SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState::record_decision(&mut self, action: SwarmCapacityAdmissionAction, now_ms: u64)` that updates the two fields when `action.holds_pressure_cooldown()` is true. Tests demonstrate that record→cooldown_remaining_secs round-trip works as designed.

2. **Production wiring**: every `SwarmCapacityAdmissionPolicy::plan(...)` caller must call `state.record_decision(action, now_ms)` after the plan returns. The state ownership question (who holds the long-lived state across plan calls?) needs to be answered — likely a per-process or per-controller singleton.

This bead covers only the substrate (part 1) — file a follow-up for the wiring (part 2) since it touches multiple subsystems and needs design review of state ownership.

## Acceptance

- `SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState` has a public `record_decision(&mut self, action, now_ms)` method.
- New unit tests demonstrate: after `record_decision(Defer, t0)`, `cooldown_remaining_secs(t0+1, config)` returns Some > 0; after `record_decision(Admit, t0)`, returns None.
- A doc-comment on `SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState` flags the wiring obligation + cross-references the follow-up bead.

## Cross-references

- ee844ccff (the commit that exposed/depends on this).
- ft-onheq.5 (the parent bead the controller serves).
- ft-onheq (epic).

## Sweep

A reviewer should also confirm whether `SwarmCapacityFairnessPolicyState` or other sibling controller-state types have the same dead-field pattern. Quick check: `grep -n 'pub struct.*State\b' runtime_telemetry.rs` — audit each for matching read-but-no-write field pairs.

title: [SEC-hardening] policy.rs SystemTime::now() falls back to ts=0 on clock-before-epoch — no observable counter
description:
[SEC-hardening] policy.rs SystemTime::now() falls back to ts=0 on clock-before-epoch with no observable counter

## Defect

Five distinct call sites in `crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs`
read system time and silently fall back to `ts = 0` when the
clock is before UNIX_EPOCH (e.g., pre-NTP-sync boot, VM with
stale RTC, container inheriting a wrong host clock):

| line | function                          | fallback shape                 |
|------|-----------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| 1862 | `now_ms()`                        | `.map_or(0, ...)`              |
| 4388 | `credential_broker_record_denial` | `.unwrap_or_default()`         |
| 5205 | namespace-registry deny path      | `.unwrap_or_default()`         |
| 5832 | `record_to_decision_log`          | `.unwrap_or_default()`         |
| 6171 | AuditActionRecord builder         | `.map_or(0, ...)`              |

Every silent fallback produces ts=0 with NO observable counter.
An operator forensically reviewing audit timestamps cannot tell
whether the chain was generated during a clock-anomaly window
(some/all entries get ts=0, indistinguishable from "many events
happened at exactly the unix-epoch instant").

The decision_log + audit_chain integrate timestamps into hash
content (audit_chain) and ordering predicates (decision_log).
Wrong ts → wrong observable timeline. Hash chain remains
internally consistent (same wrong ts on append + verify), but
correlation with external system events is broken silently.

Same observability shape as ft-luav8 (record_mcp_audit silent-
failure counter): silent state loss without a counter.

## Severity

P3 hardening. Real defect (silent forensic-timeline corruption
under clock-anomaly), but the conditions are rare in steady-state
and the audit hash chain doesn't break — only correlation is
lost. The fix is a small instrumentation addition.

## Repro

```rust
use frankenterm_core::policy::policy_clock_anomaly_count;
let before = policy_clock_anomaly_count();
// ... policy decisions made during clock-anomaly window ...
let after = policy_clock_anomaly_count();
assert!(after > before); // FAILS today — counter doesn't exist
```

## Fix

Add `static POLICY_CLOCK_ANOMALY_COUNT: AtomicU64` to policy.rs
+ `policy_clock_anomaly_count() -> u64` accessor + helper
functions `checked_now_ms_i64()` / `checked_now_ms_u64()` that
increment the counter when `duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)` returns
Err. Replace the 5 inline sites with helper calls.

## Acceptance

- Counter starts at 0.
- Counter increments at every clock-anomaly fallback site.
- All 5 inline sites route through one of the two helpers.
- Helper accessor is `pub fn` (observable from telemetry/doctor).
- Tests pin the counter machinery + the wiring to the helpers.

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs:1862, 4388, 5205, 5832, 6171
- ft-luav8 (sibling — same observability gap shape, MCP audit-write counter)
close_reason: Shipped at 6f6d3218d. Five SystemTime::now() clock-fallback sites in policy.rs (now_ms, credential_broker_record_denial, namespace-registry deny path, record_to_decision_log, AuditActionRecord builder) now route through checked_now_ms_{i64,u64} helpers that increment policy_clock_anomaly_count() on the Err arm of duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH). Public accessor exposed for forensic verification: counter > 0 implies audit chain has ts=0 entries that don't reflect real chronology. 4 tests (counter starts zero / increments per helper / unchanged on real clock / helpers agree to within 100ms) all use the test-only record_policy_clock_anomaly_for_test() shim because pre-epoch SystemTime is non-portable. Verified by grep that zero bare SystemTime::now().duration_since constructs remain in production paths (only the two inside the new helpers themselves). cargo test wedged on unrelated runtime_telemetry.rs WIP from sibling agent — fix verified by inspection.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT-2.2.cont2] Display-pipeline trifecta integration — VRR/scanout/paint.rs wiring + 24h bench + per-compositor CI matrix
description:
# Continuation: VRR + scanout integration

## Context
ft-4vxjb retired at substrate scope (commit 3738540e9):
- VRR negotiation table at `crates/frankenterm-core/src/display_pipeline.rs` — 4 platforms x WaylandCompositor x X11 Present-extension probe → VrrMechanism + diagnostic VrrFallbackReason
- RefreshRange + negotiate_refresh_range + frame_deadline (cross-link FrameBudget from ft-mpc9b.5.2)
- evaluate_scanout predicate with 6 block reasons (NotFullscreen, CompositorNoDmabuf, BufferFormatNotSupported, VendorModifierNotAdvertised, MultiPaneOverlayPresent, RecordingActive)
- should_force_present priority predicate (manual > a11y > recording > layout)
- decide_present composing all four into PresentAction (PresentNow / ForcePresent / Skip)
- 42 inline tests passing including cross-cut scenarios for Wayland-fullscreen-idle-dedup, macOS-recording-force-present, X11-no-Present-extension full pipeline

Frame-dedup foundation already shipped in 5c54dbf83 at `crates/frankenterm-gui/src/termwindow/render/frame_dedup.rs`. This bead carries the integration work.

## What this bead carries

### Platform probing
- Linux: read `/sys/class/drm/*/edid` for max_hz, query `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` / `XDG_SESSION_TYPE` for VrrPlatform, parse `wp_tearing_control_v1` advertisement from compositor globals to populate WaylandCompositor (plus a heuristic on `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` for Other)
- macOS: CADisplayLink `targetTimestamp` + `preferredFrameRateRange.preferred / minimum / maximum` reads
- Windows: DwmGetCompositionTimingInfo + DwmFlush availability
- Output: feed inputs into `negotiate_vrr_support()` and persist VrrSupport for ft doctor

### Wayland protocol bindings
- `wp_tearing_control_v1` — request `wp_tearing_control_manager_v1.get_tearing_control(surface)` then `wp_tearing_control_v1.set_presentation_hint(async)` per frame
- `linux-dmabuf-v1` — feature-probe modifier list + format support
- `wlr-layer-shell-unstable-v1` for fullscreen exclusive

### X11 XPresent
- `XPresentPixmap` with `PresentOptionAsync` flag when `negotiate_vrr_support` returns `XPresentAsync`
- Skip when `FixedRate` fallback is selected

### macOS CADisplayLink
- `CADisplayLink.preferredFrameRateRange = CAFrameRateRange(minimum:..., maximum:..., preferred:nil)` from `RefreshRange` negotiation
- Match the `60Hz fixed when ProMotion off / 48-120Hz when on` semantics

### paint.rs Present-wiring (subset 2.3 leg of the trifecta)
- Compose `decide_present(vrr, scanout, dedup_decision, force_present)` at the top of paint.rs
- Force-present short-circuits dedup; Skip short-circuits the swap-chain Present
- Per-backend framebuffer readback feeding `compute_frame_hash` (glium ReadPixels vs wgpu Buffer::map_async); decide hash *before* backend Present; mark_presented hash AFTER Present returns
- Remove `#![allow(dead_code)]` from frame_dedup.rs once paint.rs wires it

### Recording detection
- macOS: ScreenCaptureKit `SCStream` enumeration check; populates the `recording_active` input to `should_force_present`
- Linux: PipeWire `pw_registry` scan for `screencast` portal sessions
- Output: feed into both `evaluate_scanout` (block scanout) and `should_force_present` (force-present override)

### ft doctor surface
- Show negotiated VrrSupport (mechanism + fallback_reason) per display
- Show RefreshRange display caps + applied range
- Show ScanoutEligibility per fullscreen surface (Eligible vs Blocked-with-reason)
- Show ForcePresent activations counter (lifetime, per-reason breakdown)
- Show frame_dedup `dedup_rate_pct` + lifetime counters

### Bench
- `crates/frankenterm-core/benches/idle_battery_drain.rs`: 24h idle simulation; assert dedup_rate >=99% (RQ-S5 in docs/perf/resize-quality-slo.md); cross-link RQ-S7 battery drain ≤5% over 24h on M2

### CI matrix
- Per-compositor VRR test (Wayland mutter/kwin/sway/hyprland; X11 i3/Xfwm)
- Direct-scanout test on Wayland fullscreen (assert zero compositor copies via `weston-debug` or compositor-equivalent counter)
- Frame-dedup correctness proptest: identical input bytes → same FrameHash
- A11Y test: assistive-tech announcements not delayed by dedup (force_present arm fires on AT-SPI activity)
- Recording compatibility: when `recording_active`, no frames elided

## Integration ordering
1. Platform probe in `crates/frankenterm-gui/src/main.rs` startup → `VrrSupport` cached in `RenderState`
2. paint.rs frame loop: probe `recording_active` + `a11y_query_in_flight` + layout-changed flag → call `should_force_present` → `decide_present`
3. PresentAction dispatch: `PresentNow` → backend-specific Present with VRR mechanism; `ForcePresent` → bypass dedup, Present anyway; `Skip` → defer to next frame_pacing tick
4. Wayland direct-scanout path: when `decide_present` returns `PresentNow { scanout: Eligible }`, attach dmabuf and submit; otherwise fall back to standard Present
5. ft doctor surface; per-compositor CI matrix; 24h bench

## Acceptance
- Per-compositor VRR test passes on Wayland (mutter/kwin/sway/hyprland) + X11 (i3/Xfwm)
- Direct-scanout bench shows zero compositor copies in fullscreen on Wayland
- Frame-dedup idle-frame Present-skip rate ≥90% on a 5-minute idle workload
- ft doctor reports negotiated refresh rate + dedup_rate per display
- A11Y test passes (force_present fires within 16ms of AT-SPI query)
- Per-release attestation entry cross-link BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G3.1

## Cross-references
- Substrate: commit 3738540e9 (display_pipeline.rs, 42 tests)
- Frame-dedup foundation: 5c54dbf83 (frame_dedup.rs, 17 tests)
- FrameBudget allocator: ft-mpc9b.5.2
- Wayland frame-callback batching: ft-mpc9b.3.2 / ft-28opz
- SLO targets: ft-mpc9b.7 RQ-S5 / RQ-S7 / RQ-S12

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT-2.5.5] Crash-recovery test fixture: kill -9 mid-session integrity
description:
Sub-bead of ft-2okh0.5. Final regression-guard test that proves the kill -9 path actually works end-to-end.

## Scope
1. Test harness: spawn ft as a subprocess with a known input stream.
2. Mid-stream: `kill -9 <ft_pid>`.
3. Restart ft and run `ft session recover <pane_id>`.
4. Assert: scrollback content hash matches pre-kill snapshot byte-for-byte.
5. Assert: pane_uuid preserved across kill.

## Acceptance
- Test fixture lives under crates/frankenterm-core/tests/crash_recovery_kill9.rs.
- Test runs in CI (under cfg(unix) since SIGKILL semantics are unix-only).
- Test fails fast if scrollback content drifts (catches partial-write / msync timing bugs).
- Test fails fast if pane_uuid drifts (catches identity continuity bugs).

Depends on:
- ft-2okh0.5.1 (mmap write path)
- ft-2okh0.5.2 (recovery protocol — recover command must exist)

Cross-references: ft-2okh0.5 (parent).
notes:
Substrate-level regression guards shipped at crates/frankenterm-core/tests/crash_recovery_kill9.rs (commit 708b8689c) — 7 invariant tests green covering the design-doc kill-9 contract (docs/design/crash-safe-scrollback.md):

1. invariant_1_pre_msync_bytes_survive_byte_for_byte: bytes msync'd before the kill survive byte-for-byte; last_msync_at_epoch_ms preserved as the durability marker.
2. invariant_2_pane_uuid_byte_for_byte_continuity: pane_uuid byte-for-byte preserved across simulated kill (uuid with every byte distinct so single-byte drift is detectable).
3. invariant_3_bounded_loss_surfaces_recoverable_tail: partial in-flight record at the tail does not poison the header; file surfaces as Orphaned.
4. invariant_4_mid_header_tear_surfaces_as_corrupt_truncated: mid-header tear surfaces as Corrupt with the structured Truncated reason — never silently mounted.
5. invariant_5_mid_cursor_tear_surfaces_via_cursor_beyond_capacity: torn write_cursor update surfaces via CursorBeyondCapacity rather than a later panic.
6. regression_guard_kill_at_exact_msync_boundary_is_clean: boundary case at HEADER_SIZE + sum(record sizes).
7. regression_guard_kill_immediately_after_header_write: edge case (file is exactly HEADER_SIZE long, ring empty).

Why truncation rather than spawn-and-kill: the bead's full e2e (subprocess + kill -9 + ft session recover) requires MmapScrollback::append (ft-z4u60) and ft session recover CLI (ft-5te6x.cont.cli) — neither is wired. Truncation is the substrate-level analog of kill -9: bytes that *would* have hit MS_SYNC correspond to bytes the OS would have flushed before the kill. The substrate invariants guard the format-level contract; the e2e only needs to prove the wiring honors it under a real signal.

E2e placeholder spawn_and_kill_e2e_placeholder is #[ignore]'d with the explicit unblock list inline (ft-z4u60 + ft-5te6x.cont.cli) and an implementation outline so cargo test -- --ignored lists the deferred coverage gap by name. Once both unblock, drop the #[ignore] and replace the body with the full subprocess fixture.

File is cfg(unix) per the bead's specified scope (kill -9 is POSIX-specific). All 7 substrate guards run in CI today and fail fast if the format/recovery contract drifts.

title: [profiling] TOON encoder: README sells token-efficiency but toon_rust::encode hot path has zero benches
description:
## Hypothesis

`toon_rust::encode(value, None)` (called from
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_middleware.rs:90` and the MCP
helpers) is on the hot path of every `format=toon` robot/MCP
response. README sells it as the token-efficient AI-to-AI output.

There is **no bench** for it. `grep -lE "toon" benches/*.rs`
returns zero hits. The serialization/encoding cost per kilobyte
of pane state, plus the relative cost vs `serde_json::to_string`
and the cost of `try_decode` on the consumer side, is invisible.

## Why a profile + bench would deliver real perf gain

A swarm operating 200+ panes calls `wa.state` repeatedly, with
TOON output. If TOON encoding is even 2-3× slower than JSON, the
"token-efficient" framing is a poor tradeoff at swarm scale (you
trade encoder CPU on the ft side for decoder savings on the
agent side). Today no one has measured this:

- Encoder CPU per KB of pane-state Value
- Decoder CPU on the round-trip
- Output size (tokens vs JSON) at the realistic envelope shapes
  (`wa.state`, `wa.search`, `wa.events`)
- Allocation profile (does TOON allocate per cell? per row?)

## Suggested instrumentation + bench

1. **Bench**: `crates/frankenterm-core/benches/toon_encoding.rs`,
   criterion harness with three workloads:
   - `wa.state` payload at 1, 10, 50, 200 panes (matches the
     scaling-law disciplines — p95 ratio across pane counts).
   - `wa.search` payload at 10, 100, 1000 hits.
   - `wa.events` payload at 10, 100, 1000 events.
   For each: `serde_json::to_string` baseline + `toon_rust::encode`
   side-by-side. Track p50/p95/p99 + bytes/op.

2. **Instrumentation**: `tracing::instrument(skip_all)` on the
   MCP middleware encode call site, with a `format` field tag.
   Histogram: `metrics::histogram!("mcp.encode_ms", ..., format)`.

title: [SEV] mux-server Alert-after-PaneRemoved re-inserts HashMap entry, permanent leak
description:
crates/frankenterm-mux-server-impl/src/dispatch.rs:256 processes MuxNotification::Alert by calling handler.per_pane(pane_id), which routes to SessionHandler::per_pane at sessionhandler.rs:282. That function uses HashMap::entry(..).or_insert_with(..) — a get-or-insert. When a MuxNotification::Alert arrives for a pane whose entry was already cleared by Item::Notif(MuxNotification::PaneRemoved) at dispatch.rs:247, the or_insert_with re-creates a fresh PerPane entry. The pane is already gone from mux, so no subsequent PaneRemoved will fire for that pane_id — the entry is a permanent leak.

Concrete interleaving:
  1. Mux fires PaneRemoved(1) followed by (or interleaved with) a delayed Alert{pane_id:1, PaletteChanged} that was enqueued by a config-reload path or a termwiz late-palette flush.
  2. Dispatch loop processes PaneRemoved -> handler.remove_per_pane(1) clears the map entry (line 247).
  3. Dispatch loop processes Alert -> handler.per_pane(1) -> or_insert_with -> re-creates an entry (line 256).
  4. Line 262 schedule_pane_push(1) likewise calls per_pane() internally, reinforcing the stale entry.
  5. No further PaneRemoved for pane 1 is ever emitted (pane already killed). Entry leaks for the lifetime of the ClientSession.

Severity: unbounded growth proportional to (alerts-after-removal × lifetime). Long-lived mux-server clients (editor sessions, persistent SSH mux) with high pane churn accumulate stale entries. Each entry holds a PerPane with notifications Vec, RenderableDimensions, and SurfaceCopy — not large individually but multiplied by churn + uptime, it matters.

Fix: expose a non-inserting accessor SessionHandler::per_pane_if_present(pane_id) -> Option<Arc<Mutex<PerPane>>> and use it for the Alert arm. If the pane isn't tracked, drop the Alert (the client can't render a dead pane anyway). Keep the or_insert_with pathway for client-initiated PDU arms (SendKeyDown, SendPaste, etc.) where insertion on first reference is correct. Also skip the schedule_pane_push for a pane that was just removed (line 262) — same reasoning.
close_reason: Completed: added SessionHandler::per_pane_if_present non-inserting accessor and routed dispatch.rs Alert arm through it. Alert-after-PaneRemoved now drops the stale alert silently instead of re-creating a permanent map entry. Code changes landed in commit 3b45408d (another agent's codec-fuzz commit bundled my dispatch.rs + sessionhandler.rs edits into their push — my 37 lines are present in HEAD). cargo check -p frankenterm-mux-server-impl --offline passed clean in 13.28s during my local verification.

title: [PERF] stable_json_hash hot path: ~4 calls + ~12 allocations per SwarmCapacityAdmissionPolicy::plan round
description:
Phase-2 profiling pass on runtime/telemetry domain identified `stable_json_hash` (runtime_telemetry.rs:7322) as the densest per-decision hot path in the swarm capacity admission flow.

## Per-decision call graph

A single `SwarmCapacityAdmissionPolicy::plan(...)` round produces (per decision):

1. `SwarmCapacityAdmissionAuditRecord::new` — calls `stable_json_hash` 2× (once on `request.redacted_context`, once on the 13-element `record_id` derivation tuple).
2. `SwarmCapacityEvidenceRecord::new` — calls `stable_json_hash` 3× (certificate_hash, tail_risk_report_hash, config_snapshot_hash).
3. Plus calls in the bundle-assembly path (env_snapshot, fairness_policy_hash, etc.).

Estimate: **4-7 `stable_json_hash` invocations per admission decision**, depending on which evidence-record paths fire.

## Per-call cost breakdown

```rust
fn stable_json_hash<T: Serialize>(value: &T) -> String {
    let json = serde_json::to_string(value)         // alloc 1: JSON String
        .unwrap_or_else(|err| format!(r#"{{\"serialization_error\":\"{err}\"}}"#));
    format!("sha256:{}", stable_hash(&json))        // alloc 3: format! result
                                                    // (stable_hash internally allocs hex String — alloc 2)
}
```

Each call allocates **~3 Strings** (JSON, hex digest, sha256-prefixed result). For a 200-agent fleet at the documented `wa.search` / `wa.get_text` / web `/search` decision rate, this scales to **thousands of allocations per second** purely for record-id derivation.

## Bench

Added a `#[ignore]`-gated microbench at runtime_telemetry.rs:8XXX:

```text
#[test]
#[ignore = "microbench — run with --ignored to enable"]
fn bench_stable_json_hash_admission_request() { ... }
```

It times 10,000 `stable_json_hash` calls on a representative `SwarmCapacityAdmissionRequest`, reports min / median / mean / p99 / p99.9 / max + p99/median ratio. Asserts a 100µs sanity floor on median + warns at p99/median > 5×.

Run: `cargo test --lib -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features bench_stable_json_hash_admission_request -- --ignored --nocapture`. Bench numbers will be appended to this bead in a follow-up comment once a build slot frees up; current bench compile blocked on shared-target file lock contention.

## Optimization shapes (when we have numbers)

If the bench shows median in the tens of µs and p99 in the hundreds (likely under contention), the wins come from:

1. **Cache the config_snapshot_hash**: the snapshot changes only when admission/fairness/ledger config changes (rare). Compute once + memoize behind `OnceLock<String>` keyed by the config-tuple.
2. **Pre-allocate output buffers**: replace `format!("sha256:{}", ...)` with a manual concat into a `String::with_capacity(72)` (`"sha256:"` is 7 bytes, hex is 64 = exactly 71). One alloc instead of two.
3. **Avoid hex String entirely**: hash → hex is ~64 bytes; the consumer (record_id, hash field) is ALSO 64 bytes. Replace the hex String with a fixed-size `[u8; 64]` newtype that derives Serialize/Deserialize as hex. Saves one alloc.
4. **Use `serde_json::to_writer`** with a `Vec<u8>` capacity hint instead of `to_string`. Same byte count, fewer realloc cycles for medium-sized payloads.

Total potential savings: ~3 allocs/call → ~1 alloc/call = **3× allocation reduction** on the admission hot path.

## Acceptance

- `bench_stable_json_hash_admission_request` reports median, p99, p99/median in CI logs (when run with --ignored).
- A follow-up bead lands ONE of the optimization shapes above (most likely #1 — cache config_snapshot_hash, since it's the cheapest design + biggest win for the typical case where config is stable).

## Cross-references

- runtime_telemetry.rs:7322 (`stable_json_hash` definition).
- runtime_telemetry.rs:1856 (`stable_hash` SHA256 helper).
- runtime_telemetry.rs:4495+ (`SwarmCapacityAdmissionAuditRecord::new`, 2 calls).
- runtime_telemetry.rs:5500+ (`SwarmCapacityEvidenceRecord::new`, 3 calls).
- ee844ccff (the "sanitize evidence context" commit that added the per-record hash chain).
close_reason: done

The unavoidable serde_json::to_string allocation remains; further wins documented in this bead's body (config_snapshot_hash caching + to_writer(Vec<u8>)) are separate scope. title: Capability Passport and Preflight Probe Ledger for every pane/agent
description:
Build a machine-checkable capability passport for each pane/agent/session: model family, tool availability, auth surfaces, filesystem scope, network policy, expected runtime wrapper, cargo target dir policy, and known safety constraints.

- Add a passport schema with redacted fields and stable hashes for sensitive proofs.
- Add preflight probes that are bounded, read-only, and safe under AGENTS.md constraints.
- Expose robot/doctor output that distinguishes observed, declared, and verified capabilities.
- Preserve fallback behavior: if a probe fails or times out, mark unknown/unsafe rather than guessing.

- Unit tests for schema serde, redaction, stale probe expiry, and fail-closed behavior.
- E2E fixture with mixed cc/cod/gmi-like panes proving dispatch filters unsupported tasks.
- Logging must show probe budget, result class, and no secret leakage.

- Passport schema includes verified/declared/observed states and redacted sensitive proofs.
- Bounded read-only probes fail closed to unknown/unsafe on error or timeout.
- Robot/doctor output shows capability freshness, source, and confidence.

title: Token/IO Rate-Distortion Controller for capture, compression, and robot output
description:
Create a controller that allocates capture detail, compression level, tail lengths, TOON/JSON verbosity, and search excerpt budgets using a rate-distortion objective: preserve decision-relevant information under token, CPU, memory, and latency budgets.

Why it matters: massive swarms can overwhelm both storage and AI consumers. The right question is not "capture less" but "capture the most useful bits for the current mission and incident risk."

Math/artifact fit:
- Rate-distortion and information theory for budgeted summaries.
- Bandit feedback for which detail levels help downstream decisions.
- Explicit distortion metrics tied to pattern/search/replay correctness.

Proof/tests:
- Golden outputs proving critical detections remain preserved under compression.
- Benchmarks for CPU/memory/tokens before and after on synthetic 50-pane traces.
- Fallback: fixed conservative capture profile when learned/controller state is unavailable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Controller defines explicit distortion metrics tied to pattern/search/replay correctness.
- Budgeted profiles cover capture detail, compression, robot output format, tail length, and excerpts.
- Golden tests prove critical detections survive constrained profiles.
- Bench/e2e compares CPU, memory, token output, and correctness on synthetic 50-pane traces.
close_reason: Implemented and verified rate-distortion controller substrate

title: Signed Pattern Pack Supply Chain with fixture-coverage and regex-safety attestations
description:
Add a signed pattern-pack pipeline: provenance, fixture coverage, regex-safety checks, redaction review, and versioned rollout metadata for rule packs.

Why it matters: pattern rules can trigger workflows and policy decisions. A bad or malicious pack can create false actions, miss critical states, or burn CPU through regex risk.

Implementation shape:
- Define pack manifest fields: author, source, fixture hashes, lint results, regex backtrack budget, redaction review, and compatibility target.
- Add verification commands and doctor output for installed packs.
- Support staged rollout with dry-run match telemetry before enforcement.
- Fallback: unsigned/unverified packs can run in observe-only mode but not action-triggering mode.

Proof/tests:
- Unit tests for manifest parsing, signature failure, fixture mismatch, and unsafe regex rejection.
- E2E install/verify/use flow with a signed test pack and a deliberately invalid pack.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pattern pack manifest records provenance, fixture hashes, lint output, regex budget, redaction review, and compatibility target.
- Verification rejects invalid signatures, fixture drift, unsafe regex, and incompatible targets.
- Observe-only fallback exists for unsigned/unverified packs and cannot trigger actions.
- E2E install/verify/use test covers valid and deliberately invalid packs.
close_reason: Implemented and verified signed pattern-pack supply-chain attestation with observe-only fallback.

title: Shadow-mode swarm experiment harness for safe workflow and policy changes
description:
Run new workflows, policies, pattern packs, and load-shedding rules in shadow mode against live or replayed swarm data, recording what would have happened without mutating pane state.

Why it matters: operators need to evaluate automation changes under realistic traffic without risking live agent disruption.

Implementation shape:
- Add a shadow execution envelope that receives real events but writes only to an experiment ledger.
- Compare baseline and candidate decisions with causal/evidence links.
- Support experiment manifests, budgets, and automatic abort on excessive overhead.
- Fallback: if shadow path cannot keep up, record sampling gaps and disable itself.

Proof/tests:
- Unit tests for no-side-effect guarantees and ledger schema.
- Replay/e2e with candidate policy that differs from baseline, verifying pane state is unchanged and deltas are logged.
- Performance gate for overhead under synthetic 50-pane event load.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Shadow execution receives real/replayed events and writes only to an experiment ledger.
- Baseline/candidate decision deltas cite causal/evidence sources without mutating pane state.
- Unit tests prove no-side-effect boundaries and abort-on-overhead behavior.
- Replay/e2e demonstrates candidate-policy divergence with unchanged pane state.

title: Tail-latency Pareto Frontier Planner for swarm resource knobs
description:
Build an offline/doctor planner that sweeps resource knobs and reports Pareto frontiers for p50/p95/p99 latency, memory, CPU, storage write pressure, and token output quality.

Why it matters: high-end machines make the tuning space large. Operators need evidence-backed presets rather than folklore constants.

Implementation shape:
- Consume synthetic and recorded workload profiles.
- Sweep bounded knobs such as capture concurrency, search batch size, output compression, backpressure thresholds, and telemetry sample caps.
- Emit Pareto-optimal configs plus dominated-config explanations.
- Fallback: if evidence is insufficient, do not recommend; request specific benchmark coverage.

Proof/tests:
- Unit tests for frontier computation, dominance logic, and stable sorting/tie-breaks.
- Bench/e2e script with at least three scenarios and logged machine shape.
- Golden report schema with reproducible input manifest.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Planner computes stable Pareto frontiers with deterministic tie-breaking and dominated-config explanations.
- Inputs include machine shape, workload manifest, resource knobs, and measured metrics.
- Unit tests cover dominance, sorting, sparse evidence refusal, and schema serde.
- Bench/e2e emits reproducible reports for at least three synthetic swarm profiles.

title: Approval Impact Simulator for policy-gated swarm actions
description:
Before asking a human to approve a policy-gated action, simulate and summarize the expected blast radius: panes affected, commands sent, files touched, credentials involved, rollback path, and confidence/unknowns.

Why it matters: approval prompts that only say "allow/deny" do not scale when a workflow can affect many agents. Operators need fast but evidence-rich impact previews.

Implementation shape:
- Reuse tx/dry-run machinery where possible.
- Integrate capability passports and causal graph context.
- Provide concise human output plus machine-readable evidence for audit.
- Fallback: require manual approval with no automation if simulation is incomplete.

Proof/tests:
- Unit tests for redaction, unknown propagation, rollback field requirements, and deny/require-approval cases.
- E2E workflow dry-run showing preview then approved execution with matching audit record.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Approval preview summarizes panes affected, commands, file scope, credentials class, rollback, and unknowns.
- Incomplete simulation requires manual approval and does not imply safety.
- Unit tests cover redaction, unknown propagation, deny/require-approval, and rollback-field requirements.
- E2E dry-run preview matches the approved execution audit record.

title: Agent onboarding stress capsule for verifying new machines and panes

- Include optional high-end machine checks for CPU/RAM/core-aware profiles.

title: Cross-pane causal graph ledger for swarm events, missions, and policy decisions

Implementation shape:

- Persist a bounded per-session graph with retention and redaction controls.
- Expose robot/doctor queries for ancestors, descendants, shortest causal path, and suspicious gaps.
- Degrade gracefully: missing data becomes an uncertainty edge, not a fabricated fact.

Proof/tests:
- Unit tests for edge invariants, cycle handling, retention, and redaction.
- Replay/e2e test that produces a known multi-pane chain and verifies ordered causal subsequences.
- Detailed logging for every inferred edge with confidence and source evidence.

- Causal edge schema distinguishes observed, inferred, temporal, policy, mission, storage, and user-action evidence.
- Ledger query APIs return ancestors, descendants, shortest path, and uncertainty gaps without fabricating facts.
- Unit tests cover retention, redaction, cycle/partial-order handling, and edge invariants.
- Replay/e2e test produces a known multi-pane causal chain and verifies ordered subsequences.

title: Synthetic swarm fixture factory for reproducible high-scale operator scenarios
description:
Build a fixture factory that generates deterministic 10/50/100/200-pane swarm scenarios without requiring real vendor credentials, while still exercising real ft runtime, pattern, workflow, search, storage, and policy paths.

Why it matters: many valuable proofs are currently operator-only or credential-dependent. A synthetic factory lets CI and agents reproduce overload, drift, recovery, and incident scenarios safely.

Implementation shape:
- Provide deterministic pane-output scripts for rate limits, tool failures, long-running jobs, malformed output, and recovery successes.
- Include scenario manifests with budgets, expected events, and exact verifier commands.
- Do not fake the ft paths under test; only fake external agent/vendor output.
- Keep fixture generation bounded and redaction-safe.

Proof/tests:
- Golden scenario manifests with hashes.
- E2E scripts with detailed logs for at least 10-pane and 50-pane profiles.
- Negative tests proving missing expected events fail loudly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Deterministic 10/50/100/200-pane scenario manifests exist with expected events and verifier commands.
- Fixture paths exercise real ft runtime/pattern/workflow/search/storage/policy code while faking only external agent output.
- Golden hashes and negative tests prove missing expected events fail loudly.
- E2E logs include scenario seed, pane count, budgets, expected events, and actual event matches.

It generates 10/50/100/200-pane manifests with seed, budgets, verifier commands, expected pattern hits, checksum, pane scripts, and causally ordered recorder events. Verifier drives real PatternEngine detection plus search::build_semantic_chunks and records actual/expected hits and budget checks; tests cover deterministic generation, all-scale verification, tamper-negative failure, causal ordering, and real AppendLogRecorderStorage append health. title: Swarm Incident Autopsy Compiler with redacted causal postmortem bundles
description:
Compile a redacted, reproducible incident bundle from a session: causal graph, top pattern hits, mission/tx log, policy denials, storage health, pane excerpts, timeline, suspected root causes, and replay instructions.

Why it matters: world-class swarm operations require post-incident understanding. Operators should get a compact, evidence-backed autopsy instead of manually stitching logs from many panes.

Implementation shape:
- Add `ft incident compile` or equivalent robot surface that accepts session/time/pane filters.
- Include a deterministic manifest with source hashes and redaction policy version.
- Generate a human-readable report plus machine-readable JSON/TOON.
- Rank hypotheses conservatively; every claim must cite evidence or be labelled inferred/unknown.

Proof/tests:
- Unit tests for bundle schema, redaction, evidence citation, and missing-data behavior.
- E2E replay from synthetic fixture factory producing a stable autopsy hash except timestamps.
- Logging must identify every artifact included/excluded and why.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Incident compiler emits redacted human report plus JSON/TOON manifest with source hashes.
- Every root-cause hypothesis is evidence-cited or labelled inferred/unknown.
- Unit tests cover schema, redaction, source inclusion/exclusion, and missing-data behavior.
- Synthetic replay e2e produces a stable autopsy bundle and verifies report sections.

title: Portable Operator Handoff Capsules for moving swarm state across panes or machines
description:
Create signed handoff capsules that let an operator move useful swarm state between panes, machines, or future sessions: mission state, relevant context, capability passport excerpts, causal summary, pending approvals, and verification checklist.

Why it matters: long-running agent swarms need shift handoff and machine migration. A capsule prevents context loss while preserving security boundaries.

Implementation shape:
- Define a portable capsule schema with versioning, redaction, integrity hash, and optional encryption hook.
- Add export/import commands with dry-run validation and conflict reporting.
- Include compatibility checks against destination pane capability passports.
- Fallback: if a field cannot be proven safe, omit it and record an explicit gap.

Proof/tests:
- Unit tests for schema migration, integrity mismatch, redaction, and fail-closed import.
- E2E test exporting from one synthetic session and importing into another with expected skipped/accepted fields.
- Detailed logs for every included, redacted, or rejected section.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Capsule schema is versioned, integrity-checked, redaction-safe, and optionally encryption-ready.
- Export/import dry-run validates destination capability compatibility and reports conflicts.
- Unit tests cover migration, tamper detection, rejected unsafe fields, and fail-closed import.
- E2E moves a capsule between synthetic sessions with expected accepted/skipped fields.

title: Mission-aware load shedding and utility scheduler for overloaded swarms
description:
Implement a mission-aware overload controller that protects high-value work when CPU, memory, storage, API quota, or human attention budgets saturate.

Why it matters: at 64+ cores and 256GB+ RAM, the bottleneck shifts between local resources, API quota, and operator attention. Load shedding must respect mission value, dependencies, and safety, not just raw queue length.

Math/artifact fit:
- Queueing/control theory for stability and hysteresis.
- Bayesian/VOI utility estimates for which panes to slow, pause, or keep alive.
- Finite-sample tail monitors to avoid p99 regressions.

Implementation shape:
- Add a dry-run planner first: recommend pause/throttle/admit decisions with evidence.
- Require capability passports and causal graph context before enforcement.
- Fallback: observation-only mode if uncertainty is high.

Proof/tests:
- Unit tests for monotonicity, hysteresis, starvation avoidance, and fail-open/closed policy boundaries.
- Synthetic 50-pane overload e2e with logged decisions and no high-priority mission starvation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Dry-run planner emits mission-aware pause/throttle/admit decisions with utility and uncertainty evidence.
- Controller enforces hysteresis, starvation avoidance, and bounded overhead before action mode is available.
- Unit tests cover monotonicity, unknown capability behavior, and high-priority mission protection.
- 50-pane synthetic overload e2e shows logged decisions and no high-priority starvation.
close_reason: Completed dry-run mission-aware load shedding acceptance: deterministic report/log envelope, uncertainty-aware risk-adjusted utility, high-priority pause protection, bounded state, and synthetic 50-pane overload proof.

title: Prompt Drift Canary and fixture synthesizer for agent output pattern changes
description:
Detect when model/vendor/prompt updates change agent output enough to threaten pattern rules, workflow triggers, or robot orchestration assumptions, then synthesize minimal fixture candidates for review.

Why it matters: agent output changes silently. Pattern packs and recovery workflows need early warning before a real incident misses a rate limit, error, or prompt boundary.

Implementation shape:
- Track rule hit rates, unmatched high-entropy spans, and new repeated output motifs per agent family/version.
- Use sequential change detection with bounded false-alarm budgets.
- Emit candidate corpus snippets with redaction and expected-match scaffolding.
- Never auto-trust a synthesized fixture; open review artifacts and fail conservative.

Proof/tests:
- Unit tests for drift statistic updates, redaction, and false-positive budget accounting.
- Replay/e2e with old/new synthetic agent transcript showing canary alert and fixture draft.
- Logging must include baseline window, alert evidence, and suppression reason.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Drift canary tracks baseline windows, alert thresholds, suppression reasons, and redacted fixture candidates.
- Sequential drift statistic has explicit false-alarm/budget accounting and bounded state.
- Unit tests cover statistic updates, redaction, suppression, and fixture scaffolding.
- Replay/e2e with old/new transcript emits a canary alert and reviewable fixture draft.

title: [mock-finder] Fleet scrollback pressure eviction is advisory only
description:
Production defect found by mock-code-finder in crates/frankenterm-core/src/.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime.rs:2025 wires SnapshotPaneScrollbackAccess into the runtime fleet scrollback coordinator.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/fleet_scrollback_coordinator.rs:529-556 defines the production SnapshotPaneScrollbackAccess adapter and its evict_warm_pages/evict_all_warm methods return 0/no-op.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/fleet_scrollback_coordinator.rs:434 calls panes.evict_all_warm(info.pane_id) during emergency pressure handling.

Impact:
The fleet scrollback coordinator can report and decide on emergency warm-tier eviction, but the production runtime adapter cannot reclaim any warm pages. Under memory pressure the action is a placeholder/no-op while telemetry can imply eviction was attempted.

Expected fix:
Add a real runtime-side warm-eviction mutation hook to the vendored/session scrollback backend, or make the coordinator surface an explicit unsupported/advisory status instead of pretending eviction happened. Add a regression that emergency pressure changes warm bytes or emits a truthful unsupported action record.
close_reason: Enforced snapshot-backed fleet scrollback eviction and verified fleet coordinator tests

title: ft-jwst6 substrate: validate_base64_payload accepts mod-2/mod-3 payloads without padding (malformed base64)
description:
kitty_graphics_compositor.rs validate_base64_payload only rejects body_len % 4 == 1; misses mod=2 and mod=3 (without padding).

Standard base64 padding rules:
- body_len % 4 == 0: needs 0 padding chars
- body_len % 4 == 2: needs 2 ‘=’ padding chars
- body_len % 4 == 3: needs 1 ‘=’ padding char
- body_len % 4 == 1: ALWAYS invalid

Repro: payload = b"abcdef" (6 chars, no padding). body_len=6, stripped=0. Validator returns Valid{decoded_len_estimate=4}. But the decoder would fail — "abcdef" needs "==" suffix to be valid base64. Substrate hands the integration a Valid signal for malformed input.

Fix: after computing body_len, check (body_len + stripped) % 4 == 0 — i.e. the full original length must be a multiple of 4 once the substrate has accounted for padding.

Tracked under self-review pass.
close_reason: Fixed at HEAD: validator now requires (body_len + padding) % 4 == 0 with required-padding computed from body_len mod 4. 6 regression tests pin mod-2/mod-3 boundaries; 2 pre-existing tests updated to use length-valid alphabet-invalid payloads. 40 tests pass.

title: [gui][test] GPU rendering tests and visual regression suite
description:
# GPU rendering tests and visual regression suite

## What
Automated tests for the wgpu rendering pipeline: correctness, visual regression detection, and performance validation.

## Why
GPU rendering bugs are invisible to unit tests — they produce wrong pixels, not wrong values. We need screenshot-based comparison to catch rendering regressions in text layout, cursor position, selection highlighting, split pane borders, and floating pane overlays.

## Tests

### Unit Tests (no GPU required)
- `test_cell_vertex_generation` — cell (row, col) produces correct vertex positions
- `test_atlas_rect_lookup` — glyph lookup returns correct UV coordinates
- `test_atlas_eviction_lru` — LRU evicts least-recently-used glyphs

title: [subpixel_positioning.fix] ScaleFactor public fields bypass denominator!=0 + GCD-canonical invariants
description:
Same public-field-bypass family as ft-jit6o (font_features). Found via systematic sweep for validating constructors with public fields.

## Defect

ScaleFactor in crates/frankenterm-core/src/subpixel_positioning.rs:147-152:

    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
    pub struct ScaleFactor {
        pub numerator: u32,
        pub denominator: u32,
    }

new() validates denominator != 0 + reduces by GCD:

    pub fn new(numerator: u32, denominator: u32) -> Option<Self> {
        if denominator == 0 { return None; }
        let g = gcd_u32(numerator, denominator);
        Some(Self { numerator: numerator / g.max(1), denominator: denominator / g.max(1) })
    }

But direct construction bypasses both:

    let bad = ScaleFactor { numerator: 1, denominator: 0 };
    let r = bad.as_f64();  // f64::from(1) / f64::from(0) → inf

    let non_canonical = ScaleFactor { numerator: 4, denominator: 8 };
    let canonical = ScaleFactor::new(4, 8).unwrap();  // (1, 2)
    assert_ne!(non_canonical, canonical);  // PartialEq breaks

## Why it matters

Two failure modes:

1. denominator=0 → as_f64() returns inf/nan; downstream consumers (subpixel positioning) get nonsensical scale factors.
2. Non-canonical form (4/8 vs 1/2) breaks PartialEq + Hash. Two scale factors that should be equal aren't, and they hash differently. HashMap<ScaleFactor, V> can have duplicate semantically-identical keys.

## Fix

Same shape as ft-jit6o + ChunkBytes::bytes:
- Make fields private.
- Add numerator() / denominator() getters.
- Add as_f64() method (already exists, line 203).
- Existing ONE_X / ONE_25_X consts stay public (already canonical).

## Acceptance

- ScaleFactor fields private.
- Getters added.
- Regression test: cannot construct ScaleFactor with denominator=0 outside new().
- Regression test: PartialEq holds for semantically-equal fractions (already canonical).
- Existing tests still pass.

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/subpixel_positioning.rs:147-180
- ft-jit6o (sibling — same family in font_features)
- ChunkBytes::bytes private-field fix (cold_tier_pipeline)
notes:
Fix landed at commit 46c8f8af9. ScaleFactor fields made private; getters added. 4 regression tests verified.

Same public-field-bypass family as ft-jit6o (font_features AxisValue). Two failure modes both prevented:
1. denominator=0 → inf in as_f64(): structurally impossible.
2. Non-canonical form (4/8 vs 1/2) breaking PartialEq/Hash: structurally impossible.

API impact: zero external callers. All field accesses intra-module.

Pattern catalog updated:
- public-field-bypass family: 2 instances (font_features AxisValue, subpixel ScaleFactor)
- Same shape as ChunkBytes::bytes which the linter privatised earlier this session

title: [testing-fuzzing] crash-detector fuzz target for frankenterm-escape-parser Parser::parse raw bytes
description:
# Motivation

`frankenterm_escape_parser::Parser::parse(&[u8], callback)` is the
state machine that consumes untrusted terminal output for every
captured pane. The crate has 2 existing fuzz targets:

  * `termwiz_csi_parser.rs` — structure-aware around CSI sequences
  * `osc_marker_parser.rs`  — structure-aware around OSC markers

Neither is a plain raw-bytes crash detector. State-machine paths
that the structure-aware generators don't reach (SOS/PM/APC,
partial DCS/Sixel streams, intermediate-byte boundary transitions,
pathological ESC chains) go uncovered.

# Scope

New fuzz target `fuzz/fuzz_targets/escape_parser_raw.rs` that feeds
arbitrary bytes into `Parser::parse` with a no-op callback, asserts
no panic / no infinite loop / no allocator blow-up. Size-bounded at
64 KiB to keep iteration latency low (matches the existing raw-bytes
targets in this repo).

# Invariants (beyond crash-freedom)

1. `parse` consumes all bytes it's fed (state machine never strands).
2. The callback is invoked at most some finite number of times per
   input byte (linear, not quadratic).
3. `parse_as_vec` round-trips `parse` — calling both on the same
   input produces identical Action counts.

# Seed corpus

Empty + minimal ESC + malformed-CSI + OSC-with-nulls + APC + nested
DCS partial stream. 4-5 seeds.

# Build

    cargo +nightly fuzz run escape_parser_raw -- -runs=100000

Targets 2000+ exec/s given escape parsing is hot-path byte-driven
code.
close_reason: Landed as proptest in 503c9506 (frankenterm/escape-parser/tests/proptest_parse_first.rs — 10 properties covering Parser::parse_first + parse_first_as_vec crash-freedom, consumed-offset bounds, determinism, offset-ordering invariant, drain-loop termination + 4 regression tests). The earlier fuzz target shipped in c93fa5f7 hit a libfuzzer-sys SDK-version mismatch on mac and was removed in 5c470432; the proptest provides the same invariant coverage without the link issue.

title: [MEDIUM] survival::ActivityProfile::update_hour NaN-poisons hourly_ewma via clamp
description:
# Defect

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/survival.rs:455` — `ActivityProfile::update_hour`.

Same `f64::clamp(NaN, _, _)` gotcha as ft-761tz / ft-b4l62 / ft-jz40p / ft-0p5q5 / ft-x50ce. A NaN `normalized_activity`:

1. `sample = normalized_activity.clamp(0.0, 1.0)` stays NaN.
2. First sample (sample_count == 0) path writes `self.hourly_ewma[index] = NaN`.
3. Any subsequent EWMA update is `alpha * NaN + (1 - alpha) * prev = NaN`.
4. Every `predict_hour` / `predict` call returns NaN for that hour slot, forever.
5. Downstream survival/hazard math using the predicted activity gets NaN — same silent-wrong-answer class as disk_pressure.

## Fix

Guard at entry: if `normalized_activity.is_nan()`, skip the update entirely. The slot keeps its last good value (or the default if uninitialised) and the next well-formed sample continues the EWMA.

## Tests

* `ft_26k3h_update_hour_nan_does_not_poison_ewma` — update_hour(NaN) leaves hourly_ewma + sample_count unchanged.
* `ft_26k3h_update_hour_nan_then_clean_sample_still_tracks` — end-to-end: NaN → clean sample sequence still produces a finite, sensible EWMA value.

## Scope

Single file (`survival.rs`).
close_reason: done

title: [chaos.fix] ChaosReport.all_passed rubber-stamps empty assertion list
description:
## Defect

ChaosReport::from_scenario at chaos.rs:512:

    all_passed: assertion_results.iter().all(|r| r.passed)

Iterator::all returns true on an empty iterator. So a chaos
scenario with NO assertions configured produces a report with
all_passed: true, assertions_passed: 0, assertions_failed: 0
— silently green.

## Why it matters

Operator running chaos drills sees 'all_passed: true' and
concludes the system survived the chaos scenario. But the
scenario may not have had any assertions defined, in which case
the verdict is meaningless.

## Fix

    all_passed: !assertion_results.is_empty()
        && assertion_results.iter().all(|r| r.passed)

Empty assertion list → all_passed: false (no verdict possible).

## Acceptance

- ChaosReport::from_scenario on a scenario with zero assertions
  reports all_passed: false.
- Existing tests with non-empty scenarios still pass.

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/chaos.rs:512
- ft-38rxl (sibling: same Iterator::all([]) == true defect in
  ContinuityReport::from_checks)
close_reason: done
