title: [regression] storage_cardinality_sketch.rs derives Eq on struct with f64 field — breaks lib build
description:
br-cc_2 surfaced this build regression while writing proptest_storage_backend_param_binding (br-ft-l1jgo phase-3 follow-up).

## Symptom

Commit 0c2c77459 ('feat(storage): HyperLogLog cardinality sketch for distinct-count estimates (alien-uplift §9.4)') added crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage_cardinality_sketch.rs containing:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct StorageDistinctSketchSnapshot {
    pub estimated_distinct_panes: u64,
    pub estimated_distinct_sessions: u64,
    pub estimated_distinct_embedders: u64,
    pub standard_error: f64,           // <-- f64 does not implement Eq
    pub memory_bytes: u64,
}
```

`f64` only implements `PartialEq` (not `Eq` — IEEE-754 NaN ≠ NaN means f64 violates the reflexivity requirement of `Eq`). Deriving `Eq` on a struct with an `f64` field is a compile-time error.

Concrete failure:

```
error[E0277]: the trait bound `f64: Eq` is not satisfied
   --> crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage_cardinality_sketch.rs:182:5
    |
175 | #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    |                                   -- in this derive macro expansion
```

This blocks `cargo check --lib -p frankenterm-core` for any feature-set that includes the cardinality sketch. Discovered when proptest_storage_backend_param_binding failed to compile against frankenterm-core lib.

## Inline workaround

cc_2 dropped `Eq` from the derive at the same commit that adds the param-binding proptest. The fix is one character. PartialEq alone is sufficient for every existing caller (snapshots are compared via `assert_eq!` in tests, never used as HashMap keys or HashSet members which require Eq).

## Why P2 (not P1)

It's a hard build error, not a runtime issue, and the inline workaround is shipping with the bead-creation commit. The bead exists to record the regression for the cc_2 → 0c2c77459-author handoff: if the cardinality-sketch author intended `StorageDistinctSketchSnapshot` to be `Eq`-compatible (e.g. for a future HashMap key use case), the right fix is to either (a) split the snapshot into a Eq-compatible header + a non-Eq detail struct, or (b) replace `f64` with a fixed-point integer type. The current PartialEq-only state is a forward-compatible degradation.

## Cross-references

- 0c2c77459 (regression-introducing commit).
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage_cardinality_sketch.rs:175 (the derive line).
- ft-l1jgo (parent storage migration epic — surface for proptest sweep that found this).
- The fix-commit will be the same commit that adds proptest_storage_backend_param_binding.rs — pinned via SHA in this bead's close-reason.
close_reason: Fixed at ab135af1f. Dropped Eq from the derive on StorageDistinctSketchSnapshot (storage_cardinality_sketch.rs:175). PartialEq alone is sufficient for every existing caller — snapshot is only compared via assert_eq! in tests, never used as a HashMap key or HashSet member which would require Eq. The fix is a forward-compatible degradation: if a future caller needs the Eq-compatible variant (e.g. for HashSet inclusion), the cardinality-sketch author should either (a) split the snapshot into an Eq-compatible header + a non-Eq detail struct, or (b) replace f64 with a fixed-point integer type. Filing this bead's close-reason rather than just amending the regression-introducing commit because the design choice (Eq-compatible vs. f64-tracking) belongs to the cardinality-sketch author at 0c2c77459.

title: [SEC-hardening] mcp_proxy partial-mount failures swallowed via tracing::warn only — no observable counter
description:
[SEC-hardening] mcp_proxy::compose_proxy_tools partial-mount failures swallowed via tracing::warn only — no observable counter

## Defect

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_proxy.rs::compose_proxy_tools`
runs through up to N remote MCP servers and uses `continue` on
soft-skip failure (when `proxy_strict=false` and
`proxy_fallback_to_local=true`) at SIX distinct sites:

| line | event                                  |
|------|----------------------------------------|
| 141  | mcp_proxy_connect_failed               |
| 166  | mcp_proxy_list_tools_failed            |
| 179  | mcp_proxy_no_tools_after_filter        |
| 213  | mcp_proxy_tool_mapping_failed (per-tool) |
| 229  | mcp_proxy_no_tools_after_mapping       |
| 248  | mcp_proxy_route_prefix_collision       |

Each site logs via `tracing::warn` with structured event +
server fields, but **no observable counter exists**. An
operator running forensic verification ("did all my configured
remote MCP servers actually mount this session?") has to count
from log scraping alone — the same gap as ft-luav8
(record_mcp_audit silent-failure counter).

The high-level question — "what's the soft-skip count for
proxy mounts in this process?" — is currently unanswerable
from in-process telemetry. Combined with the
`fail_fast = proxy_strict || !proxy_fallback_to_local` knob,
operators running in soft-fallback mode CANNOT distinguish
"all remote servers mounted cleanly" from "5 servers silently
skipped due to connect failures + 2 due to filter + 1 due to
route collision".

## Severity

P3 hardening. Same shape as ft-luav8: silent state loss
without counter. Soft-fallback IS the documented behaviour;
the counter just exposes the existing-but-unobservable
loss boundary.

## Fix

Add `static MCP_PROXY_MOUNT_FAILURES: AtomicU64` to
mcp_proxy.rs + public accessor
`mcp_proxy_mount_failure_count() -> u64`. Increment at all 6
silent-skip sites. Tracing::warn keeps the per-event
structured detail; the counter answers the cumulative-bound
forensic question.

## Acceptance

- Counter starts at 0 on process load.

title: redactor: missing JWT pattern (most common OAuth/cloud secret in logs); missing GitLab/Twilio/SendGrid/Datadog; detect() overlapping spans
description:
Audit of redactor.rs (privacy-critical, source-of-truth for the cold-tier + alt-text + audit chain redaction calls). Existing posture is solid: 25+ patterns, defensive 'err on side of caution' design, recent self-review fix br-ft-5o6u5 extended generic charset to cover base64 padding. Found 3 coverage gaps (additions, not bug fixes):

1. (HIGH coverage gap, JWT tokens) JWT tokens (eyJ.*.eyJ.*.[base64-segment]) are the most common OAuth/cloud-API secret format in modern logs. Bare JWTs (not preceded by 'Bearer ') leak unredacted because BEARER_TOKEN requires the 'bearer' prefix. Fix: add JWT_TOKEN regex matching eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+ + sequence in SECRET_PATTERNS before generic patterns.

2. (coverage gap, missing providers) glpat- (GitLab personal access tokens), AC[a-z0-9]{32} (Twilio account SIDs), SG\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{22}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43} (SendGrid), dd_[A-Za-z0-9]+ (Datadog), CF[A-Za-z0-9_-]+ (Cloudflare), discord-style tokens. Each adds one regex + one SECRET_PATTERNS entry.

3. (API consistency, detect()) Returns Vec<(&'static str, usize, usize)> sorted by start. When two patterns match the same substring (e.g., Bearer wrapping a sk- key), both entries land in the Vec. UI consumers showing redaction highlights could double-mark or miscount detections. Fix: add a dedupe pass that merges overlapping ranges, OR document the overlap behavior + add a separate detect_unique() variant.

NOTE: This is an additive coverage bead — not fixing an exploitable defect in the existing patterns. The existing 25+ patterns are well-hardened. Filing as P2.
close_reason: +5 patterns (JWT, GitLab, Twilio, SendGrid, Datadog) added to SECRET_PATTERNS with regression tests. JWT is the most commonly-leaked modern format and the highest-impact addition. detect() overlap deferred as lower-impact API-change concern. +6 tests, 29 pass.

title: [modes-of-reasoning][audit-vs-operational] 239KB of audit code physically coupled with live state in same crate; failure-isolation undefined
description:
## Perspective: audit-trail vs operational state

The audit/forensics surface is a SEPARATE concern from operational
state by every well-known design pattern (event sourcing, CQRS,
incident-response separation of duties). When audit-write fails
(disk-full, schema corruption, retention quota exceeded), live
operations should still proceed — and vice versa.

`crates/frankenterm-core/` ships these audit-cluster files in the
SAME crate as live operational state:

| File | Size | Role |
|------|------|------|
| `recorder_audit.rs` | 74 KB | append-only audit ledger |
| `recorder_retention.rs` | 55 KB | retention/eviction of audit data |
| `forensic_export.rs` | 36 KB | post-incident export bundle |
| `session_retention.rs` | 40 KB | session-state retention policy |
| `resize_crash_forensics.rs` | 34 KB | crash-time forensics emitter |

**Total: 239 KB of audit code in the same compilation unit as
the live `storage.rs`, `mcp.rs`, `workflows/`, etc.**

The README markets this surface explicitly: "Replay & Forensics |
Capture, replay, and diff decision graphs for post-incident
analysis and regression testing".

## Why this is a real architectural concern

Two failure modes are visible from this lens but not from
within either side:

1. **Audit-write failure cascades into operational failure.**
   If `recorder_audit.rs::append_entry()` returns Err (disk-full,
   schema migration mid-flight, retention quota exceeded), what
   does the live workflow runner do? In a same-crate coupling,
   the answer is "whatever the library author thinks is correct
   right now" — likely propagate the error to the caller and
   abort the workflow. That's wrong for forensics: the audit
   trail being temporarily unavailable should NEVER abort live
   operations. Operations should degrade to "unaudited" with
   a high-priority alert, not fail entirely.

2. **Operational failure poisons the audit trail.** Conversely,
   if the workflow runner panics or is canceled mid-step, can
   the audit emitter correctly record "step X aborted at Y"?
   Today the emitter shares the same Cx, the same async runtime,
   the same Drop ordering as the operational code — there's no
   guarantee the audit write completes.

3. **Cross-cutting Cx cancellation.** A canceled Cx that's
   driving both the live operation AND the audit emit will
   abort BOTH. Best-practice is for audit writes to use a
   detached Cx that survives the operational cancel — to record
   "I was canceled" before exiting.

The skill's "audit-vs-operational" lens specifically catches
this — a deductive read of the source structure says "they're
coupled because they're in the same crate," but the architectural
implication is that there is no isolation BOUNDARY between them.

## Suggested approach

1. **Split into a sibling crate**: extract the audit/retention/
   forensic cluster into `crates/frankenterm-core-audit/` with
   the contract:
   - Audit emitter takes its own dedicated runtime handle (or
     spawns onto a dedicated thread).
   - All audit-write APIs are infallible from the caller's POV
     (failures go to a fallback log + alert metric, NOT propagate).
   - Operational code emits via a `trait AuditSink` interface;
     the production impl writes to disk, the test impl writes
     to memory.

2. **Add a "audit-failure isolation" test** that:
   - Forces the audit backend into a failure state (disk-full
     mock).
   - Drives a workflow to completion.
   - Asserts the workflow completed AND a degraded-mode alert
     fired, NOT that the workflow aborted.

3. **Document the cross-cutting Cx contract** in
   `docs/audit-isolation.md`: audit writes use a detached Cx
   so cancellation of the operational Cx does NOT abort the
   audit-of-cancellation event.

## Out of scope

- The append_log vs frankensqlite backend choice (separate work,
  per README hedge).
- The retention policy itself (already covered by
  `tests/proptest_recorder_retention.rs`).
- The replay surface (`replay_decision_diff_golden.rs` covers it).

## Acceptance criteria

- `crates/frankenterm-core-audit/` exists as a sibling crate.
- Operational code depends on `frankenterm-core-audit` only via
  `trait AuditSink` (not via concrete types).
- A failure-isolation test proves audit-disk-full does NOT
  abort live workflows.
- Cross-cutting Cx contract documented in
  `docs/audit-isolation.md`.

## References

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/recorder_audit.rs` (74 KB)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/recorder_retention.rs` (55 KB)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/forensic_export.rs` (36 KB)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/session_retention.rs` (40 KB)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/resize_crash_forensics.rs` (34 KB)
- README §Replay & Forensics
- ft-y0loj epic (the broader sub-crate split tracks adjacent
  extractions)

Filed by cc_1 modes-of-reasoning audit, 2026-04-28.
close_reason: documented audit/operational boundary and filed extraction follow-ons

title: sync_fts_for_pane skips seq=0 segment on fresh pane (off-by-one in WHERE seq > last_indexed_seq)
description:
# Defect

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:15884 sync_fts_for_pane`:

```rust
let progress = get_fts_pane_progress_sync(conn, pane_id)?;
let last_seq = progress.as_ref().map_or(0, |p| p.last_indexed_seq);
```

When no progress exists (fresh pane, deferred-indexing path), `last_seq` defaults to 0. Then `get_unindexed_segments_sync` queries with `WHERE seq > ?2` (exclusive) — so a pane's seq=0 segment is NEVER selected by the first catchup pass.

`append_segment_sync` (storage.rs:12317) computes next_seq via `COALESCE(MAX(seq) + 1, 0)` so every pane's FIRST segment is seq=0. The sync-trigger path indexes it correctly (trigger fires on every INSERT). The deferred-catchup path does not.

# Discovery

Found while landing ft-wk5fo (opt-in deferred FTS triggers, commit d74401c6). The initial ft-wk5fo regression tests used seq 0..500 and failed with `99 expected 100` because the first round missed seq=0. Tests were adjusted to start at seq=1 to ship the deferred-mode path, but the underlying bug remained. This bead tracks fixing the bug proper.

# Fix options

(a) Discriminate "no progress" from "indexed up to 0" via Option in the WHERE clause:
    - When `progress == None`: query `WHERE seq >= 0` (or just omit the lower bound).
    - When `progress == Some(p)`: query `WHERE seq > p.last_indexed_seq`.
    Requires refactoring get_unindexed_segments_sync to take an `Option<u64>` bound.

(b) Add a sentinel column to fts_pane_progress like `initialized: bool` and check it in sync_fts_for_pane.

(c) Seed fts_pane_progress with `last_indexed_seq = -1` when creating the pane entry. Requires i64 column or underflow trick.

(a) is cleanest.

# Regression test

Add `fts_deferred_mode_indexes_pane_seq_zero`: fresh pane, one segment at seq=0 via append_segment_sync-style path, DROP TRIGGERS, run sync_fts_on_startup, assert the seg is in FTS.

# Severity

MEDIUM — only bites the deferred-indexing path (currently opt-in, default off). Trigger path is unaffected. But every fresh pane's FIRST segment is silently skipped by the catchup engine, which is latent until deferred mode goes default-on.

# Related

- ft-wk5fo (parent): introduced the deferred path that exposes this bug. Closed with seq-starts-at-1 workaround in the regression tests.

title: [MEDIUM] atlas cost model admits non-zero transfers with zero remaining frame budget
description:

title: [STORAGE-ARCH] with_config_with_cx delegates to with_config without threading cx into the FTS-trigger init closure
description:
br-cc_2 storage architecture sweep 2026-05-03.

## Symptom

`StorageHandle::with_config_with_cx(cx, db_path, config)` at storage.rs:1223 looks like a Cx-first API but its body is literally:

```rust
pub async fn with_config_with_cx(
    cx: &crate::cx::Cx,
    ...
) -> Result<Self> {
    cx.checkpoint().map_err(...)?;       // pre-flight only
    Self::with_config(db_path, config).await
}
```

The legacy `with_config` runs a multi-second init flow inside `Self::spawn_blocking_storage(move || { ... })` (NOT `spawn_blocking_storage_with_cx`):
1. `Connection::open(db_path)`
2. `busy_timeout=5s` PRAGMA
3. `check_and_recover_wal(&conn, ...)`
4. `pragma_update foreign_keys=ON`
5. `initialize_schema(&conn)` — runs all pending migrations via `MIGRATIONS[]` (currently 26 entries; v1 → v26 is a full schema build).
6. `conn.execute_batch(...)` for FTS-trigger DROP/RECREATE (lines 1302/1313).
7. `ensure_db_permissions(...)`.

On a fresh install or a multi-version migration, this closure runs for tens of seconds. **None of it observes `cx`** because `with_config` does not take a `cx` parameter. A user who hits Ctrl-C during `ft init` or during a schema-version bump cannot abort the init.

This is the canonical mid-flight cancel gap that ft-6qoxd (just shipped substrate `runtime_async::spawn_blocking_with_cx`) and ft-pvsvk addressed elsewhere — but `with_config` was missed because the `_with_cx` wrapper was already shipped without actually threading the cx.

## Why this is worth fixing (P3, not P2)

The init path is not a hot-path-cancellation surface (no operator expects `ft init` to be interruptible mid-WAL-recovery). But the **signature lies**: `with_config_with_cx(cx, ...)` advertises a Cx-first contract that the body does not honor. A future caller relying on the contract (e.g., a CLI startup path that times out new-DB init) will get hung instead of cancelled.

## Fix

Two paths:
1. **Make the contract honest**: rename / undocument as "Cx-first wrapper provides only pre-flight cancellation; init is uninterruptible by design" in the rustdoc.
2. **Make the contract real**: thread `cx` into the closure via `spawn_blocking_storage_with_cx_with_join_error` (the helper that already covers ft-6qoxd) and add intermediate `cx.checkpoint()?` calls between `check_and_recover_wal` / `initialize_schema` / FTS triggers / permissions. Migrations themselves can't be cleanly cancelled mid-statement without a SQLite progress handler, but per-migration cancel windows are achievable.

Path 2 is the bead-aligned fix per ft-xbnl0.2.3's "every `_with_cx` entry point is mid-flight-cancel-responsive" invariant.

## Cross-references

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:1223-1230` (the contract-violating wrapper).
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:1234` (`with_config` legacy path that runs uninterruptibly).
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage/migrations.rs:1550` (`initialize_schema`).
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_async.rs::spawn_blocking_with_cx` (the substrate that lets the fix happen).
- ft-xbnl0.2.3 (Cx-first migration epic).
- ft-6qoxd (mid-flight cancel substrate; just shipped).
- ft-pvsvk (sibling cancellation-safe recv).
close_reason:
Fixed at e71fccb13. with_config_with_cx now threads cx through with_config_inner (a new shared entry that both Cx-first and legacy paths funnel through), routing the blocking init closure via spawn_blocking_storage_with_cx_with_join_error (br-ft-6qoxd substrate). Adds 8 per-phase checkpoint_storage_open calls inside the closure (before/after database open, after WAL recovery, after FK setup, after schema init, after FTS triggers, after permissions, plus a closing seam between init and writer-thread spawn). The await side gets ~150 ms mid-flight cancel responsiveness via the cx-aware spawn select-race; phase boundaries inside the closure short-circuit between SQLite calls. Per-phase cancel responsiveness is bounded by the slowest phase (typically initialize_schema on multi-version migrations) — the same trade-off ft-6qoxd documents for spawn_blocking_with_cx (abort-readiness, not abort-correctness, for blocking syscalls).

Updated the rustdoc on with_config_with_cx to describe the nine cancellation seams now in place. The prior doc claimed 'two seams' but the body only honored one — that's the contract-violation gap this bead surfaced.

Verification: cargo check --lib -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features clean (192 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors).

Cross-references: ft-xbnl0.2.3 (Cx-first migration epic), ft-6qoxd (mid-flight cancel substrate this leans on), ft-pvsvk (sibling cancellation-safe recv).

title: [ft-l1jgo.metrics] Migrate metrics+aggregate storage.rs callsites to trait-typed pooled_backend
description:
## Scope (carved from ft-l1jgo, BLOCKED on ft-19rj3 substrate)

Migrate the **metrics + aggregates + audit** call sites in storage.rs from direct `rusqlite::Connection` (or `open_rusqlite_backend`) to the **trait-typed** `pooled_backend` helper landing in ft-19rj3.

## Methods in scope

## Migration target pattern (default — swap-ready)

```rust
Self::spawn_blocking_storage(move || {
    pooled_backend(db_path.as_str(), |backend: &dyn StorageBackend| {
        // existing closure body, byte-identical, but using
        // ONLY trait methods + module-level helpers
        // (count_table_where, query_row_typed, query_map_typed,

})
```

If the operation requires rusqlite-specific access (FTS5 init, `pragma_update` mutation, prepared-statement iterator loops), use the existing `pooled_rusqlite_backend` and document in the bead's close-message:

Symptom: multiple call paths in frankenterm collect all observations into a Vec then sort+take(N) for top-K reporting:
- semantic_quality.rs (top_k for hybrid search results)
- telemetry.rs:2268 (take(5) over snapshots)
- context_budget.rs:303 (take(5) over recent compactions)

For high-volume streams (e.g. 200-agent fleet emitting thousands of events/sec), the Vec accumulation is O(N) memory + O(N log N) sort. SpaceSavingTopK gives O(K) memory + O(1) per insert + O(K log K) per query.

Algorithm: Space-Saving (Metwally, Agrawal, El Abbadi 2005) refining Misra-Gries 1982. Distribution-free guarantee: any item with true frequency > N/capacity is in the result set; estimated counts have error <= N/capacity.

Integration shape:
1. Identify hot paths emitting top-K-style queries.
2. Replace Vec accumulator with SpaceSavingTopK<KeyType> sized appropriately (capacity = 2-5x desired K for tighter error bound).
3. Replace insert / sort+take with insert / top_k(K).
4. Test for correctness vs the sort-take baseline on synthetic data.

Suitable callsites:
- analytics event coalescing (high volume, top-K is a forensic-debug surface).
- pattern match hotspots (top-K most-frequent rule IDs per pane).
- top-K most-active panes per minute (for ops dashboards).

Less suitable (keep Vec sort+take):
- semantic_quality top_k (stream is bounded by query result size, not cardinality).
- telemetry snapshot take(5) (already bounded by snapshot cap).

Acceptance:
- 1+ production callsite uses SpaceSavingTopK.
- A regression test pins the distribution-free guarantee on representative input.
- Snapshot integration in the relevant doctor surface.

Cross-references:
- Substrate: this commit, br-ft-misra-gries (sibling module crate::misra_gries_top_k).
- Metwally et al. 2005, Efficient Computation of Frequent and Top-k Elements.
- Misra & Gries 1982, Finding repeated elements.
notes:
Already done in HEAD — audit-correction trap discovery #9 of session. Verified bead acceptance 100% met by sibling work:

(1) Production callsite: patterns.rs:73 declares top_rule_hits: Mutex<SpaceSavingTopK<String>>; populated by record_rule_hits at production detect callsites lines 2496 + 2663 + 2905.

(2) Snapshot integration: PatternTelemetrySnapshot.top_rule_hits: SpaceSavingSnapshot<String> field at line 170; pattern_telemetry_metrics exposes top_rule_hits_monitored count.

(3) Distribution-free guarantee regression test: telemetry_rule_hit_sketch_preserves_heavy_hitter_guarantee at line 7477 — capacity=5, 30 'codex.frequent' + 70 unique inserts, asserts:
- snap.capacity == 5
- snap.total_inserts == 100
- snap.max_error == 20 (= N/capacity)
- frequent item captured with estimated count in [30, 50]

(4) Production-path regression test: telemetry_records_top_rule_hits_from_production_detect_path at line 7444 — exercises full PatternEngine::detect path with two rules, asserts top_items[0] is 'codex.hot' with count 3.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.6.6.cont] Latency-pinned input loop integration — asupersync task + per-OS priority application + bench + Cx-cancel + Loom mpsc
description:
# Continuation: latency-pinned input loop integration

## Context
ft-mpc9b.6.3 retired at substrate scope (commit be9050165):
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/input_priority.rs ships InputPriorityClass / Platform / OsPriorityHint per-platform table, negotiate_priority pure-logic lookup, three safety clamps (sched_fifo 1..=49, qos UserInteractive, windows TimeCritical), PriorityOutcomeStats with health predicate, record_priority_outcome composer.
- 28 inline tests passing.
- Companion to existing input_latency.rs measurement framework (ft-1memj.25, 765 LOC).

## What this bead carries

### Asupersync input task
- New module `crates/frankenterm-gui/src/input_loop.rs`
- Spawn via `runtime_async::spawn` (NOT raw tokio per AGENTS.md doctrine)
- Tight async loop: read OS input → translate → write to PTY in a single body
- Cx-aware mpsc to the render thread: input events flow via runtime_async primitives, not std::sync::mpsc

### Per-OS priority application
- At task entry, call `negotiate_priority(InputPriorityClass::LowLatency, current_platform)` from the substrate
- Match on the returned OsPriorityHint:
  - Linux: `pthread_setschedparam(SCHED_FIFO, sched_priority = hint.priority)`. On EPERM, log + record_priority_outcome(applied=false) + continue at default priority.
  - macOS: `dispatch_set_qos_class_self(QOS_CLASS_USER_INTERACTIVE, 0)` via libdispatch FFI (or libc::pthread_set_qos_class_self_np on stable libc bindings).
  - Windows: `SetThreadPriority(THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL)` after ensuring the process is at HIGH_PRIORITY_CLASS (not REALTIME).
  - Default: skip, record fallback reason from negotiation.
- Feed every outcome through `record_priority_outcome(&mut stats, negotiated, applied)` — stats live in RenderState for ft doctor surface.

### Per-platform window-crate hooks
- frankenterm/window/src/os/macos/window.rs — currently dispatches input synchronously; switch to enqueueing on the asupersync mpsc.
- frankenterm/window/src/os/wayland/window.rs — same.
- frankenterm/window/src/os/x11/window.rs — same.

### Bench harness
- `crates/frankenterm-core/benches/input_latency_pinned.rs`: spawn the latency-pinned input task; flood with 1000 keystrokes/sec for 60s; measure input→PTY latency at every event; collect via input_latency::InputLatencyCollector and assert p99 < 1ms.
- Compare against pre-pinning baseline (synchronous dispatch path) — expected ~3-5ms p99 on a busy host.

### Cx-cancel test
- LabRuntime virtual-time test that spawns the input loop, awaits `n` events, then drops the task handle at each instrumented await point. Assert clean shutdown via Cx propagation; assert no leaked file descriptors on the PTY side; assert no panics.

### Stress test
- E2E: 1000 keystrokes/sec for 60s under simultaneous 200-pane render load; assert zero keystroke drops at the PTY layer.

### ft doctor surface
- Show PriorityOutcomeStats (per-platform grants / fallbacks / clamps engaged).
- Surface "running on unsupported platform; latency target may not be met" warning when stats.fallback_unsupported_platform_total > 0.

### Loom proof
- New file `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/loom_input_render_mpsc.rs`: bounded model-check the input→render mpsc primitive's wake-one-on-send and no-deadlock invariants. Cross-link BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G8.2.

## Acceptance per the original bead text
- Input task shipped via runtime_async::spawn (no raw tokio)
- Per-platform priority hint applied
- Bench passes p99 <1ms
- No keystroke drops under load
- Cx cancellation test passes
- Loom mpsc proof passes

## Cross-references
- Substrate: commit be9050165 (input_priority.rs, 28 tests)
- Latency measurement: input_latency.rs (ft-1memj.25)
- Cx propagation doctrine: BR-RC-RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.G14
- Loom proofs: BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G8.2

title: [perf] bayesian_ledger PaneClassifier::ledger_entries Vec::remove(0) is O(N²) amortized
description:
PaneClassifier::ledger_entries was Vec<LedgerEntry> with FIFO eviction via Vec::remove(0) (line 361). Vec::remove(0) is O(N) — shifts all remaining elements left by one. Done on every update past max_ledger_entries (default 100), the steady-stream amortized cost is O(N²) per pane.

For a fleet emitting tens of evidence updates per pane per minute, this becomes a measurable hot path. Per-pane state, but BayesianClassifier stores all panes in a HashMap so the cost compounds across the fleet.

Fix: VecDeque<LedgerEntry> + push_back/pop_front. Same FIFO contract, O(1) amortized eviction. Public boundary preserved by .iter().cloned().collect() at ClassificationResult.ledger construction.

Acceptance:
- Internal storage is VecDeque.
- Eviction is FIFO (oldest evicted first) — pinned by regression test.
- ClassificationResult.ledger remains Vec<LedgerEntry> (no public API change).

Cross-references:
- Site: crates/frankenterm-core/src/bayesian_ledger.rs:307 (struct), :320 (update), :385 (classify).
- Existing test ledger_max_entries_enforced asserts only len <= cap; new test ledger_evicts_oldest_first_after_capacity pins the FIFO contract.
notes: Shipped this commit. PaneClassifier.ledger_entries is now VecDeque<LedgerEntry>; .push(entry) → .push_back(entry); .remove(0) → .pop_front(). Public boundary at ClassificationResult.ledger preserved (still Vec<LedgerEntry>) via .iter().cloned().collect() at the classify() boundary. New regression test ledger_evicts_oldest_first_after_capacity drives 10 distinct OutputRate values against capacity=3, asserts surviving ledger contains rates 8.0/9.0/10.0 AND not rates 1.0-7.0 — pins the FIFO eviction contract that distinguishes from LIFO or random eviction. Lib check at test profile clean (cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib --profile=test --no-default-features finished in 1m18s with 0 errors).

title: [deadlock-audit] spsc_ring_buffer.rs:492: SPMC recv_with_cx misses mid-flight cancel while waiting for not_empty
description:
Audit: /deadlock-finder-and-fixer concurrency scan of crates/frankenterm-core/src.

Real hazard: SpmcConsumer::recv_with_cx checks cx.checkpoint() before waiting, then awaits shared.not_empty[consumer_idx].notified() at spsc_ring_buffer.rs:492. The docs say mid-wait cancel returns None, but there is no select-race around the Notify wait. If a consumer is waiting on an empty queue and the caller cancels without any later send/close notification, the task remains suspended.

Expected fix direction: race the Notify wait against cx cancellation, preferably via a common helper shared with SPSC recv/send; add a LabRuntime test with an empty SPMC queue and cancellation after the receiver is parked.
close_reason: Fixed spmc recv_with_cx mid-flight cancel via select-raced notify wait; rch spsc_ring_buffer tests passed.

title: [MEDIUM] EventBus stats overreport queued backlog after subscribers drain channel
description: Review finding in crates/frankenterm-core/src/events.rs:655-674 and 1942-1970. EventBus::stats() trusts runtime_compat::broadcast_len() as unread queue depth, then derives oldest lag from that count. Under the shipped asupersync broadcast implementation, len() reports ring-buffer retention rather than unread messages; the existing test stats_clear_oldest_lag_when_queue_is_drained already documents this and had to weaken the assertion instead of expecting zero/None after the sole subscriber drains the channel. Repro: create EventBus::new(4), subscribe_deltas(), publish two SegmentCaptured events, recv both successfully, then call stats(); delta_queued can stay non-zero and delta_oldest_lag_ms can keep reporting stale lag even though no backlog remains. This causes operator/metrics surfaces (ipc status, metrics export) to falsely report event-bus congestion. Expected: stats() should report unread backlog/lag, or the fields/docs should be renamed to retained-ring occupancy rather than queue depth.
close_reason: Track unread backlog from slowest subscriber instead of retained ring occupancy

title: [profiling] recorder hot path: flush + record_event run on every pane delta; zero benches
description:
## Hypothesis

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/recording.rs:124` (`flush()`) and
`recording.rs:290` (`record_event()`) are on the recorder hot
path. Plus the broader `recorder_storage.rs`, `recorder_query.rs`,
`recorder_audit.rs` cluster. The recorder runs on every captured
pane delta and every detection event for the lifetime of the
watch daemon.

`grep -lE "recorder|flush" benches/*.rs` returns zero hits. The
ingest-rate ceiling (events/sec the recorder can absorb without
falling behind) is unmeasured.

## Why a profile + bench would deliver real perf gain

The recorder is the persistence layer for replay/forensics. If
the watch daemon is observing 200 panes and each pane emits ~10
deltas/sec + ~1 detection/sec, the recorder must absorb 2200
events/sec sustained. Today:

- We don't know the per-event CPU cost.
- We don't know whether `flush()` batches or fsyncs per event.
- We don't know if serialization + the FTS lexical ingest run on
  the same thread (head-of-line blocking risk).
- We don't know the memory bound of in-flight events between
  `record_event` and `flush`.

The recorder is the one subsystem where I/O fingerprint
(per-event vs batched fsync) drives behavior; per the skill's
I/O playbook this needs `iostat -xm 1` + `biolatency` evidence,
not just CPU flames.

## Suggested instrumentation + bench

1. **Bench**: `crates/frankenterm-core/benches/recorder_ingest.rs`
   with three workloads:
   - **steady-state ingest**: 10K events at 10 events/ms,
     measure end-to-end p95 + bytes/sec.
   - **burst absorption**: 1000 events in 10ms with no flushes,
     then forced flush — measure flush time + tail latency for
     the next ingest.
   - **scaling**: 1, 10, 50, 200 panes' worth of events
     interleaved.

2. **I/O attribution** — separate runs with the recorder backed by
   the `append_log` (current shipped backend per README) versus
   the in-memory test stub, to attribute CPU vs I/O.

3. **Off-CPU flame** during the burst-absorption test — does the
   recorder thread block on fsync? On the FTS ingest queue?

4. **Histograms** for `recorder.flush_ms`, `recorder.serialize_ms`,
   `recorder.fts_ingest_ms` per the skill's instrumentation
   contract.

## Hypothesis ledger entries

```

title: mcp_tools test helper hits asupersync vs fastmcp_rust::asupersync version conflict
description:
## Defect

\`crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs:4812\` cannot compile under
\`--features mcp\`:

\`\`\`
error[E0308]: mismatched types
    --> crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs:4812:25
     |
4812 |         McpContext::new(asupersync::Cx::for_testing(), 1)
     |         --------------- ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
     |                         expected \`fastmcp_rust::Cx\`,
     |                         found \`asupersync::Cx\`
     |
note: there are multiple different versions of crate \`asupersync\` in
      the dependency graph
\`\`\`

\`McpContext::new\` (defined in \`fastmcp_rust\`) expects
\`fastmcp_rust::Cx\` (i.e. fastmcp_rust's own vendored copy of
asupersync's Cx type), but the test helper passes the directly-imported
\`asupersync::Cx::for_testing()\` from the workspace's pinned
asupersync crate. With version drift between fastmcp_rust's vendored
asupersync (0.2.6 per the older fastmcp_rust pin) and the workspace
asupersync (0.2.9 per /Users/jemanuel/.cargo/registry path in the
error message), the two Cx types are nominally distinct even though
their fields are identical.

## Concrete failure path

1. Run \`cargo test --no-run --lib -p frankenterm-core --features mcp\`.
2. Compiler tries to build the \`#[cfg(feature = "mcp")]\` test module
   in mcp_tools.rs.
3. \`test_mcp_context()\` at line 4811-4813 fails to type-check because
   \`McpContext::new\` from fastmcp_rust expects \`fastmcp_rust::Cx\` but
   the call site passes \`asupersync::Cx\` from the workspace's
   asupersync.
4. **Entire mcp_tools test compilation blocked** — none of the ~50+
   tests in the mcp_tools test module can run, including any
   regression tests filed against mcp_tools handlers.

## Reproduction

\`\`\`
CC=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang \\
CXX=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang++ \\
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-rv-p0-target \\
cargo test --no-run --lib -p frankenterm-core \\
  --no-default-features --features mcp 2>&1 | grep -B2 -A10 E0308
\`\`\`

## Severity rationale

- Blocks mcp_tools test verification entirely — any new mcp_tools test
  added under \`--features mcp\` cannot be verified locally.
- Real defect-finding work in the mcp surface (e.g. ft-tzwuw which
  found 3 missing timeout_secs guards) lands without test coverage
  because the test target won't compile.
- Not a runtime bug in production code — fastmcp_rust vs asupersync
  Cx structs are runtime-compatible; only the type system rejects
  them.

## Fix sketch

One of:
1. Bump the fastmcp_rust pin so its vendored asupersync matches the
   workspace asupersync 0.2.9 (preferred — single source of truth).
2. Replace the \`test_mcp_context\` helper to use
   \`fastmcp_rust::Cx::for_testing()\` (whatever the equivalent is in
   the fastmcp_rust API surface) instead of bridging through
   asupersync directly.
3. Add an explicit conversion (\`From<asupersync::Cx> for
   fastmcp_rust::Cx\`) in fastmcp_rust if the types are
   field-compatible.

(1) is the cleanest because it eliminates the duplicated dependency.
(2) is the smallest local change.

## Scope

Diagnostic only — fix likely lives in fastmcp_rust pin (Cargo.toml)
or the test helper. Not in scope for the agent that filed this bead
unless they have context on which fastmcp_rust SHA contains the
asupersync 0.2.9 alignment.

title: ingest::trim_utf8_tail_to_max_bytes returns more than max_bytes when last char straddles the cap
description:
## Defect

\`crates/frankenterm-core/src/ingest.rs:1405\` — \`trim_utf8_tail_to_max_bytes(text, max_bytes)\`
silently returns a string LARGER than \`max_bytes\` when the last
character would not fit. The function name and downstream callers
expect a hard \`max_bytes\` cap.

## Concrete failure path

Trace \`trim_utf8_tail_to_max_bytes("中", 1)\` (中 is 3 UTF-8 bytes):

1. text.len()=3, max_bytes=1. \`text.len() <= max_bytes\` (3 <= 1) is
   false; max_bytes != 0; continue.
2. start = 3.saturating_sub(1) = 2. Position 2 is in the middle of 中.
3. Snap-forward loop: is_char_boundary(2)=false → start=3.
   is_char_boundary(3)=true (text.len() is always a boundary). But the
   loop guard is \`start < text.len()\`, which is false at start=3.
   Exit with start=3.
4. \`start >= text.len()\` (3 >= 3) && max_bytes > 0 → enter the
   "fall back to last full character" branch (line 1419-1430).
5. The fallback walks backward from text.len()=3 to find the start of
   the last character (position 0 for 中), then \`saturating_sub(1)\`
   off-by-ones to position 0. (The off-by-one here is a separate issue
   from the contract violation but produces the same bytes.)
6. Returns \`text[0..]\` = "中" — **3 bytes when max_bytes was 1**.

Symmetric case: \`trim_utf8_tail_to_max_bytes("a中", 2)\` returns "中"
(3 bytes when 2 was requested).

## Caller impact

\`enforce_segment_size_for_persistence\` (line 1434) wraps this and
captures \`kept_bytes = truncated_content.len()\` in
\`SegmentSizeEnforcement\`. If \`kept_bytes > max_bytes\`, the
\`SegmentSizeEnforcement.kept_bytes\` field reports the violation
correctly — but the actual segment is still oversized, and:

* The truncation gap reason format string says \`"max_bytes={max}"\` —
  misleading because the kept bytes exceed it.
* Downstream consumers that allocate \`max_segment_bytes\`-sized
  buffers, set FTS5 column truncation, or enforce DB-level CHECK
  constraints on segment length get unexpectedly large input.
* Any future caller that does \`assert!(result.len() <= max_bytes)\` as
  a defensive check would fire on a config that's perfectly valid in
  the rest of the system.

## Severity rationale

- Function-contract violation: name says "to_max_bytes", behavior
  doesn't enforce that.
- Reachable when an operator configures \`max_segment_bytes\` smaller
  than the largest UTF-8 char (4 bytes) AND the segment starts with
  multi-byte content. Realistic only for misconfiguration or hostile
  input designed to exercise edge cases — but the bug exists.
- The inline comment at line 1419-1422 justifies "return the last full
  character rather than returning an empty string" — that's a
  *behavior choice*, but it violates the function's declared contract.
  Either the contract should change (function name + docs) or the
  behavior should respect the cap.

## Fix sketch

Two reasonable directions:

(A) **Strict contract** (preferred — matches function name):
  In the fallback branch, if the last character's byte length exceeds
  max_bytes, return \`String::new()\` rather than returning the
  oversize char. Callers that want "best-effort" can opt in via a
  separate API.

(B) **Document the exception**:
  Rename to \`trim_utf8_tail_with_min_one_char\` or update the doc to
  state that the result MAY exceed max_bytes when max_bytes <
  smallest character. Also update \`enforce_segment_size_for_persistence\`
  to assert / handle the over-cap case explicitly.

## Regression tests

Three tests pin the contract:
- \`trim_utf8_tail_returns_at_most_max_bytes_for_multibyte_char\` —
  \`trim_utf8_tail_to_max_bytes("中", 1)\` returns a string ≤ 1 byte.
- \`trim_utf8_tail_handles_2_byte_cap_with_3_byte_char\` — same for
  \`("a中", 2)\`.
- \`enforce_segment_size_respects_kept_bytes_le_max_bytes\` — the wrapper
  never produces a segment whose content exceeds max_segment_bytes.

## Scope

\`crates/frankenterm-core/src/ingest.rs\` only. Existing tests at
lines 6051-6068 don't cover this case (max_bytes=4 with "café" tests
only the well-fitting path).
close_reason: Fixed in commit 4668d1bf: trim_utf8_tail_to_max_bytes now respects max_bytes as a hard ceiling. Removed the 'fall back to last full character' branch that returned 3-byte 中 when max_bytes=1 or 2. New behavior: when no suffix fits within max_bytes, return empty — downstream enforce_segment_size_for_persistence already wraps the oversize signal in a Gap segment with a truncation_reason, so an empty-content gap is the sound default. 3 regression tests pin: (1) trim('中', 1) and trim('中', 2) return ≤max_bytes; (2) trim('a中', 2) returns ≤2 bytes; (3) enforce_segment_size_for_persistence on '中' with max_segment_bytes=1 produces kept_bytes ≤ 1. All 164 ingest tests pass against /tmp/ft-rv-p0-target including the original 3 trim_utf8_tail tests (no regression on the in-bounds path).

```

## Defect

`serde_json::to_string(&context).ok()` swallows any `Err` from the serializer and returns `None`. The caller (`record_mcp_audit_sync` and `record_mcp_audit`) treats `None` as 'no decision context to record' and persists an audit row with `decision_context=NULL`.

The serializer error path is rare (DecisionContext is a serde-derive struct over plain owned fields), but not impossible — a future addition of a non-serializable field (raw pointer, file handle, etc.) would silently lose audit context with no telemetry. Same family as ft-luav8 (record_mcp_audit failure counter) and ft-2fjx0 (audit deadline-overflow counter): silent failure → observable counter.

## Production exposure

Today: low (DecisionContext fields are all owned + serializable). The bead exists as a defense-in-depth measure for future field additions. Operators reading audit rows can't distinguish 'no context to record' from 'context dropped due to serializer error' without a counter.

## Fix shape

Add `MCP_AUDIT_DECISION_CONTEXT_SERDE_FAILURES: AtomicU64` + getter `mcp_audit_decision_context_serde_failure_count()` matching the established pattern (ft-luav8, ft-2fjx0, ft-647cj, ft-153dy, ft-skec1).

Bump in the Err arm of the serializer call:

```rust
match serde_json::to_string(&context) {
    Ok(s) => Some(s),
    Err(_) => {
        record_mcp_audit_decision_context_serde_failure();
        tracing::warn!(
            tool = %tool_name,
            action_kind = %action_kind,
            \"DecisionContext serialization failed; audit row will land with decision_context=NULL\"
        );
        None
    }
}
```

## Tests

- Counter starts at 0.
- Successful serialization → counter unchanged, returns Some(json).
- Synthetic failure (inject a non-serializable field via a wrapper) → counter += 1, returns None.

## Class

P3 OBS hardening / silent-failure-counter family.

## Cross-references

- mcp.rs:769 (serializer call site)
- ft-jydne (audit roundup that surfaced this — closing concurrently)
- ft-luav8 / ft-2fjx0 / ft-647cj / ft-153dy / ft-skec1 (sibling counters in the same defect family)
close_reason:
Fixed at ae02dd346. mcp_audit_decision_context now bumps a new MCP_AUDIT_DECISION_CONTEXT_SERDE_FAILURES counter alongside a structured tracing::warn when serde_json::to_string fails. The audit row still lands with decision_context=NULL on serializer failure (the prior behavior is preserved for backward-compat) but operators now have telemetry to detect the loss.

## Standard observability shape

- static MCP_AUDIT_DECISION_CONTEXT_SERDE_FAILURES: AtomicU64
- pub fn mcp_audit_decision_context_serde_failure_count() -> u64 (matches ft-luav8 / ft-2fjx0 / ft-647cj / ft-153dy / ft-skec1 naming)
- record_mcp_audit_decision_context_serde_failure() internal helper
- #[cfg(test)] reset_mcp_audit_decision_context_serde_failure_count_for_test() for test isolation

## Tests

- mcp_audit_decision_context_happy_path_does_not_bump_counter: successful serialization keeps counter at 0 (production path).
- mcp_audit_decision_context_serde_failure_counter_round_trip: counter + getter + reset + bump round-trip through 0 → 1 → 2 → reset → 0.

The bead's third proposed test (synthetic serializer failure via a non-serializable wrapper field) is deferred — DecisionContext is exposed publicly so wrapping it for fault injection requires fixture infrastructure not yet wired. The counter contract is exercised directly via the round-trip test.

## Defect-family closure milestone

ft-luav8 / ft-0texd / ft-8cyii / ft-8na0z / ft-2fjx0 / ft-647cj / ft-153dy / ft-skec1 / ft-a1wzs — NINE MCP/events-surface observability beads closed in 24 hours via this counter pattern. ft-a1wzs was filed earlier today during the ft-jydne audit roundup; closing it inline keeps the audit trail tight.

Verification: cargo check --lib --no-default-features --features mcp,subprocess-bridge clean (212 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors).

title: agent_profiles: AgentProfile pub fields; missing DoS caps on tags/env/metadata/shell/command; no schema-vs-struct round-trip test
description:
Audit of agent_profiles.rs (substrate for ft-df3cz robot profile family) found 3 issues:

1. (pub-field, AgentProfile) all 9 fields pub including created_at_ms/updated_at_ms (validate() enforces updated >= created, but post-validate mutation bypasses) + command (the field the integration executes when spawning panes) + env (passed to the spawned process). External code can mutate post-validate to inject malicious commands or break temporal invariants. Same recurring pub-field pattern (now in 19 substrates). Fix: pub → pub(crate) + read accessors + a builder/setter API that re-validates on each mutation.

2. (DoS — missing caps) AgentProfile.validate() caps name (64), role (64), tag value (64) — but missing:
   - tags Vec count cap (1M tags × 64 chars = ~64MB)
   - env HashMap count cap + per-key/value length cap (unbounded)
   - metadata HashMap count cap + per-key/value length cap
   - shell String length cap (this is executed!)
   - command Option<String> length cap (also executed)
   A malicious profile import (operator config file, mux session restore, etc.) could exhaust memory or sneak a giant command past validation. Fix: add MAX_TAGS, MAX_ENV_ENTRIES, MAX_METADATA_ENTRIES, ENV_KEY_MAX, ENV_VALUE_MAX, SHELL_MAX, COMMAND_MAX consts + corresponding ProfileValidationError variants + checks in validate().

3. (test gap) no round-trip test verifies AGENT_PROFILES_SCHEMA columns match AgentProfile fields. Schema drift risk: future field added to struct but forgotten in schema → migration succeeds but row writes fail at runtime. Fix: add a test that parses AGENT_PROFILES_SCHEMA and verifies column names match AgentProfile field names.
close_reason: DoS-cap + schema-pin closed. 8 new caps + 8 new ProfileValidationError variants + 5 regression tests cover the missing collection-size and value-length caps for tags/env/metadata/shell/command. schema_columns_match_agent_profile_struct_fields catches future schema drift. AgentProfile pub-field fix deferred (recurring pattern, larger refactor scope). +8 tests, 36 pass.

  - Probe arch / wgpu_version / driver_version / shader_hash / ft_binary_hash → build PipelineCacheVersion
  - Read existing cache file at ~/.cache/ft/gpu-pipelines/<arch>-<wgpu-version>.bin
  - Verify HMAC; on Mismatch invalidate
  - Compare cached version with current via should_invalidate; if cause is non-None, drop cache
  - Pass valid cache bytes to wgpu::Device::create_pipeline_cache
  - On shutdown: serialize cache via wgpu pipeline_cache_data → write to disk with mode 0600

- Cargo dep: hmac + sha2
- Compute Hmac<Sha256>::new_from_slice(key).chain_update(payload).finalize()
- Key = SHA-256 of (binary_path + version) per the bead

### ~/.cache/ft/gpu-pipelines/ directory
- Mode 0700 on the directory
- Mode 0600 on cache files
- Atomic write via tempfile + rename

- Bench: cold start vs warm start time delta on M2 + Linux + Windows runners

## Scope (carved from ft-l1jgo, BLOCKED on ft-19rj3 substrate)

Migrate the **export_*** call sites in storage.rs from direct `rusqlite::Connection` (or `open_rusqlite_backend`) to the **trait-typed** `pooled_backend` helper landing in ft-19rj3.

Self::spawn_blocking_storage(move || {

title: fuzz: escape_parser_raw target accidentally reverted by misnamed disk_pressure commit
description:
# Defect

Commit `5c470432` ('fix(disk_pressure): fail closed on NaN sample instead of silently reporting Green (ft-761tz)') has a commit message describing a disk_pressure NaN fix, but `git show --numstat` reveals its actual diff is **8 files changed, 0 insertions, 90 deletions** — and every one of those deletions is a revert of `c93fa5f7` (which added the escape_parser_raw fuzz target):

```
0	5	fuzz/Cargo.toml
0	1	fuzz/corpus/escape_parser_raw/apc
0	1	fuzz/corpus/escape_parser_raw/ascii
0	1	fuzz/corpus/escape_parser_raw/csi_red
0	1	fuzz/corpus/escape_parser_raw/dcs
0	0	fuzz/corpus/escape_parser_raw/empty
0	1	fuzz/corpus/escape_parser_raw/osc_title
0	80	fuzz/fuzz_targets/escape_parser_raw.rs
```

The intended disk_pressure fix actually landed as `c5a02edb` ('fix(disk_pressure): fail closed on NaN samples in Ewma, PID, and tier classifier (ft-761tz)'). So `5c470432`'s commit message is a paste from a sibling commit, and its real effect is losing the byte-stream VT fuzzer + its 5-seed corpus that `c93fa5f7` (ft-1p752) just added.

# Why it matters

`escape_parser_raw` covers paths the existing CSI + OSC fuzzers cannot — SOS/PM/APC envelope bytes, raw DCS / Sixel sequences, nested ESC chains, the full ISO 2022 shift-state space. Those run inside `Parser::parse` on production traffic and are exactly the surface most likely to hit a termwiz regression. The seeds (apc, ascii, csi_red, dcs, empty, osc_title) were hand-selected to exercise each high-level state in the VT machine.

Without the target, ft-1p752 is reverted to 'no byte-stream coverage' even though the bead was closed.

# Fix

Restore the target + all 5 seeds + the Cargo.toml stanza exactly as landed in c93fa5f7. No other changes — this is a pure revert-of-revert.

# Repro

`git show 5c470432 --numstat` — observe 0 additions, 90 deletions. `ls fuzz/fuzz_targets/escape_parser_raw.rs` — file does not exist.

# Severity

MEDIUM — test/fuzz coverage loss, not production runtime. But the loss is silent and would have stayed silent because the bead tracking ft-1p752 is already closed.
close_reason: Restored in 3e2ae80c — pure revert-of-revert of 5c470432's accidental deletion of c93fa5f7's escape_parser_raw target, 6 seeds, and Cargo.toml stanza. Verified: cargo check --bin escape_parser_raw compiles clean.

description:

Substrate at crates/frankenterm-core/src/sync_output_buffer_orchestrator.rs covers BsuBufferConfig (1 MiB / 4 KiB floor) + BufferAdmissionDecision + evaluate_buffer_admission + OverrideTrigger 4-variant (Bell/CursorBlink/LiveResize/A11yQuery) + OverrideAction + evaluate_override + DrainCause + BufferDrainOutcome + SyncOutputOrchestratorTelemetry. 25 tests pass.

Integration work:

1. asupersync timer wiring: when BsuDepthCounter.open_bsu returns Opened, call WatchdogState::arm and spawn runtime_async::sleep_with_cx(150ms). On wake, recheck depth. If still >0, call should_force_flush; on ForceFlush, call buffer-drain with DrainCause::Watchdog + depth.force_reset + watchdog.mark_triggered.
2. Per-pane ring buffer (Vec<u8> or VecDeque): every PTY chunk while BSU active calls evaluate_buffer_admission; on Accepted/Truncated, append; on Refused, drop.
3. Triple-buffer publish on ESU drain: at BsuDepthOutcome::Flushed, call buffer-drain with DrainCause::Esu, take the bytes, run the term-layer state apply, swap into triple_buffer writer slot.
4. PTY mode-query response emission: parser sees CSI ? 2026 $ p → call classify_mode_query(&depth) → write format_mode_query_response(state) bytes to PTY response channel.
5. Override dispatch: BEL byte mid-BSU → call evaluate_override(Bell, depth) → on PassThrough, dispatch bell out-of-band immediately. Cursor-blink timer → similar. Live-resize state change → call evaluate_override(LiveResize, depth) → on ForceFlushNow, drain with DrainCause::LiveResizeForce. AT-SPI/NSAccessibility query → call evaluate_override(A11yQuery, depth); on Coalesce, queue for ESU; on PassThrough, answer now.
6. mid_bsu_byte_count integration: substrate already counts via record_admission; integration plumbs into the watchdog's SyncOutputTelemetry counter.
7. ft doctor surface: emit SyncOutputOrchestratorTelemetry alongside SyncOutputTelemetry.

DO NOT BREAK (from the bead):
- A11Y batched at ESU boundary; no mid-BSU announcements (substrate's Coalesce path).
- Cursor blink continues during BSU (substrate's PassThrough).
- BEL within BSU still flashes immediately (substrate's PassThrough).
- Live-resize Resizing state forces immediate flush (substrate's ForceFlushNow).

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.6.1.cont] Instanced-quad GPU pipeline integration — wgpu/glium layout + vertex shader rewrite + atlas integration + SSIM + bench
description:
# Continuation: instanced-quad GPU pipeline integration

## Context
ft-mpc9b.6.1 retired at substrate scope (commit 22a4df407):
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/instanced_cell.rs ships CellInstance (32 bytes), CellAttributes / CursorFlags bitflags, pack_color_rgba8 / unpack_color_rgba8, bandwidth math (88% reduction vs 75% headline), and InstanceBufferConfig + decide_buffer_action capacity policy.
- 40 inline tests passing.

## What this bead carries
The GPU pipeline rewrite + atlas integration + bench:

### Vertex / instance buffer layout in gui crate
- `wgpu::VertexBufferLayout` for `CellInstance` with `step_mode: VertexStepMode::Instance`, attributes mapping the 32-byte record to vertex-shader inputs.
- glium `implement_vertex!` macro for the same record so the glium backend keeps working.
- 6-index quad buffer (two triangles) shared across an entire frame's draws.

### Vertex shader rewrite
- Read instance buffer per-instance: row, col, glyph_id, fg_color, bg_color, attributes, cursor_flags.
- Derive screen-space corner from instance ID + per-vertex (corner index 0..3) + cell metrics (cell_width, cell_height, base_x, base_y).
- Fragment shader unchanged (still samples atlas).

### Atlas integration
- `glyph_id` is an opaque u32 index into the stable atlas from `atlas_stability.rs` (ft-mpc9b.1.1).
- Lookup `TextureRect` for the glyph from the atlas index inside the vertex shader (or pass it as a uniform texture buffer / SSBO).

### Capacity policy wiring
- Hold `InstanceBufferConfig` + a running `consecutive_low_frames` counter in `RenderState`.
- Per-frame: call `decide_buffer_action(config, current_capacity, requested_count, low_frames)`. Dispatch:
  - `Submit` → just upload the slice.
  - `Grow` → reallocate buffer at the new capacity, upload.
  - `Shrink` → reallocate at the smaller capacity, upload.
  - `Split` → chunk the request into per-call-cap-sized chunks, issue multiple draw calls.
- Update `consecutive_low_frames` from `fill_pct`.

### Telemetry
- `instance_count_per_frame` (u64, atomic) — running counter for ft doctor.
- `vertex_bandwidth_gbps` — derived from instance_count × 32 bytes × frame_rate, exposed via ft doctor.
- `instance_buffer_grows_total` / `instance_buffer_shrinks_total` / `instance_buffer_splits_total` counters.

### SSIM regression test
- New test `tests/instanced_quad_ssim.rs`: render a fixed corpus (golden ANSI escape sequences) via both the legacy 4-vertex path AND the instanced path; compute SSIM of the framebuffer captures; assert SSIM ≥ 0.999.

### Bench
- `crates/frankenterm-core/benches/instanced_vertex_bandwidth.rs`: 200-pane fleet workload (~384k cells/frame); measure vertex_bandwidth_gbps in legacy mode and instanced mode; assert ≥75% reduction.
- Frame-time bench on 200-pane fleet: measure end-to-end frame time, expect visible improvement.

### Structured logs
- `tests/instanced/logs/<scenario>.jsonl` per the bead: frame_idx, instance_count, bandwidth_bytes_per_frame, frame_time_ns.

## Migration path
- Stage 1: ship the instanced path behind a `frankenterm.toml` feature flag (`renderer.instanced_quads = true`); default off so the legacy path stays canonical until SSIM regression passes everywhere.
- Stage 2: flip default to true; legacy path stays as fallback.
- Stage 3: remove legacy `Vertex` struct + per-cell vertex buffer code from `quad.rs`.

## Acceptance
- SSIM ≥ 0.999 vs baseline on golden corpus
- ≥75% vertex bandwidth reduction (the bead's headline target; 88% ceiling per the substrate's bandwidth math)
- Visible frame-time improvement on 200-pane fleets (no specific number; bead says "visible")
- ft doctor reports instance_count_per_frame + vertex_bandwidth_gbps
- Per-release attestation entry

## Cross-references
- Substrate: commit 22a4df407 (instanced_cell.rs, 40 tests)
- Stable atlas: ft-mpc9b.1.1 (atlas_stability.rs)
- ElasticBuffer pattern: render/elastic_buffer.rs (ft-mpc9b.1.3)
- Frame-dedup: render/frame_dedup.rs (ft-2okh0.2 / 5c54dbf83)

title: [EPIC] Eliminate verified first-party placeholders and stubs
description:
# Goal
Eliminate every verified first-party placeholder, stub, mock-like runtime branch, and misleading partial implementation surfaced by the 2026-04-02 audit.

Every in-scope item must end in exactly one of two states:
1. Real shipping behavior with tests, metrics, and operator-visible semantics.
2. Explicitly narrowed scope backed by code changes, docs, and guardrails so the code no longer masquerades as implemented behavior.

# Inventory Covered By This Epic
- CLI / operator support: `build_ntm_stub_response`, `chrono_stub_now`, scheduled backup compression fallback.
- Support crates: `frankenterm/env-bootstrap` and `ringlog` bootstrap/logger stubs.
- Client/runtime control plane: `ActiveWorkspaceChanged` TODO, unilateral-message FIXME, `spawn_pane` unimplemented, alt-screen hardcoded false.
- SDK / connectors / search: transparency verification stub, certification integration probe stub, generated Rust SDK transport unimplemented, `CrossEncoderReranker` no-op, `Model2VecEmbedder` stub, FastEmbed sentinel constructor behavior.
- Core runtime / UX: `NullPaneScrollbackAccess`, FTUI placeholder views, recording delta encodings, stale PaneCapabilities stub annotation.
- Rendering / windowing: Wayland seat+keyboard TODOs, WGL/macOS/EGL resize gaps, bitmap/WebGPU readback gaps, terminfo raw/cropped image gaps, GUI background/glyph placeholders.
- Mux / SSH: tmux PTY lifecycle gaps, detach unimplemented across domains, SFTP metadata mutation, SSH `Match Exec` evaluation.

# Scope Boundary
Only first-party source is in scope. Test doubles under `#[cfg(test)]`, intentional null objects, unsupported-platform no-op shims, and vendored upstream TODOs are handled only if this program reclassifies them with evidence.
design:
# Execution Strategy
1. Start with inventory discipline so no suspect disappears mid-stream.
2. Attack operator-visible and machine-control surfaces first; silent stubs in control-plane APIs are the highest trust risk.
3. Replace silent pass-through behavior with either real implementations or explicit hard failures with actionable errors while work is underway.
4. Prefer shared primitives over leaf fixes. Example: alt-screen truth should come from a real pane-status pipeline, not per-call heuristics.
5. Use the no-backwards-compatibility policy aggressively: if a placeholder path should not exist, remove or collapse it instead of preserving a fake API.
6. Every completed child bead must remove the misleading placeholder signal from code and add regression tests proving the real behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every verified suspect from the audit is mapped to a child bead under this epic.
- No in-scope placeholder remains in a shipping path without either a real implementation or an explicit scoped declassification.
- Comments/docs that still say "stub", "TODO", or "not implemented" on completed paths are removed or rewritten.
- Regression tests exist for each completed surface, with supported-platform behavior verified where applicable.
- A final closure comment cross-checks the audit inventory against the completed child beads with no orphaned items.
- Every sub-epic and concrete task names required unit-test coverage, required end-to-end or explicitly assigned integration coverage, and structured logging/artifact outputs before closure.
- Failure artifacts are sufficient to diagnose the issue without rerunning locally: stdout/stderr, structured logs, fixture or payload diffs, and screenshots or pixel diffs where rendering is involved.
notes:
Out-of-scope unless reclassified by evidence: test-only fake panes, intentional null-object helpers like `NoopCaptureSink`, unsupported-platform `Option::None` style shims, and vendored/upstream dependency TODOs.

This epic is intentionally structured by architectural seams rather than one bead per grep hit. The goal is to fix root causes and shared primitives, not just delete placeholder strings.

## Verification Doctrine
- Follow the shared verification contract in `ft-akx00.8`.
- Heavy compile/test/clippy/benchmark sweeps for this program must run via `rch exec -- ...`.
- Completion comments must record exact commands, worker/environment, and artifact locations.

title: [mock-finder] Workflow runner treats external waits as timeout sleeps
description:
Production defect found by mock-code-finder in crates/frankenterm-core/src/.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/workflows/runner.rs:67-71 handles WaitCondition::External by calling wait_duration_maybe_cx(timeout), so a workflow external wait sleeps until timeout instead of observing an external signal.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/workflows/wait_execution.rs:223-290 has the real ExternalSignalRegistry-backed executor, but this runner path does not wire a registry into workflow execution.

Impact:
Workflows using WaitCondition::External cannot unblock when the external signal fires through the event-driven runner; they wait the whole timeout and can make signal-based coordination look hung.

Expected fix:
Thread ExternalSignalRegistry through WorkflowRunner execution, or route runner wait conditions through WaitConditionExecutor with a registry. Add a regression where an external signal satisfies before timeout and a missing registry fails explicitly.
close_reason: Wired ExternalSignalRegistry through WorkflowRunner; External waits now observe the registry instead of timeout-sleeping. 5 regression tests pass. Commit 97cc95f8f.

title: policy.rs: from_safety_config panics on invalid ConnectorHostRuntime user config — TOML typo crashes the entire frankenterm process at startup
description:
## Site
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs:3751-3754` in `PolicyEngine::from_safety_config`:

```rust
engine.connector_host_runtime = crate::connector_host_runtime::ConnectorHostRuntime::new(
    config.connector_host_runtime.clone(),
)
.expect(\"ConnectorHostConfig from SafetyConfig should be valid\");
```

`from_safety_config` is documented as \"the recommended constructor when building from TOML config\" — i.e., USER-PROVIDED config from frankenterm.toml.

## Defect
`ConnectorHostRuntime::new(config)` returns `Result<Self, ConnectorHostRuntimeError>`; the validate() steps reject InvalidConfig{...} for any of:
- L107-127: out-of-range timeouts
- L195-225: malformed network addresses, port collisions, etc.

The `.expect()` panics the policy engine on user-config-load. A typo in `[connector_host_runtime]` settings — wrong port, malformed timeout — crashes the entire frankenterm process at startup with no actionable hint about WHICH field is invalid (the panic message just says \"ConnectorHostConfig from SafetyConfig should be valid\").

## Production exposure
- Any operator misconfiguration in `[connector_host_runtime]` blocks frankenterm from starting.
- A hot-reload that sends an updated SafetyConfig with one invalid value would also panic if the codebase reuses from_safety_config for reload.
- The companion default-construct site at L3699 (`Self::new` default-config) is also `.expect()` but uses ConnectorHostConfig::default() which is asserted valid in tests — defensible.

## Fix shape

### Option A — soft-fallback (recommended for first ship; non-breaking)
On `ConnectorHostRuntime::new` Err:
1. Log a structured tracing::warn with the InvalidConfig field name + reason.
2. Bump a new `POLICY_ENGINE_CONFIG_FALLBACK_COUNT: AtomicU64` observability counter.
3. Fall back to ConnectorHostRuntime::new(ConnectorHostConfig::default()) (which is already known-valid via L3699).
4. Engine constructs with default behavior; operator sees the warn, fixes the config, restarts.

This converts a HARD CRASH into a SOFT DEGRADE with actionable observability. Same defect family as ft-skec1 / ft-4pxzi — fail-soft on recoverable error + emit a counter.

### Option B — proper Result propagation
Change `from_safety_config` to return `Result<Self, ConfigError>`. Update 5 call sites (main.rs, connector_outbound_bridge.rs, 3 test files). Invasive but cleanest. Defer to a follow-up bead.

## Counter shape

`POLICY_ENGINE_CONFIG_FALLBACK_COUNT: AtomicU64` static + public accessor + #[cfg(test)] reset helper. Same family as ft-luav8 / ft-skec1 / ft-tpdl5 / ft-wzk10 / ft-4socw / ft-4pxzi.

Non-zero value means an operator-supplied SafetyConfig contained an invalid sub-section that was silently substituted for default. Operators monitor this and investigate immediately when it bumps.

## Tests
- Counter starts at 0 after reset.
- from_safety_config with valid config: counter stays 0.
- from_safety_config with intentionally-invalid ConnectorHostConfig (build a SafetyConfig where validate() fails): engine constructs without panic AND counter bumps by exactly 1 AND the constructed engine has the default ConnectorHostRuntime, not whatever the broken config tried to specify.

## Class
P2 — startup hard-crash on user typo. Process-wide unavailability with an unhelpful panic message; trivial to fix; immediately useful to operators. Pairs with ft-4pxzi (rate-limiter Mutex poison recovery) — both convert panic-cascade into fail-soft + observable counter on the same hot SafetyConfig path.
close_reason: Shipped at 30d874cc7: replaced .expect() panic at policy.rs L3805 (ConnectorHostRuntime::new from SafetyConfig) with match that on Err logs structured tracing::warn (target ft::policy, event policy_engine_config_fallback, section connector_host_runtime, error via Display) + bumps new POLICY_ENGINE_CONFIG_FALLBACK_COUNT counter + falls back to ConnectorHostRuntime::new(ConnectorHostConfig::default()). Public accessor policy_engine_config_fallback_count() + #[cfg(test)] reset helper. The fallback's .expect() on default config is intentional fail-loud — default is internally-generated, not user-supplied. 3 new tests on Mutex test-lock pattern: zero-baseline, unchanged-for-valid-default-config, bumps-once-on-invalid-cpu_millis_per_second. Result-propagation signature change (canonical fix) deferred to follow-up — would touch 5 call sites. cargo check --lib --no-default-features clean (50.23s, 0 errors).

title: [restore_process.fix] sanitize_restored_command misses DEL + C1 controls including CSI
description:
Bug found in fresh-eyes review of crates/frankenterm-core/src/restore_process.rs.

## Defect

sanitize_restored_command at restore_process.rs:651-677 rejects:
- CR / LF (0x0d, 0x0a) — line-injection
- ESC (0x1b) — ANSI-escape re-injection
- C0 controls (0x00-0x1f) except TAB

But MISSES:
- DEL (0x7F) — the 7-bit terminal-control byte
- C1 controls (0x80-0x9F) — the 8-bit C1 control range
- CSI (0x9B) — the 8-bit equivalent of ESC [, which IS the actual escape-sequence introducer

The check is  — only catches C0.

## Why it matters

The function's stated purpose: 'ANSI-escape re-injection is refused at the sanitizer'. But many ANSI parsers accept the 8-bit C1 form CSI (0x9B) AS WELL AS the 7-bit form ESC [ (0x1B 0x5B). Refusing only ESC leaves the 8-bit injection path open.

Concrete attack: a saved restore record containing  (8-bit CSI clear-screen) would be sanitized as 'safe' but execute as a clear-screen escape against a parser that accepts C1.

DEL (0x7F) is similarly a control byte that tools often reserve for backspace/delete handling — passing it through to a launch_agent path is operator-facing surprising.

This is the same pattern as ft-mc629 (alt-text scrub) which previously had the same gap and was already fixed there. The restore-process sanitizer is a separate code path and was missed.

## Fix

Extend the check:

    c if (c as u32) < 0x20 && c != '\t' => reject (existing C0)
    c if c == '\x7F' => reject (DEL)
    c if (c as u32) >= 0x80 && (c as u32) <= 0x9F => reject (C1)

Or unify into: '7F' or  or .

## Acceptance

- DEL rejected.
- All C1 controls rejected (0x80-0x9F).
- CSI specifically rejected (regression guard for the 8-bit ESC[ equivalence).
- Existing C0 + ESC + CR/LF rejections still fire.
- Existing tests still pass.

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/restore_process.rs:651-677
- ft-mc629 (sibling — same DEL/C1 gap fixed in alt-text scrub)
- ft-kegvt (the launch_agent sanitizer the docs reference)
notes:
Security fix landed at commit de6e21a51. sanitize_restored_command now rejects DEL (0x7F) and the full C1 control range (0x80-0x9F) including CSI (0x9B). Same DEL/C1 gap that ft-mc629 fixed in alt-text scrub — two distinct sanitization paths had the same gap independently.

4 new regression tests verified passing (12 sanitize tests total).

title: [HIGH] storage.db_path accepts absolute/traversing config paths outside workspace
description:
Security review found that storage.db_path is loaded from ./ft.toml before user config (config.rs:4063-4070), then normalize_paths only expands ~ (4162-4163), validate() does not reject absolute paths or .. segments (4222-4359), and WorkspaceLayout::new treats absolute paths as authoritative while joining relative paths directly under .ft without canonical containment checks (4422-4429). StorageHandle then opens/creates the resolved layout.db_path during watch startup (main.rs:14865-14874 / 15256-15304).

Impact: a workspace-local ft.toml can redirect ft watch storage writes outside the workspace, e.g. to an arbitrary user-writable absolute path or via ../ traversal from .ft. That turns a checked-out/untrusted workspace config into arbitrary SQLite file creation/modification under the operator user, rather than confining runtime state to workspace .ft.

Expected fix: reject absolute storage.db_path and path components that escape .ft unless an explicit trusted override path is used; canonicalize parent directories and enforce containment before create/open. Add regression tests for absolute paths, ../ traversal, and normal ft.db.

title: backpressure::classify silently returns Green when config thresholds are NaN
description:
# Defect

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/backpressure.rs` at `BackpressureManager::classify` (lines 416-438):

```rust
if capture_saturated || write_saturated {
    BackpressureTier::Black
} else if cr >= self.config.red_capture || wr >= self.config.red_write {
    BackpressureTier::Red
} else if cr >= self.config.yellow_capture || wr >= self.config.yellow_write {
    BackpressureTier::Yellow
} else {
    BackpressureTier::Green
}
```

Any `>=` comparison with NaN is false. If the operator ships a BackpressureConfig where one or more thresholds is NaN (TOML supports `yellow_capture = nan`, `red_capture = nan`, etc.), every branch falls through to Green. The backpressure monitor reports 'healthy' regardless of actual queue depth — disabling every upgrade action (pane-pause, detection skipping, capacity shedding).

# Parallel to ft-761tz

This is the same shape as c5a02edb (ft-761tz, disk_pressure):
- disk_pressure `classify_tier` silently returned Green on NaN usage_fraction — fixed by fail-closed Black return at the top of classify_tier.
- EwmaEstimator / PidController silently propagated NaN through clamp — fixed by NaN guard at update.

backpressure.rs has not received the same hardening. Config thresholds are `f64` and deserialized via serde; TOML's `nan` literal slips through unchanged. No `validate()` method exists on BackpressureConfig.

# Fix

1. Add a `BackpressureConfig::validate()` method that rejects non-finite thresholds, negative values, and yellow ≥ red misordering. Emit a descriptive error.
2. Defense-in-depth inside `classify`: if ANY relevant config threshold or input ratio is non-finite, return `BackpressureTier::Black` to fail closed (same disposition as ft-761tz).
3. Regression tests:
   - config_validate_rejects_nan_yellow_capture
   - config_validate_rejects_red_below_yellow
   - classify_returns_black_on_nan_config_threshold (defense-in-depth path)

# Severity

MEDIUM — requires operator misconfiguration to trigger, but the failure mode is silent (no panic, no error) and the blast radius is 'backpressure is effectively disabled' which can let the watcher runaway into OOM under load. The ft-761tz fix landed as HIGH; applying the same shape here keeps the fleet's failure model consistent.
close_reason: Landed in 5eb9f956 (fix(apc, backpressure, ingest): NaN-proof backpressure)

title: [parser] CSI ? 2026 $ p (DECRQM query) does not reliably dispatch QueryDecPrivateMode
description:
Discovered while shipping ft-d7af6. The parser test for \\x1b[?2026$p at escape-parser/src/parser/mod.rs around line 1313 is currently commented out, and Terminal::advance_bytes(b"\\x1b[?2026$p") does not reliably dispatch QueryDecPrivateMode(Code(SynchronizedOutput)) to perform_csi_mode.

Repro:
1. Build a Terminal with a captured writer (Arc<Mutex<Vec<u8>>>-backed Box<dyn Write + Send>)
2. Send b"\\x1b[?2026h" (BSU) — synchronized_output flag flips to true (verified by getter)
3. Send b"\\x1b[?2026$p" (DECRQM query)
4. Expected: writer receives \\x1b[?2026;1$y
5. Observed: writer is empty in all-tests-in-binary runs; writer has the correct response in single-test isolated runs

The term-layer dispatch arm at frankenterm/term/src/terminalstate/mod.rs:1572 (added in 12b684db6) is correct — both BSU/ESU paths parse correctly and toggle the flag, and the Query arm calls decqrm_response which writes the correct bytes. The disconnect is in the parser → CSI::Mode → perform_csi_mode dispatch chain specifically for the $ intermediate combined with the ? private prefix.

Likely fix scope: re-enable the parser test at parser/mod.rs:1313, debug why the encode path works but the parse-from-bytes path doesn't for this exact sequence, and ship a real round-trip test. Other DECRQM queries (\\x1b[?N$p for N != 2026) likely have the same issue and would benefit from the same fix.

Cross-references:
- ft-d7af6 (term-layer slice that surfaced this)
- escape-parser/src/parser/mod.rs:1313 (commented-out test that was the canary)
- frankenterm/term/tests/dec_synchronized_output.rs (the suppressed query tests this bead unblocks)
close_reason:
Fixed in commit f48ebb6e2.

Investigation: the parser-layer disconnect was a stale TEST, not stale code. The dispatch arm at csi.rs:1852-1855 is correct, the state-machine path is correct, and the term-layer arm at terminalstate/mod.rs:1572 is correct.

The parser test at parser/mod.rs:1313 was commented out because its call signature predates the refactor that absorbed CSI intermediates into the CsiParam stream as CsiParam::P variants. The old call CSI::parse(&[CsiParam::Integer(2026)], &[b'?', b'$'], false, 'p') no longer compiles — CSI::parse now takes (params: &[CsiParam], parameters_truncated: bool, control: char) with intermediates embedded in params.

Fix:
1. Re-enabled the parser test with corrected signature: feed the CsiParam triple [P(b'?'), Integer(2026), P(b'$')] to CSI::parse with control 'p'; round-trips to '\x1b[?2026$p' correctly.
2. Added parse-from-bytes round-trip via round_trip_parse: VT state machine correctly produces Mode::QueryDecPrivateMode(DecPrivateMode::Code(SynchronizedOutput)) from wire bytes.
3. Added 3 term-layer integration tests in frankenterm/term/tests/dec_synchronized_output.rs using CapturedWriter per the bead's repro recipe: BSU+DECRQM=Ps=1, no-BSU+DECRQM=Ps=2, BSU+ESU+DECRQM=Ps=2. All pass.

The 'writer empty in all-tests-in-binary runs' symptom from the bead's repro was likely a test-isolation issue in an earlier state of the term layer that has since been fixed; the suppression note at dec_synchronized_output.rs:21-31 is now stale and the 3 new tests prove the chain works.

10/10 dec_synchronized_output tests pass; 1 parser-layer decset test passes (now with both direct-construction and parse-from-bytes assertions for DECRQM 2026).

title: [sec] ipc.rs: non-constant-time token compare (HIGH)
description: CVSS v3.1 AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N ~5.7. Fixed in 5810a3a4.
