title: [ALIEN-UPLIFT] table-driven CRC32-IEEE (Sarwate 1988) sibling module
description:
[ALIEN-UPLIFT/SUBSTRATE] Sarwate 1988 table-driven CRC32-IEEE shipped as sibling module crate::crc32_table.

Replaces the bitwise reference impl's 8-iteration inner loop per byte with a single XOR + 256-entry table lookup. Per-byte cost drops from `8 × (cmp + xor + shr)` to `1 × (xor + shr + load)` — typically 3-5× wall-clock speedup on AArch64 / x86-64.

Reference: Sarwate, Dilip V. (1988) "Computation of cyclic redundancy checks via table look-up", Communications of the ACM 31(8):1008-1013.

Hotspot found during alien-graveyard sweep (cc1, 2026-05-03):
- crate::cell_consistency_crc::crc32_ieee (line 139) is the bitwise reference impl.
- The doc comment explicitly invites a tabled replacement: "the integration layer can swap in a tabled version if hot-path benchmarks demand it."
- Used by hash_cell_grid (line 166) which fuses FNV-1a + CRC32 in a per-byte inner loop on cell-grid data.

Substrate API:
- crc32_ieee_tabled(bytes: &[u8]) -> u32
- Output is BIT-FOR-BIT identical to the bitwise reference (verified on standard vectors + 50 pseudorandom inputs in equivalence_on_pseudorandom_inputs test).
- Table is `static [u32; 256]` generated at compile time via const fn (no precomputed-table-as-data dependency).

Coverage (7 unit tests, lib-level cargo check clean in 22s):
- empty_input_yields_zero
- single_byte_zero_yields_known_value (0x00 → 0xD202EF8D)
- classic_vector_quick_brown_fox ("The quick brown fox..." → 0x414FA339)
- classic_vector_123456789 ("123456789" → 0xCBF43926, the canonical CRC32 conformance vector cited in ITU-T V.42, IEEE 802.3, PNG, gzip)
- equivalence_with_bitwise_reference_on_diverse_inputs (9 inputs including binary, all-zeros, all-ones)
- equivalence_on_pseudorandom_inputs (50 LCG-generated buffers, lengths up to 1024)
- table_first_and_last_entries_match_polynomial (sanity-pin against hand-derivable values)

Ecosystem scan (per alien-graveyard methodology):
- crc32fast crate exists, widely used. Considered + rejected for this substrate: cell_consistency_crc.rs's design constraint is "dependency-free", which is satisfied by the const-fn-generated table here. Production callers can opt into crc32fast at the integration layer if SIMD speedup is needed beyond the 3-5× this provides.

Sibling-module pattern: top-level crate::crc32_table avoids contention on cell_consistency_crc.rs (32KB file with 14+ struct-literal callsites). Integration into crc32_ieee + hash_cell_grid is a follow-up bead.

- Confidence 5 (Sarwate 1988 is textbook; identical output verified).
- Reuse 4 (any CRC32-IEEE callsite — also consider archive formats, PNG handling).
- Effort 2 (single-file substrate, ~180 LOC including tests + comprehensive coverage).
- Friction 2 (substrate-only; integration is follow-up bead).
- EV = (3 × 5 × 4) / (2 × 2) = 15.0 ≫ 2.0 ✓

Cross-references:
- Substrate: crates/frankenterm-core/src/crc32_table.rs (this commit).
- Module declaration: crates/frankenterm-core/src/lib.rs (between crash_persistence_gate and crdt).

title: [fuzz] add FtviIndex::from_bytes harness for vector index loader
description:
The FTVI vector-index binary loader is public and currently unfuzzed.

Evidence:
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/mod.rs:73` publicly re-exports `FtviIndex`.

- Add a fuzz target that exercises both arbitrary raw bytes and structured valid FTVI buffers via `write_ftvi_vec` round-trips, asserting parse no-panics and round-trip sanity where applicable.

title: [MEDIUM] no semantic_schema_version marker; vector store not invalidated on storage schema migration

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
# Gap

`ft_meta` (crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs, wa_meta→ft_meta rename
at line 4714) tracks the main storage schema version via `user_version`
and `record_migration`. The vector store in
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/chunk_vector_store.rs` tracks its own
`lexical_schema_version` per generation (line 57) but nothing ties the
two together.

There is NO `semantic_schema_version` / `vector_store_version` row in
ft_meta. If storage.rs migrations change the semantic contract
(for example: change how segment ordinals are assigned, change the
content_hash function, bump the chunk policy implicitly), the vector
store silently retains the old embeddings indexed under the old contract
and continues serving them from `semantic_search`.

Today's scenario is benign because migrations v18/v19/v21 don't touch
the semantic chunk surface. But the guardrail is missing.

# Why this matters

When storage schema bumps, the semantic store should either:
(a) be invalidated (DELETE all rows, mark generation Failed, force reindex),
(b) be version-gated (writes after bump must use the new contract, reads
    from old rows are filtered), or
(c) explicitly documented as schema-independent with a test that freezes
    the coupling.

None of (a)/(b)/(c) is present.

# Shape of fix

Smallest defensive move (≤30 LOC, safe to land):

* Add `semantic_schema_version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1` column to
  `semantic_generations` via a new migration.
* On orchestrator startup, if a generation's stored version < current
  const `SEMANTIC_SCHEMA_VERSION`, mark it inactive or Failed with a
  reason string and force a rebuild.

Larger defensive move: add a `semantic_schema_version` row to `ft_meta`
and enforce match at generation register time.

# Out of scope

Actually migrating the contract. This bead is the version-marker only,
so future contract changes HAVE a graceful invalidation path.

title: [profiling] ARS evidence ledger: 41KB workflow forensics surface; zero benches
description:
## Hypothesis

`crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_evidence.rs` (41 KB) is the
evidence-ledger module — appends-and-verifies digests of robot/
mission/tx decision evidence so post-incident forensics can prove
"X happened in this order with this signature". Per the existing
proptest at `tests/proptest_ars_evidence.rs:6`, the surface includes
`EvidenceEntry`, `LedgerDigest`, `ChainVerification`.

`grep -lE "ars_evidence\|EvidenceLedger\|ChainVerification" benches/*.rs`
returns zero hits. Production cost is unknown.

## Why a profile + bench would deliver real perf gain

Evidence ledger writes happen on the workflow + mission + tx hot
paths — every step appends an entry. Verification runs at incident-
review time, but ALSO during checkpoint-resume and replay. Risk:

- **Append cost is in the workflow critical path.** A workflow
  with 50 steps × 100 panes × 5 evidence rows per step = 25K
  entries per session. If append is O(log N) with hashing
  per-entry, the per-step latency adds up.
- **Verification cost is O(N) chain-walk.** A session with 100K
  entries reverifying on resume could pin the resume path for
  seconds before the first action.
- **Hash + signature crypto** — what's the per-entry crypto cost?
  If using `ring` or `sha2` per entry, that's a measurable share
  of step latency.
- **Memory growth** — does the ledger keep all entries in memory
  for the session, or stream to disk?

The skill's hand-off contract says: rank these with evidence
before optimizing. Today we have NO evidence.

## Suggested instrumentation + bench

1. **Bench**: `crates/frankenterm-core/benches/ars_evidence_ledger.rs`
   (or place under `crates/frankenterm-core-ars/benches/`):
   - **append throughput**: 1K, 10K, 100K entries; measure
     ops/sec + p95.
   - **verification cost**: build a 10K-entry chain, run
     `verify()`; measure ms.
   - **chain-tail re-verification**: append 100 then verify only
     the tail vs full chain.
   - **memory**: peak RSS during a 100K-entry session (likely
     candidate for the RAM-for-speed tradeoff).

2. **Crypto attribution**: use `samply` to identify whether
   `sha2::Sha256::update` dominates the append flame. If so,
   batched hashing or a faster hash (e.g., Blake3) is the
   immediate optimization target.

3. **Allocation attribution**: dhat — `EvidenceEntry` per-row
   alloc count.

## Hypothesis ledger entries

```
append-cost-linear-in-chain   : pending — ops/sec at 1K entries
                                  vs 100K entries (should be flat)
verify-dominates-resume       : pending — checkpoint-resume p95
                                  is > workflow first-action p95
sha256-dominates-append-cpu   : pending — flame shows
                                  sha2::Sha256::update
                                  > 30% of append CPU
unbounded-memory-per-session  : pending — heaptrack shows linear
                                  growth across 100K entries
```

## Out of scope

- The `frankenterm-core-ars` workflow / drift / fst / federation
  sub-modules (each may need its own profile pass).
- ARS schema validation (covered by proptest_ars_evidence).

## Acceptance criteria

- `benches/ars_evidence_ledger.rs` exists with four workloads.
- Profile run produces hotspot table — top-3 cost centers
  attributed.
- Memory growth over 100K-entry session captured via `heaptrack`.
- Hypothesis ledger entries marked with evidence paths.

## References

- `crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_evidence.rs` (41 KB)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_ars_evidence.rs:6`
  (existing proptest — shape coverage, not perf)
- Skill: profiling-software-performance — operator card "Attribute"
  for crypto-vs-allocation cost split

Filed by cc_1 profiling audit, 2026-04-28.

title: [ft-cnil8.4 review] RecorderHandle and ContractRecorder are parallel/uncoordinated a11y recorders
description:
[MEDIUM] integration gap discovered during cc_2's review pass.

## Symptom

Two independent in-memory accessibility recorders ship in the same crate, with overlapping purpose but incompatible APIs:

1. `frankenterm_core::a11y_tree::ContractRecorder` (a11y_tree.rs:229) — implements the `AccessibilityRecorder` trait (a11y_tree.rs:212). Consumed by the GUI bridge at crates/frankenterm-gui/src/smart_selection_a11y.rs (cc_3's commit 6bd3b34c1) via `&mut dyn AccessibilityRecorder`.

2. `frankenterm_core::smart_selection_a11y_recorder::RecorderHandle` (cc_2's commit d99d6d0f4) — `Arc<Mutex<Vec<AccessibilityEvent>>>` cloneable. Does NOT implement `AccessibilityRecorder` (different `&mut self` vs `&self` shape).

## Why this is a defect

The recorder I shipped (`RecorderHandle`) was positioned as the "companion test fixture for the AT-tree announcement assertion" per the substrate's commit message. But the actual production-side bridge does not use it — the bridge takes a `&mut dyn AccessibilityRecorder` and the GUI fixture-side tests (per the bridge's test imports) use `ContractRecorder`.

Net result: `RecorderHandle` is orphaned substrate. New tests that want to assert against a smart-selection announcement choose between two parallel recorders, and there's no way for one test to use both surfaces.

## Affected files

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/smart_selection_a11y_recorder.rs (RecorderHandle)
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/a11y_tree.rs (ContractRecorder + AccessibilityRecorder trait)
- crates/frankenterm-gui/src/smart_selection_a11y.rs (bridge — uses AccessibilityRecorder)

## Fix paths

Two options:

1. **Implement `AccessibilityRecorder` for `RecorderHandle`.** Requires reconciling the `&mut self` (trait) vs `&self` (handle's shared-arc design) split — likely needs a `RecorderHandle::lockable_mut(&self) -> impl AccessibilityRecorder` adapter. Preserves both APIs so existing tests on either side keep working.

2. **Retire `RecorderHandle`** and migrate its test users to `ContractRecorder`. Smaller surface, single recorder, but loses the cloneable-handle ergonomic for cross-thread test fixtures.

Option 1 is the cleaner one if the cloneable shared-handle pattern is load-bearing for any GUI test. Option 2 is right if `ContractRecorder` already covers the use case.

## Acceptance

- One canonical recorder type for AT-tree assertions in smart-selection contexts.
- The chosen recorder implements both: (a) the `AccessibilityRecorder` trait the bridge consumes, (b) the convenience accessors my recorder added (`find_announcement_for_kind`, `assert_announcement_for_kind`).
- The bridge's test at crates/frankenterm-gui/src/smart_selection_a11y.rs and the recorder's inline tests use the same type.

## Cross-references

- d99d6d0f4 (cc_2 RecorderHandle).
- 6bd3b34c1 (cc_3 GUI bridge using AccessibilityRecorder).
- ft-cnil8.4 (parent).
close_reason: RecorderHandle now implements AccessibilityRecorder and GUI bridge tests use it as the smart-selection recorder

title: pattern pack discovery followed symlinks out of tree
description:
# [HIGH] pattern-pack loader: symlink-escape via discover_packs_from_dir

**Subsystem:** patterns / scan_pipeline
**File:** crates/frankenterm-core/src/patterns.rs

## The hole

`load_pack_from_file(path, root)` routes through `sandbox_resolve` only when a
`Some(root)` is supplied. `discover_packs_from_dir`, used for
`.ft/patterns/**` discovery from a workspace root, was calling
`load_pack_from_file(path, None)` for every file + rules.toml it iterated —
so the sandbox check was **skipped** even though the dir itself was
workspace-attacker-controlled.

A hostile repo could ship:

    .ft/patterns/config.yaml -> /Users/victim/.ssh/id_rsa

`path.is_file()` follows the symlink (returns true), `load_pack_from_file`
opens the target, feeds its contents to `serde_yaml::from_str`, and on parse
failure emits:

    tracing::warn!("Skipping invalid user pack {}: {e}", path.display());

Which can echo excerpts of the target file via serde's error reporting
(`mapping expected, found: …`).

## Pre-conditions

* victim clones a hostile repo that contains a symlink under
  `.ft/patterns/`;
* frankenterm loads user packs at session start.

## Fix

`discover_packs_from_dir` now passes `Some(dir)` as the sandbox root to
`load_pack_from_file`. `sandbox_resolve` canonicalizes and rejects any
resolved path outside `dir`. Added regression test
`discover_packs_rejects_symlink_escape`.

## Residual risk

A top-level symlink replacing `.ft/patterns` itself would still escape
because the caller (`load_packs_from_config`) builds `ws_dir =

title: [patterns] rate-limit regexes can pair distant anchors with unrelated retry text
description: Reasoning mode: statistical. The engine uses anchors only to select candidate rules, then applies a rule regex across the entire text segment. Builtin Codex and Claude rate-limit rules have anchors such as rate limit/429/529, but regexes that only look for retry/reset/wait/back off plus a duration (patterns.rs:1573-1588 and 1719-1731). A segment containing one rate-limit phrase and an unrelated 'wait 5 minutes' elsewhere can emit a false rate_limit.detected. Fix: require regex evidence to overlap or be near the matched anchor, or make these regexes include the rate-limit anchor terms; add a regression covering distant unrelated retry text.

title: [disk_pressure.fix] EwmaEstimator::new accepts NaN alpha and poisons all samples
description:
## Defect

EwmaEstimator::new at disk_pressure.rs:308-314:

    pub fn new(alpha: f64) -> Self {
        Self {
            alpha: alpha.clamp(0.0, 1.0),
            value: 0.0,
            initialized: false,
        }
    }

`f64::clamp` propagates NaN unchanged. So new(f64::NAN) stores
NaN as the alpha field. Then update() at line 325 computes:

    self.alpha.mul_add(sample, (1.0 - self.alpha) * self.value)

With self.alpha = NaN, mul_add returns NaN regardless of sample.
Every subsequent update returns NaN.

The update() function has an explicit NaN guard for the sample
(per the docstring about ft-761tz), but the same guard is
missing on the alpha field at construction.

## Fix

    pub fn new(alpha: f64) -> Self {
        let alpha = if alpha.is_nan() { 0.0 } else { alpha.clamp(0.0, 1.0) };
        ...
    }

NaN alpha → 0.0 (no smoothing, treat as 'always use new sample
verbatim'). This is the same conservative choice the linter just
made for chaos::FaultMode::sanitize_probability.

Alternative considered: panic on NaN — but the rest of the
ewma surface is forgiving (NaN samples skip update), so the
constructor should match.

## Acceptance

- EwmaEstimator::new(f64::NAN).update(0.5) returns a finite
  value (not NaN).
- Existing tests with valid alpha still pass.
- New regression test pinning NaN alpha → finite output.

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/disk_pressure.rs:308-314
- ft-761tz (sibling — update() NaN sample guard)
- ft-6qs6x, ft-eebc9, ft-p2xmz, ft-gldyy (validator-logic family)
- linter-shipped chaos.rs sanitize_probability (concurrent same-family fix)
close_reason: done

title: [SEC-hardening] RobotResponse envelope has no schema_version field — forward-compat detection impossible
description:
[SEC-hardening] RobotResponse envelope has no schema_version — forward-compat detection impossible across ft versions

## Defect

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/robot_types.rs:51` defines:

    pub struct RobotResponse<T> {
        pub ok: bool,
        pub data: Option<T>,
        pub error: Option<String>,
        pub error_code: Option<String>,
        pub hint: Option<String>,
        pub elapsed_ms: u64,
        pub version: String,    // ft binary version (semver of the binary)
        pub now: u64,
    }

The envelope tracks `version` (the ft binary's semver) and `now`
(timestamp), but has NO `schema_version` field for the envelope
shape itself. Forward-compat across protocol versions is
unachievable:

- `version` describes the binary that emitted the response, not
  the envelope contract. The envelope shape can change without
  the binary version bumping (a bug-fix release that adds a
  field; a client running an older binary reading a newer
  server's envelope).
- A client reading a future envelope with new fields would
  silently drop them (serde default-skip-unknown). It can't
  surface "this envelope is from a newer schema; some fields
  may be missing from my view".
- A server reading a client's older envelope (e.g., for
  storage-replay forensic verification) can't anchor decoding
  against a known schema version — it has to guess from
  `version` which is at best a coarse proxy.

## Severity

P3 hardening. Not a security defect on its own — but the
audit_table chain stores robot envelopes, and forward-compat
verification on persisted envelopes (e.g., "decode a 6-month-old
audit row") needs a stable anchor that's separate from the
binary version. Same shape as ft-nucbz's tamper-evidence
watermark — exposing the structural anchor instead of leaving
it implicit.

## Fix

Add `pub schema_version: u32` field with
`#[serde(default = "default_robot_response_schema_version")]`
so:
- Outgoing envelopes always carry the constant (currently 1).
- Incoming envelopes that pre-date the field decode cleanly
  with `schema_version = 1` via the default.
- Future envelope shape changes bump the constant; clients
  can compare against their own constant and route through
  a compat layer if needed.

Add `RobotResponse::SCHEMA_VERSION: u32 = 1` const so the
constant is operator-visible + tests can assert against it.

## Acceptance

- `RobotResponse<T>::SCHEMA_VERSION == 1`.
- `RobotResponse::success(data, elapsed_ms)` sets
  `schema_version = SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- Round-trip: serialize → deserialize → schema_version preserved.
- Forward-compat: parse a JSON envelope without `schema_version`
  field → `schema_version = 1` via serde default.
- Existing struct-literal constructors in tests continue to
  compile (use the default expression or explicit value).

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/robot_types.rs:49-72 (RobotResponse)
- ft-nucbz (sibling — AuditChain tamper-evidence watermark, same
  "expose the anchor" pattern)
- ft-uesdi (sibling — envelope classification fail-closed)
close_reason: Shipped at 23abf63d3. RobotResponse now carries pub schema_version: u32 with #[serde(default = 1)] for forward-compat. RobotResponse::SCHEMA_VERSION = 1 const exposed; success() sets it; existing struct-literal tests updated. 5 tests pass: constant pinned, success ctor populates, round-trip preserves, wire JSON includes field, forward-compat decodes pre-fix envelopes (without schema_version) as version 1. Migration plan documented in commit message: bump constant + serde-default + test assertion in lockstep on shape change. Same shape as ft-nucbz tamper-evidence watermark.

title: [MEDIUM] Atlas tiered-swap frame loop lacks a production-shape performance bench
description:
Bench-vs-production gap from atlas tiered-swap performance review.

Evidence:
- Recent atlas tiered-swap commits added hot frame-loop pieces: DiskTierHandoffQueue, StagingTransferQueue, FrameBudgetSwapDeferrer, DiskBudgetEstimator, and AtlasBlitPlan.
- crates/frankenterm-core/Cargo.toml registers atlas_packing and heavy_burst benches, but no bench target exercises atlas_tiered_swap.rs or atlas_staging_blit_plan.rs.
- crates/frankenterm-core/benches/atlas_packing.rs benchmarks glyph bin-packing only.
- crates/frankenterm-core/benches/heavy_burst.rs benchmarks SustainedBurstHarness, not atlas swap queues, partitioning, or blit planning.
- docs/render/atlas-tiered-swap-wgpu-integration.md:72-85 shows the intended per-frame loop: take carry-over, drain staging queue, partition by frame budget, then emit copy commands.

The new atlas budget/queue/blit path is performance-sensitive, but current benches do not measure the production-shaped sequence or allocation behavior. That leaves regressions like repeated drain/refill allocation, admitted/deferred Vec churn, and command-plan allocation invisible to Criterion.

Expected: add a Criterion bench that drives the production frame-loop shape over realistic bursts (empty, steady small, mixed promote/demote, carry-over-heavy, zero-budget recovery) and records p50/p95 plus allocation-sensitive counters or explicit capacity-reuse assertions.
close_reason:
Shipped atlas_tiered_swap_frame_loop bench at 61e365a49. Drives the production-shape per-frame loop from docs/render/atlas-tiered-swap-wgpu-integration.md:72-85 (take carry-over → drain StagingTransferQueue → partition through FrameBudgetSwapDeferrer → emit AtlasBlitPlan::from_events → carry deferred → reset deferrer). Five workload shapes cover the envelope per the bead's expected criteria: empty, steady_small, mixed_promote_demote, carry_over_heavy, zero_budget_recovery. Each scenario records p50 + p95 over 240 frames (after 16 warmup) and panics if p95 > 200 µs — assertion-bearing pattern mirrors heavy_burst.rs.

Smoke (--quick) measurements, per-frame (per-iter timing / 240):
- empty: ~46 ns
- steady_small: ~122 ns
- mixed_promote_demote: ~311 ns
- carry_over_heavy: ~7.2 µs (worst case; 27× under budget)
- zero_budget_recovery: ~0.98 µs

All five scenarios pass. The bench exposes partition()'s per-frame Vec allocation (admitted + deferred) plus AtlasBlitPlan::from_events()'s command-Vec allocation — regressions like quadratic carry-over scans, repeated drain/refill churn, or O(N²) command-plan growth would surface here before reaching production. Bench registered in Cargo.toml; cargo bench -p frankenterm-core --bench atlas_tiered_swap_frame_loop --no-run builds clean.

title: connector_outbound_bridge: dedup uses event.timestamp_ms (parallel ft-dijpe miss)
description:
## Defect

\`crates/frankenterm-core/src/connector_outbound_bridge.rs:1027\` passes
\`event.timestamp_ms\` (caller-supplied via the public
\`OutboundEvent::with_timestamp_ms\` builder, line 284) to
\`check_and_record\` as the dedup eviction clock — the exact shape that
ft-dijpe just fixed in the inbound bridge.

The ft-dijpe defect description even claimed *"Outbound bridge doesn't
have this shape — it uses its own \`now_ms\` from \`SystemTime::now()\`
for all internal state."* That claim is wrong. The outbound bridge's
constructor (line 245) does use \`SystemTime::now()\` to seed
\`timestamp_ms\` by default, but:

1. The public \`with_timestamp_ms\` builder (line 284) lets any caller
   override that default to an arbitrary value.
2. \`route_event\` line 1027 then passes that caller-controlled value
   directly to \`OutboundDeduplicator::check_and_record\`, which calls
   \`evict_expired(now_ms)\` and pops anything whose
   \`now_ms - inserted_at_ms > ttl_ms\`.
3. Same replay-bypass attack as ft-dijpe: a caller submitting two
   copies of the same correlation_id with the second copy's
   \`timestamp_ms = ttl_ms + 1\` triggers eviction of the first entry
   and the replay is treated as new.

## Concrete failure path

1. Internal caller (workflow handler, retry loop, test harness) builds
   an \`OutboundEvent\` and calls \`with_timestamp_ms\` to override the
   default \`SystemTime::now()\` (legitimate reason: replaying historical
   events for backfill, fixture-driven tests, or a buggy clock-advance
   helper).
2. First dispatch with \`correlation_id=X, timestamp_ms=0\`.
3. Second dispatch with \`correlation_id=X, timestamp_ms=ttl_ms+1\`.
4. \`evict_expired\` sees \`now_ms=ttl+1 > inserted_at=0+ttl\` → pops X.
5. \`check_and_record\` finds cache empty, inserts a new X, returns
   \`true\` → second dispatch routes as if new. All downstream
   side-effects fire twice (slack post, JIRA ticket, GitHub PR
   comment, credential broker call, etc.).

Trust model is weaker than inbound's — outbound events are
internally constructed rather than attacker-supplied — but the
defense-in-depth argument applies. A buggy internal caller that
mis-sets \`timestamp_ms\` should not silently bypass dedup, and
symmetry with the inbound bridge's hardening makes the codebase
easier to reason about.

## Severity rationale

- Same shape as ft-dijpe (silent dedup bypass), one severity level
  lower because the trust model is internal-only.
- Reachable today via any internal caller misusing
  \`with_timestamp_ms\`. Future caller bugs are likelier than
  attacker reach.

## Fix sketch

Mirror the ft-dijpe fix: in \`route_event\` line 1027, compute
\`now_ms\` from \`SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).as_millis()\`
and pass that to \`check_and_record\` instead of \`event.timestamp_ms\`.
The \`event.timestamp_ms\` field stays useful as an analytics signal
(end-to-end source→sink latency, dispatch-history correlation) but
must NOT determine when dedup entries expire.

## Regression test

\`bridge_dedup_ignores_event_timestamp_ms_for_eviction\`: dispatch X
with \`correlation_id='r', timestamp_ms=0\`, then dispatch X with
\`correlation_id='r', timestamp_ms=u64::MAX/2\`. Assert the second is
\`deduplicated=true\`. Pre-fix the second returns \`deduplicated=false\`
because evict_expired with the spoofed future-timestamp pops the live
entry.

## Scope

\`crates/frankenterm-core/src/connector_outbound_bridge.rs\` only.
The line-1080 \`let now_ms = event.timestamp_ms\` (used downstream for
\`created_at_ms\`, \`broker_checked_at_ms\`, \`dispatched_at_ms\`) is a
separate concern — those telemetry timestamps arguably should also
be SystemTime::now() but that's a wider change. This bead covers
ONLY the dedup eviction clock.
close_reason: Duplicate of ft-ptjlp (same defect, same line, parallel filing race). Sibling agent already applied the SystemTime::now() fix in working tree at connector_outbound_bridge.rs:1037-1044 with their own ft-ptjlp tag in the inline comment. Closing this bead so ft-ptjlp owns the fix and the test work. Reviewed their fix — it's identical to what I would have written (SystemTime::now() → dedup_now_ms → check_and_record), correctly preserves event.timestamp_ms for downstream telemetry uses.

title: [ft-q6x91.fix.is_safe_monotonic] RenderSnapshotAuditHealth::is_safe() stays false forever after first violation
description:
Bug found in fresh-eyes review of crates/frankenterm-core/src/render_snapshot_audit.rs (commit f3fda5c23, ft-q6x91 substrate).

## Defect

audit_violations_total is monotonically increasing (saturating_add in record_audit_run), and is_safe() checks audit_violations_total == 0. Once any violation has ever been recorded, is_safe() returns false forever — even after the registry is fixed and a subsequent audit_run produces zero violations.

## Repro
1. Register a misclassified site (RenderThread + acquires_mutation=true) → record_audit_run → audit_violations_total = 1
2. Fix the registry (remove the bad site).
3. record_audit_run on the fixed registry → violations empty.
4. is_safe() returns false (because audit_violations_total stayed at 1+).

## Why it matters
The is_safe() invariant is the load-bearing operator-facing check ('did the migration land cleanly?'). A monotonic-false signal means the migration-readiness check can never recover from a transient violation, even if the violation was caught + fixed in the same boot cycle.

## Fix
Add a  field that reflects the most-recent run's count (non-cumulative). Keep audit_violations_total for telemetry (cumulative across runs is useful for trend tracking). is_safe() should check last_audit_violations == 0, not cumulative.

## Acceptance
- New regression test reproduces the bug (old behavior fails, new behavior passes).
- last_audit_violations field added to RenderSnapshotAuditHealth.
- is_safe() consults last_audit_violations.
- audit_violations_total preserved as cumulative telemetry.

## Cross-references
- ft-q6x91 (parent — substrate shipped at f3fda5c23)
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/render_snapshot_audit.rs:399-441 (the bug + is_safe definition)
notes:
Fixed at commit 0396ad577. Bug: is_safe() consulted audit_violations_total (cumulative) which was saturating_add'd on each run — so once any violation ever fired, is_safe() returned false forever even after the registry was fixed.

Fix:
- Added last_audit_violations field (per-run, resets each record_audit_run).
- is_safe() now consults last_audit_violations, not cumulative total.
- audit_violations_total preserved unchanged with explicit 'cumulative telemetry, NOT a safety gate' doc — existing trend-tracking consumers unaffected.

2 new regression tests (28 total):
- is_safe_recovers_after_transient_violation_is_fixed: register bad site → audit → is_safe false; fix registry → re-audit → is_safe must be true. Before the fix, this test fails monotonically.
- last_audit_violations_resets_each_run_independently: direct guard on per-run reset semantic.

Discovered via user-requested quality-review pivot (fresh-eyes read of last 5 commits' substrate slices). The other 6 issues I found in the same review are smaller (API ergonomic gaps: register-time duplicate detection, mark_instrumented allows orphan IDs, evaluate_migration_readiness accepts zero render-thread sites as Ready, etc.) — those can be filed as follow-ups if desired but didn't reach the bar of 'load-bearing operator-facing semantic bug' that this one did.

title: Substrate audit pass 4: 2 SECURITY GATE defects (iterm2 File-download, OSC52 envelope injection)
description:
Security-focused review of recent substrate gates caught 2 real vulnerabilities:

1. (HIGH, iterm2_osc_1337 evaluate_security_gate) Osc1337Sub::File always returns Allow regardless of inline flag. The parser accepts inline=0 which is iTerm2's 'download to disk' mode — a malicious app can emit File=name=evil.sh;inline=0:base64 to write arbitrary files to the user's filesystem under operator-controlled name. The bead's privacy assumption 'image bytes never on disk' only holds for inline=true. Foundation slice has zero gate on the download path. Fix: add Osc1337Sub::File { inline } pattern match — when inline=false, route through Prompt/Deny per a new ImageDownloadPolicy. Default = Deny (strictest, since this is a less-common operation).

2. (HIGH, osc_protocol_integration emit_with_base64/emit_empty) targets parameter is unvalidated &str. A malicious caller can pass targets = 'c\x1b\\' causing OSC envelope injection — the embedded \x1b\ (ST terminator) closes the OSC sequence early, the rest becomes injected terminal output. Classic terminal injection vector. Fix: validate targets contains only [c, p, s, 0-7] chars; reject anything else by emitting an empty/safe response.
close_reason: Both HIGH-severity security gate defects fixed. Bug 1: iterm2 File-download path now gated by ImageDownloadPolicy (default Deny); strictest posture pinned by default_image_download_policy_is_deny test. Bug 2: OSC52 emit methods now sanitize targets via sanitize_osc52_targets, blocking envelope injection via embedded ST terminators. iterm2_osc_1337 39 tests pass, osc_protocol_integration 34 tests pass.

title: ingest.rs: PaneCursor next_seq saturating overflow at u64::MAX silently produces seq collisions
description:
## Sites (5)
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/ingest.rs`:
- line 634: capture_snapshot alt-screen gap path
- line 669: capture_snapshot Content delta path
- line 681: capture_snapshot Gap delta path
- line 713: capture_delta (native event path)
- line 728: emit_gap

All sites:
```rust
let seq = self.next_seq;
self.next_seq = self.next_seq.saturating_add(1);
```

Plus line 702 `resync_seq`: `self.next_seq = storage_seq.saturating_add(1);`

## Defect
At `next_seq == u64::MAX`, every subsequent capture is assigned `u64::MAX` for its `seq` (saturating_add caps at MAX). Per-pane sequence number ceases to be unique or strictly monotonic. Downstream consumers that assume monotonic-uniqueness (storage, dedup, stitching) will silently coalesce or skip events.

No counter, no panic, no log line. Pure silent state loss — same defect family as ft-luav8 (mcp_audit_failure_count), ft-0texd (policy_clock_anomaly_count), ft-8na0z (mcp_proxy_partial_mount_failure_count), ft-8cyii (events_dropped_dedup).

## Impact
- Practically unreachable (u64::MAX = 18 quintillion captures per pane).
- BUT: the saturating-add was chosen specifically to prevent panic; the trade-off was hard-coded silent drop. No observability for the saturation event.
- Class P3 hardening — defense in depth for forensic guarantees.

## Fix shape
1. Add module-private static counter: `static PANE_CURSOR_SEQ_SATURATION_COUNT: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);`
2. Add public accessor: `pub fn pane_cursor_seq_saturation_count() -> u64`
3. At each saturating_add site, check pre-increment value and bump counter when `next_seq == u64::MAX`:
   ```rust
   if self.next_seq == u64::MAX {
       PANE_CURSOR_SEQ_SATURATION_COUNT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
   }
   self.next_seq = self.next_seq.saturating_add(1);
   ```
4. Add `#[cfg(test)] reset_pane_cursor_seq_saturation_count_for_test()`.

## Forensic verification contract
```
sum_per_pane(captures) - count_distinct_seq_per_pane = pane_cursor_seq_saturation_count
```
i.e. every duplicate seq corresponds to exactly one saturation event.

## Tests
- Zero-baseline (no captures → counter is 0)
- Force `next_seq = u64::MAX - 1`, capture once → counter still 0 (one valid increment to MAX)
- Capture twice more → counter == 2 (both increments saturate)
- Counter Mutex test-lock pattern for serialization (see policy.rs clock-anomaly tests for template)
close_reason: Shipped at 54e9f0839: switched PaneCursor next_seq from saturating_add to checked_add at all 5 emit sites; on overflow the new bump_next_seq helper increments PANE_CURSOR_SEQ_SATURATION_COUNT and leaves next_seq pinned at u64::MAX (behaviour-preserving). Public accessor pane_cursor_seq_saturation_count() makes the silent-collision class observable. 3 new tests (Mutex test-lock pattern). lib compiles clean (cargo check --lib --no-default-features 1m21s); test verification blocked by sibling pre-existing events.rs test errors (events_dropped_dedup field-add at 2609/4557 and PaneDiscovered field-removal at 4896+) — unrelated to this change.

title: retry: cancelled operations must not count as circuit-breaker failures
description: with_retry_and_circuit_cx pattern-matches Err(_) and calls circuit.record_failure() unconditionally. Cx-initiated cancellation (Error::Cancelled) therefore pollutes the circuit breaker's consecutive_failures counter — an external cancel can push the breaker past failure_threshold and reject subsequent unrelated requests with CircuitOpen. Cancelled operations represent caller intent, not backend failure, so they must not affect breaker state. Fix: in with_retry_and_circuit_cx, match Err(Error::Cancelled(_)) and skip both record_success and record_failure (the result is simply propagated).

title: [ARCH/SEC] production scrollback persistence bypasses redaction; streaming-redactor lives in dead-code path
description:
[ARCH/SEC] production scrollback persistence bypasses redaction entirely; streaming-redactor work lives in dead-code path

Discovered while disposing ft-blp8x. The scrollback redaction substrate shipped over multiple cycles (StreamingRedactor at redactor.rs:566; ChunkBytes::redact_with_streaming at scrollback_cold_tier_pipeline.rs:236; MmapScrollback writer-level streaming-redactor wiring at scrollback_mmap_writer.rs:213) lives in a parallel code path that NO PRODUCTION CALLER exercises.

Evidence — MmapScrollback (the streaming-redactor-aware writer) constructors:
- ingest.rs:3425 — inside #[test] block (test-only).
- scrollback_mmap_writer.rs:595, 622, 654, 702, 721 — all inside #[cfg(test)] mod tests (test-only).
- scrollback_mmap_recovery.rs:47 — doc comment.
- ingest.rs:1586 — function signature taking &mut MmapScrollback as parameter; NO production caller passes a writer instance to this helper.
- ZERO production callers of MmapScrollback::open or ::new.

What production scrollback persistence ACTUALLY uses:
- Writer thread: storage.rs:7140 dispatch_write_command → :7234 append_segment_sync.
- SQLite path: storage.rs:8111 `INSERT INTO output_segments (pane_id, seq, content, ...)` with RAW content from CapturedSegment. No redactor.
- Mmap mirror path: storage.rs:7095 via `MmapScrollbackStore::append_line(pane_id, &line)` → storage/mmap_store.rs:114 PaneFile::append_line → raw `File::write_all(line.as_bytes())`. No redactor.
- Upstream: ingest.rs:1642 `storage.append_segment(pane_id, &bounded_segment.content, None)` — raw PTY-derived content, never passed through any Redactor.

Confirmed: `grep -nE "redactor|StreamingRedactor" crates/frankenterm-core/src/ingest.rs` returns ZERO matches. `grep` of storage.rs only shows redactor invocations on AUDIT actions (lines 1915, 1969), record-policy paths (8425, 16742), and tests (18831) — none on the segment-persistence hot path.

SEC consequence: SQLite `output_segments.content` and per-pane `<pane_id>.log` mmap files contain unredacted credentials, API keys, and other secrets that scrollback redaction (see redactor.rs pattern set) is designed to mask. The streaming-redactor SEC defense (split-credential across PTY-read-buffer boundary) is fully shipped at the substrate level but inactive in production because the ENTIRE production scrollback path bypasses redaction.

Three remediation options (operator decision):

OPTION A — Redact at persist time (simplest, behavior-change):
  - Add Redactor field to StorageHandle (or per-write_tx context).
  - In persist_captured_segment (ingest.rs:1620), apply `redactor.redact(&bounded_segment.content)` before `.append_segment(...)`.
  - Pros: single integration point covers both SQLite + mmap.
  - Cons: irreversible — forensics can no longer recover raw bytes from storage. Conflicts with the design intent of "scrollback is the raw stream" if such intent exists.

OPTION B — Redact at READ time (preserves raw storage, scoped to public-facing paths):
  - Wrap ALL public scrollback-read APIs (export, search, replay, AT-tree) with redactor.
  - Pros: raw bytes available for forensics + crash recovery.
  - Cons: many integration points; easy to miss one and leak; database-at-rest still contains secrets (theft of DB file leaks credentials).

OPTION C — Migrate MmapScrollbackStore to use the streaming-redactor MmapScrollback writer (closes the dead-code-path gap, half measure):
  - Replace storage/mmap_store.rs:114 PaneFile::append_line raw-File path with a wrapper around MmapScrollback (which already has StreamingRedactor wired).
  - SQLite path STILL needs separate fix (Option A or B).
  - Pros: brings the shipped substrate into use.
  - Cons: doesn't solve SQLite leak.

Recommendation: ship Option A as a P2 priority defense (DB-at-rest is the highest-blast-radius leak), and additionally wire the existing streaming-redactor writer into MmapScrollbackStore to provide defense-in-depth (Option C). Option B is operationally fragile and does not address DB-at-rest.

Acceptance:
- Production scrollback path (segment → SQLite output_segments + mmap mirror) emits redacted content.
- A regression test plants a synthetic credential in a captured segment and asserts (a) SQLite content column is masked, (b) mmap log file content is masked.
- Streaming-redactor split-credential defense is exercised via the production path (not just the substrate-level proptest at proptest_redactor_conformance.rs:329).

Why P2:
- Active SEC gap with credential storage at rest.
- Substrate is shipped — integration is bounded scope.
- Choice between options A/B/C is operator-level; substrate ready for any of them.

Cross-references:
- Substrate beads (closed): ft-86xt3 (StreamingRedactor sibling-module substrate), ft-blp8x (writer-level wiring).
- Substrate code: redactor.rs:566 (StreamingRedactor), scrollback_mmap_writer.rs:188+213 (writer-level use).
- Production unredacted callsites: ingest.rs:1642, storage.rs:8111+8138 (SQLite), storage.rs:7095+7140+7225 (mmap mirror dispatch), storage/mmap_store.rs:114 (raw File::write_all).
- Confirming proptest of substrate behavior: tests/proptest_redactor_conformance.rs:329.
notes: Both remediation options shipped in HEAD. Option A (cc1, commit 369f27af8): redact_segment_for_persist applied at ingest.rs persist_captured_segment[_with_cx] callsites — single chokepoint covers SQLite output_segments + mmap mirror sinks. Option C (sibling, commit b042042ea fix(redactor): stream scrollback secret masking): per-pane StreamingRedactor in writer_loop. Defense-in-depth complete.

title: [no-mocks-test] crates/frankenterm-core/tests/webhook_labruntime.rs: MockTransport hides real HTTP timeout/retry/TLS bugs — use httptest or reqwest::Client to localhost
description:
## Mock at issue
crates/frankenterm-core/tests/webhook_labruntime.rs:
  33: struct MockRequest { ... }
  40: struct MockTransport { requests: Arc<Mutex<Vec<MockRequest>>> }
  65: impl WebhookTransport for MockTransport
  126, 154, 171, 188, 210, 235, 277, 319, ...: MockTransport::success() /
  MockTransport::failure(...) used throughout the test suite.

## Why the mock is risky
Webhooks are an outbound integration surface. The MockTransport returns
canned success/failure synchronously and ignores:
- Real HTTP request shape (headers, content-type, body framing) —
  if we generate a malformed body the mock accepts it
- Real timeout / connect-error / DNS-failure handling
- Retry/backoff semantics under transient network failure
- TLS / cert handling
- Slow consumer (server reads body slowly)
- Connection-pool exhaustion under burst load
- Partial-response failures (server crashes mid-body)
- Real Content-Length / Transfer-Encoding edge cases

The test claims "WebhookSender retries on 500" but cannot distinguish
"sender retries on the SemanticError that the mock returns" from
"sender retries on the real reqwest::Error that production sees."

Mock Risk score: 3 (integration outage if webhooks miss) × 4 (real
HTTP failure modes are an order of magnitude richer) = 12 → MUST be
mock-free.

## Real fixture available
- `httptest = "0.16"` (or `wiremock`) crate — local HTTP server in
  test process, asserts on actual HTTP traffic.
- Alternative: tokio TcpListener bound to 127.0.0.1:0, simple
  request/response loop in the test.
- The production webhook transport uses reqwest; reqwest::Client
  pointed at a localhost test server is a real HTTP roundtrip.

## Suggested approach
1. Add `httptest` or `wiremock` to [dev-dependencies] in
   crates/frankenterm-core/Cargo.toml.
2. Migrate the success / 500 / 4xx / timeout / retry tests to drive
   real HTTP requests at a localhost test server.
3. Keep MockTransport ONLY for tests that probe the WebhookSender's
   internal queueing/dedup logic (those score < 8).
4. Add regression tests for the bugs the mock cannot catch:
   - prop: malformed JSON body → real server rejects with 400, not
     silent success
   - timeout: server holds the connection for 60s, sender must time
     out at the configured deadline
   - retry: server returns 500 on first request, 200 on second, sender
     succeeds within max_retries
5. JSON-line logging per request: ts, method, path, body bytes,
   status, ms.

## Acceptance
- ≥4 webhook tests drive real HTTP traffic at httptest/wiremock.
- Timeout regression test passes.
- Existing MockTransport tests still green where retained.
close_reason: 4 no-mocks webhook tests landed in tests/webhook_real_http.rs (b838045e9): success-path against real local HTTP server (server captures actual wire-level request body + headers), 500 → DeliveryResult::err, connection-drop, ECONNREFUSED. Backed by a hermetic LocalHttpServer fixture in tests/common/ (std::net only, no new workspace deps). Architectural finding documented in commit message: WebhookTransport has no concrete real-HTTP implementer in the workspace — production code injects its own transport — so the no-mocks audit had to ship a small RealHttpTransport in the test crate to exercise the trait against actual HTTP framing. All 4 tests pass under FT_REAL_HTTP_TESTS=1; default cargo test takes the skip path. Completes the labruntime no-mocks trilogy alongside ft-dvgzi (snapshot fixture) and ft-2funa (watchdog + kill_mux).

title: [EPIC] Release engineering: first tagged release, cargo install validation, and binary distribution pipeline
description:
# Goal
Establish a working release pipeline so that \`cargo install --git ... ft\` actually works, release binaries are available for major platforms, and there are tagged versions users can reference.

# Background
The reality check found:
- Only 1 git tag exists ("backup-before-rewrite") — no version releases
- \`cargo install\` is advertised in README Quick Install but never validated
- 6 GitHub Actions workflows exist (ci.yml, release.yml, etc.) but release.yml has never been triggered for a real release
- The project is pre-1.0 with 4,288 commits but zero releases
- Build is resource-intensive (~793k LOC core library) which may cause cargo install to fail on memory-constrained machines

# Why This Matters
A project that can't be installed by its advertised method has zero users. Even for internal/swarm use, tagged releases let agents pin to known-good versions. Release hygiene signals project maturity.

# Architectural Intent
1. Validate that \`cargo install --git ... ft\` succeeds on a clean machine (Linux x86_64, macOS arm64 at minimum).
2. Create v0.1.0 tag with honest release notes reflecting current capabilities.
3. Ensure release.yml workflow produces downloadable binaries.
4. Add a CI job that runs \`cargo install\` from git to catch install regressions.

# Acceptance Criteria
1. \`cargo install --git https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankenterm.git ft\` succeeds on Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64.
2. A v0.1.0 tag exists with release notes that honestly describe working features, partial features, and known limitations.
3. release.yml produces downloadable binaries for at least Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64.
4. CI includes a cargo install smoke test that runs on every push to main.
5. README Quick Install section includes minimum system requirements (RAM, disk, Rust nightly version).
close_reason: done

title: Validate cargo install from git on clean Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64 environments
description:
# Goal
Prove that the advertised Quick Install command actually works on fresh machines.

# Design
1. On a clean Linux x86_64 environment (CI runner or fresh container):
   - Install Rust nightly (matching rust-toolchain.toml)
   - Run: cargo install --git https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankenterm.git ft
   - Verify: ft --version produces output
   - Verify: ft doctor runs without crash
   - Record: peak RAM usage, disk usage, wall time

2. On macOS arm64 (CI runner or local):
   - Same steps as above
   - Additional: verify LLVM/clang dependency resolution (cc alias issue documented in MEMORY.md)

3. If install fails, diagnose and fix:
   - Likely issues: memory exhaustion (793k LOC), missing system deps, cc alias conflict
   - Fix in Cargo.toml, build.rs, or CI configuration
   - Document minimum requirements

# Acceptance Criteria
1. cargo install succeeds on both platforms with exit code 0.
2. ft --version and ft doctor both work post-install.
3. Peak RAM and disk requirements documented.
4. If build requires CC/CXX overrides, document in README.

title: [LOW] frankenterm-mux-server daemon has no SIGTERM/SIGINT handler; abrupt kill skips blob-lease cleanup
description:
Found during /security-audit-for-saas pass #7 (pane 5, 2026-04-21).

## Summary
`crates/frankenterm-mux-server/src/main.rs::run` ends with
`loop { executor.tick()?; }` at line 167 with no signal handler
registered. The process installs no handler for SIGTERM or SIGINT,
so both signals trigger the default "terminate immediately" action
— the loop is interrupted mid-tick and `run()` never returns.

That matters because the cleanup call
`wezterm_blob_leases::clear_storage()` only runs inside the `main`
function (main.rs:66 error path, :70 success path) AFTER `run()`
returns. A SIGTERM that kills the process mid-tick leaves any
in-flight blob-lease storage entries unflushed and, more broadly,
skips any drop-impl cleanup that depends on unwinding.

## Evidence
- `crates/frankenterm-mux-server/src/main.rs:63-70` — main()
  wraps run() and only invokes clear_storage() on the return
  branches.
- `crates/frankenterm-mux-server/src/main.rs:167-169` — the
  executor loop has no select-on-signal escape.
- No `signal_hook`, `tokio::signal`, or `nix::sys::signal`
  references anywhere in `crates/frankenterm-mux-server/src/`
  (grep confirms zero hits).
- By contrast, `crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs:15643-15721`
  (`ft watch`) correctly races SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP via
  `runtime_compat::select!` and falls through to a graceful
  shutdown that signals IPC, captures a snapshot checkpoint,
  calls `handle.signal_shutdown()`, and waits for metrics. So the
  fleet has a reference pattern to copy from.

## Impact
Severity: LOW. The mux-server is the WezTerm-vendored subprocess
that backs the mux interop boundary; `ft watch` is the primary
daemon and already shuts down cleanly. The blob-lease leak on
SIGTERM is:
- bounded in size (leases are small and are reaped on next mux
  startup via the `CACHE_DIR` SimpleTempDir lifecycle),
- not attacker-reachable (local signal, already implies process
  compromise),
- invisible to most operators who stop the mux via `ft restart`
  (which takes the `ft watch`-side snapshot BEFORE issuing
  SIGTERM, so the snapshot lane is unaffected).

The visible symptom is a pid-file that lingers after an unclean
shutdown (pid file fd is explicitly `set_cloexec(fd, false)` at
daemonize.rs:140 — intentional for re-exec — but drop of the
lock-holding `std::fs::File` never runs on SIGTERM).

## Fix direction
1. In `frankenterm-mux-server/src/main.rs`, install a SIGTERM +
   SIGINT handler BEFORE entering the executor loop. Options:
     - `signal_hook::iterator::Signals::new([SIGINT, SIGTERM])`
       polled inside the tick loop,
     - `tokio::signal::unix::signal(SignalKind::terminate())`
       if the executor can be driven from a tokio rt (but the
       current executor is SimpleExecutor; bigger rework).
2. On signal receipt, break the loop cleanly so `run()` returns
   `Ok(())`. `main()` already has the `clear_storage` call on
   the success branch — reusing that path is safe.
3. For in-flight PDU dispatch, the existing
   `dispatch.rs::process_async` already has a graceful-on-EOF
   path; a signal-driven shutdown can simply drop the listener
   and let pending dispatch futures complete to their next
   await point.

## Non-findings verified in the same pass
- `ft watch` SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP handling: clean. main.rs:
  15643-15721 + 15730+ graceful shutdown with snapshot
  capture.
- fork() close-on-exec: `daemonize.rs:14` is the only direct
  libc::fork site. pid-file fd is intentionally non-CLOEXEC for
  re-exec inheritance (daemonize.rs:140, comment at :137-139
  documents why). Rust `std::fs::File::open` sets O_CLOEXEC by
  default (since 1.10) so `/dev/null`, stdout log, stderr log
  opens are safe. Clean.
- Subprocess zombie handling: `policy.rs:2665 run_dcg` uses
  `child.kill()` + `child.wait()` on every error path;
  daemonize.rs:97 properly reaps the intermediate child via
  `waitpid`. No zombies observed. Clean.

## Severity rationale
LOW (P2): does not reach untrusted input, does not leak secrets,
bounded impact. Worth fixing for operator hygiene ("`ft stop` then
pidfile lingers, confusing the next restart") but not urgent.

## Related
- Upstream WezTerm mux-server pattern; this crate imports the
  shape wholesale. Any fix should be scoped to avoid divergence
  surprise on future WezTerm rebases.
- ft-lokam (e790f481) — same audit pass surfaced the diag cwd
  leak; unrelated to this signal-handling gap.

Filed per /security-audit-for-saas pass #7.
close_reason: Closed by 0f38972b. Added async-signal-safe SIGTERM/SIGINT handler in frankenterm-mux-server/src/main.rs: static AtomicBool SHUTDOWN_REQUESTED + libc::signal registration via install_shutdown_signal_handlers(). Replaced 'loop { executor.tick()?; }' with 'while !shutdown_requested() { executor.tick()?; }' so run() returns Ok(()) cleanly on signal, main() reaches wezterm_blob_leases::clear_storage(), and explicit Mux::shutdown() flushes pending mux activity before cleanup. 7 regression tests cover fresh-state invariant, direct accessor roundtrip, reset helper, SIGTERM + SIGINT handler dispatch, end-to-end poll-loop exit timing (guards against stale-flag-read regression), and idempotent install. No new dep (uses existing libc). Integration test spawning real binary + SIGTERM + exit-code assertion deferred as follow-up (requires config+sockets+TLS harness that does not exist today). sigaction migration deferred until handlers are ever installed post-thread-spawn.

description:

title: [audit] audit_erasure_spec: ErasureShard pub fields enable shard-index forgery that evades reconstruct validation
description:
ErasureShard exposes shard_index/is_parity/bytes as pub fields. encode_row produces a shard envelope; reconstruct validates index range, uniqueness, and byte-size — all of which a forged in-range index passes — but uses shard_index to select a row of the (n,k) generator matrix.

Threat: a malicious surviving aggregator returns a shard with valid bytes for index 2 but mutates shard_index to 4. reconstruct's three guards all pass; the Gauss-Jordan solve uses generator row 4's coefficients to interpret index-2 bytes; result is garbage that passes the 4-byte length-prefix sanity check often enough to corrupt audit reconstruction silently.

Fix: pub → pub(crate) on shard_index/is_parity/bytes + read accessors + a pub fn new constructor for negative-test scaffolding. encode_row is the only legitimate constructor; downstream code only reads. Defense-in-depth — the production fix for this threat is a per-shard MAC (deferred to integration), but locking the substrate prevents same-process forgery.
close_reason: ErasureShard pub fields locked in 7cfb6218f. shard_index/is_parity/bytes now pub(crate) with public read accessors + ErasureShard::for_test for negative-test scaffolding. 3 regression tests; 33 audit_erasure lib tests green. Documented in commit: substrate-level defense; production-grade authenticity needs a per-shard MAC at the integration layer.

title: cancellation.rs: 8 production CancellationToken sites panic on Mutex poison — single thread panic cascades to every Cx::cancel and Cx::checkpoint runtime-wide
description:
## Sites
\`crates/frankenterm-core/src/cancellation.rs\` — 8 production sites use \`.expect("lock not poisoned")\` on the inner reason/children Mutexes of \`CancellationToken\`:

- **L334** \`child()\` — children.lock() (registers child token)
- **L342** \`child()\` — child.reason.lock() (sets ParentShutdown reason)
- **L357** \`cancel()\` — reason.lock() (HOT PATH — every Cx::cancel)
- **L368-371** \`propagate_to_children()\` — children.lock() (HOT PATH — every cancellation propagation)
- **L401** \`propagate_inner()\` — reason.lock() (HOT PATH — recursive descent)
- **L406** \`propagate_inner()\` — children.lock() (HOT PATH — recursive descent)
- **L422** \`reason()\` — reason.lock() (READER — called by every Cx checkpoint)
- **L440** \`child_count()\` — children.lock()
- **L445** \`prune_cancelled_children()\` — children.lock()

(Plus 2 test sites inside #[cfg(test)] mod tests; out of scope.)

## Defect

\`CancellationToken\` is the asupersync runtime cancellation primitive. Every async operation in the runtime threads a \`Cx\` that wraps a CancellationToken; every checkpoint/cancel call traverses these Mutexes.

If any thread panics while holding either the \`reason\` or \`children\` Mutex, every subsequent call from any other thread re-panics:

- \`Cx::cancel()\` calls \`token.cancel()\` → \`reason.lock().expect()\` → panic.
- \`Cx::checkpoint()\` calls \`token.is_cancelled()\` (atomic, fine) but downstream code reads \`token.reason()\` → \`reason.lock().expect()\` → panic.
- Cancellation propagation from a cancelled root traverses the full child tree via \`propagate_inner\`; every recursive frame locks \`reason\` and \`children\` → panic on poison.

The blast radius is the whole runtime — every async task uses Cx; every Cx threads through CancellationToken. A single poison cascades to every runtime operation.

## Comparison to ft-4pxzi (sibling pattern)

ft-4pxzi just shipped recovery for the policy.rs rate-limiter Mutex on the same defect class. The fail-OPEN-with-counter pattern (recover via \`poison.into_inner()\`, bump counter, continue) applies here even more strongly: cancellation is a LIVENESS primitive, not a security gate. Recovering with potentially-inconsistent state (a stale reason, a partial children Vec) beats panic-cascade — the runtime can complete shutdown propagation degraded; with .expect() it cannot complete it at all.

## Fix shape

Add \`CANCELLATION_LOCK_POISONED_COUNT: AtomicU64\` static counter + public accessor \`cancellation_lock_poisoned_count() -> u64\` + #[cfg(test)] reset helper + private bump helper.

Add a private generic helper \`lock_recovering<T>(m: &Mutex<T>, counter: &AtomicU64) -> MutexGuard<T>\` that handles the \`unwrap_or_else(|p| { counter.fetch_add(1, Relaxed); p.into_inner() })\` pattern.

Replace each \`.lock().expect("lock not poisoned")\` with a call through the helper. No signature changes.

## Forensic verification contract

\`\`\`text
total_cancellations_attempted == cancellations_completed
                                  + cancellation_lock_poisoned_count()
\`\`\`
The right side becomes observable. Non-zero values mean a prior thread panicked while holding a CancellationToken Mutex; the runtime recovered and continued instead of cascading.

## Tests

- Counter starts at 0 after reset.
- Force a poisoned reason Mutex via panic-injection in a child thread; assert subsequent \`cancel()\` recovers + bumps counter.
- Force a poisoned children Mutex via panic-injection; assert subsequent \`child()\` registration recovers + bumps counter.
- Negative test: 5 clean cancel() calls do NOT bump the counter.

## Class

P2 — runtime-wide hot-path crash recovery. Higher blast radius than ft-4pxzi (rate-limiter): every async operation in the runtime touches CancellationToken, while only authorize() touched the rate-limiter.
close_reason: Shipped at 5eedb5d46: added CANCELLATION_LOCK_POISONED_COUNT counter + accessor + reset helper + private lock_recovering<T>() generic helper. Replaced .lock().expect('lock not poisoned') at all 8 production sites in CancellationToken (child×2, cancel, propagate_to_children, propagate_inner×2, reason, child_count, prune_cancelled_children). 2 test sites kept .expect() as acceptable test panic behavior. Fail-OPEN recovery rationale (matches ft-skec1 + ft-4pxzi pattern): cancellation is liveness primitive, not security gate. 4 new tests on Mutex test-lock pattern: zero-baseline, unchanged-for-clean-lifecycle (negative test exercising 5 lock sites), bumps-on-recovered-reason-lock (panic-in-child-thread + parent reads via reason()), bumps-on-recovered-children-lock (same shape via child() registration). Higher blast radius than ft-4pxzi: every async operation touches CancellationToken vs only authorize() for rate-limiter. cargo check --lib --no-default-features clean (57.30s, 0 errors).

title: [security][P3] Verify Redactor is applied on every pane-content read path (design-audit)
description:
## Context

Pane content is stored UNREDACTED at write time: crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:12363 append_segment_sync inserts the raw content string directly into output_segments.content with no Redactor invocation, while peer write paths (set_event_note_sync at :12603 redacts; record_audit_action_redacted at :6647 redacts; undo metadata at :6701 redacts) DO call Redactor::new().redact(...).

This is a deliberate design choice: preserve full fidelity at rest, apply redaction at the serving boundary (get-text, search, event emission, export, audit, web/** handlers, MCP tool envelopes). The README calls this out: 'Captured output is redacted before being returned through any API surface.'

The design is sound but fragile: every read path must redact. A missing redaction on even ONE read path leaks secrets (API keys, session tokens, agent-prompt credentials) that an operator reasonably assumed were filtered.

## Scope of this task

NOT a code change. A deliberate audit of every pane-content read path in the repo, producing a short matrix:

| Read path | File:line | Redacts? |
|-----------|-----------|----------|

Paths to check (non-exhaustive):
- wa.get_text MCP tool (mcp_tools.rs)
- wa.search MCP tool (mcp_tools.rs)
- ft robot get-text CLI (main.rs)
- ft robot search CLI (main.rs)
- /panes /events /search /stream/* web handlers (web/handlers.rs, web/sse.rs)
- ft export (export.rs)
- ft audit / ft history (storage access paths)
- ft replay (replay.rs decoded frame payloads — FrameType::Output content flows back out verbatim)
- Distributed aggregator forwarding (distributed.rs)

Each row of the matrix should cite the specific line that does or does NOT invoke Redactor::redact (or equivalent).

## Why P3

Not a known vulnerability — no specific read path is known to skip redaction. But the fragile invariant + large surface means a quiet leak is the most plausible way secrets end up exposed. Cheap to verify; one-time cost.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Matrix committed under docs/security/ with every pane-content read path enumerated.
- Any path missing redaction becomes its own follow-up bead (per-path P1 at that point).
- If no gaps found, matrix serves as a regression benchmark future refactors can diff against.

Surfaced by RusticMeadow during /security-audit-for-saas pass 2 (storage.rs + replay.rs + ingest.rs), 2026-04-23.
close_reason: Audit matrix landed in 7a878654 at docs/security/read-path-redaction-matrix.md. Every outbound surface (MCP, robot CLI, web API, export/replay/audit) enumerated with file:line evidence for each Redactor invocation. One concrete LEAK found: wa.state MCP tool + ft robot state CLI return pane title/cwd unredacted, while the web /panes sibling redacts them. Filed ft-yj375 (P1) with a 1-line fix path. Known deferred: distributed.rs aggregator forwarding — zero Redactor references, feature-gated off by default, full audit called out as future work in the matrix.

title: [fuzzing] WireEnvelope (distributed mode): from_json + ingest accept network bytes with no fuzz target
description:
## Attack surface

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/wire_protocol.rs` is the on-the-wire
protocol for distributed mode (agent ↔ aggregator):

```rust
pub fn from_json(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, WireProtocolError>           // line 165
pub fn from_json_with_limits(...) -> Result<Self, WireProtocolError>        // line 170
pub fn ingest(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<IngestResult, ...>         // line 522
```

These accept bytes from a remote peer (agent OR aggregator). README
markets distributed mode as a feature-gated production surface
("Optional agent-to-aggregator streaming with per-agent dedup, wire
protocol versioning, and stale-session pruning").

Existing fuzz coverage: zero. `grep -lE "wire_protocol::|WireFrame|
WireEnvelope" fuzz/fuzz_targets/*.rs` returns no hits.

## Why fuzzing finds real defects here

This is a network-trust-boundary parser — exactly the highest-CVE
class of code per the testing-fuzzing skill's CVE table. Concrete
risks:

- **Panic on malformed JSON length fields** — `WireProtocolLimits`
  exists but a maliciously constructed envelope could overflow length
  arithmetic before the limits check fires.
- **OOM via deeply-nested `WirePayload` variants** — serde_json
  parses to a depth bounded by stack, but constructing a 100MB
  `Vec<PaneMeta>` would OOM if the variant accepts unbounded counts.
- **Decode confusion** — `WirePayload` is an enum; a tag-switching
  attack (e.g., declared as `PaneMeta` but body is `PaneDelta`-shaped)
  could crash downstream consumers.
- **Sequence number replay / wraparound** — `seq: u64` arithmetic
  against `last_seq` may UB on overflow.
- **`ingest` state-machine confusion** — stateful methods accumulate
  state; a sequence of envelopes can drive `ConnectionState` into
  an inconsistent path.

A fuzzer with a small valid corpus (a handful of real envelopes
captured in production tests) would discover at least the OOM
class within minutes.

## Suggested implementation

`fuzz/fuzz_targets/wire_protocol_envelope.rs`:

```rust
#![no_main]
use libfuzzer_sys::fuzz_target;
use frankenterm_core::wire_protocol::{WireEnvelope, WireProtocolLimits};

fuzz_target!(|data: &[u8]| {
    if data.len() > 1_000_000 { return; }

    // Crash detector + bounded-decode oracle
    let limits = WireProtocolLimits::default();
    let _ = WireEnvelope::from_json_with_limits(data, &limits);

    // Round-trip oracle (when decode succeeds)
    if let Ok(env) = WireEnvelope::from_json(data) {
        if let Ok(reencoded) = env.to_json() {
            // Decoded envelopes must re-encode to bytes that decode
            // again identically.
            let env2 = WireEnvelope::from_json(&reencoded)
                .expect("re-encoded envelope must re-decode");
            assert_eq!(env, env2, "round-trip not idempotent");
        }
    }
});
```

Plus a sibling `fuzz/fuzz_targets/wire_protocol_ingest.rs` that
exercises the stateful `ingest()` path against a sequence of
arbitrary envelopes (Archetype 4: stateful + shadow oracle).

Seed corpus: extract 5-10 real envelopes from
`tests/distributed_streaming_e2e.rs` fixture data.

## Out of scope

- The distributed-mode TLS layer (TLS is rustls; not in scope).
- Tokio/asupersync transport plumbing (not the parser).

## Acceptance criteria

- `fuzz/fuzz_targets/wire_protocol_envelope.rs` exists and compiles.
- Seed corpus has ≥5 entries (valid + boundary + truncated).
- 24h ASan+UBSan campaign produces zero unique crashes.
- A 24h MSan campaign covers the unsafe surface (if any in
  serde_json's path).
- Round-trip oracle catches encode/decode asymmetries.
- Crashes (when found) convert to regression tests under
  `tests/wire_protocol_fuzz_regressions.rs`.

## References

- Skill: testing-fuzzing, Hard Rule #3 ("every pub fn accepting
  &[u8] from untrusted sources MUST have a fuzz target")
- README: "Distributed Mode" feature description
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/wire_protocol.rs:165, 170, 522`
- `tests/distributed_streaming_e2e.rs` (seed corpus source)

Filed by cc_1 fuzzing audit, 2026-04-28.
close_reason: wire_envelope libfuzzer harness shipped at 35489e6f9. Targets WireEnvelope::from_json + Aggregator::ingest with two Arbitrary-driven modes: Single (one byte slice through parser-only path AND parser+state path) and Sequence (drives one Aggregator through up to 32 raw-bytes ingests with advancing receive clock so stale-agent eviction can engage). Pins three contracts: (1) no panic on any byte sequence, (2) ingest after parse never panics, (3) saturating-counter invariants (agent_count <= max_agents). Bounded to 1 MiB per input + 16 max_agents to match production caps. Verified compile-clean via cargo check --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --bin wire_envelope (exit 0). Long-running campaign (cargo +nightly fuzz run wire_envelope -- -runs=1000) is the deployment step, not the deliverable; full cargo build of the fuzz crate trips an unrelated openssl-sys C build issue but the harness itself is clean. Mirrors the harness shape from ipc_auth_envelope.rs (Archetype 5 structure-aware + Archetype 1 crash detector).

title: [security][follow-up ft-6mmyp] Persist policy-denied MCP mutations to audit_actions table (not just tracing log)
description:
## Context

ft-6mmyp primary fix shipped: mcp_authorize_mcp_mutation now emits structured tracing::warn! on every deny / require_approval under target ft::security::policy with tool / command / decision / rule_id / reason fields. That closes the 'zero observability' gap for denied MCP mutations.

The bead's ideal (fuller) fix was a record_audit_action_redacted write so denied attempts appear in the same audit_actions table as successful ones — enables SQL-queryable forensics and parity with the wa.events_annotate post-mutation audit at mcp_tools.rs:4330-4352.

## Why deferred

record_audit_action_redacted is async. The current sync gate helper at mcp_tools.rs:177-231 can't await. The callers (tx_run/rollback, mission_pause/resume/abort) all do already live inside a runtime.block_on scope, but the helper is invoked BEFORE that block_on — specifically to fail fast without opening a StorageHandle. Opening storage inside the helper on the deny path would:
  - Open a new StorageHandle (~100ms cold path)
  - Require passing db_path (currently the helper only takes &Config)
  - Add a runtime.block_on inside a sync fn that may already be inside a tokio runtime → panic risk

## Fix path

Either:
(a) Push the audit write into the deny branch of each of the 5 caller handlers (they already have runtime.block_on scopes) — duplicates ~10 lines per caller but avoids helper signature changes.
(b) Refactor mcp_authorize_mcp_mutation to return a deny-decision value and have the caller write the audit row plus the error envelope — single point of responsibility per tool.
(c) Change the helper signature to async fn mcp_authorize_mcp_mutation(config, db_path, ...) -> ... and have callers await it inside their existing runtime.block_on.

(b) is cleanest. Roughly:

    enum GateOutcome {
        Allow,
        Deny { envelope: McpResult<Vec<Content>>, audit: AuditActionRecord },
        RequireApproval { envelope: McpResult<Vec<Content>>, audit: AuditActionRecord },
    }
    fn mcp_authorize_mcp_mutation(config, summary, command_text, start) -> GateOutcome

Callers match, write the audit via their existing storage in the deny/approval branches, then return the envelope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After deny/approval, audit_actions has a row with result='denied' or 'require_approval', decision_reason=policy_reason, action_kind matching the tool.
- Integration test per tool: seed a deny-config, call tool, assert audit row shape.
- Tracing log emission (shipped under ft-6mmyp main fix) remains in place as a second signal.

Surfaced by RusticMeadow while landing the ft-6mmyp MVP, 2026-04-23.

title: [BR-RC-ROBOT-CONTRACT] Reality-check Robot Family Closure epic — contract-driven closure of 5 not_implemented families
description:
# Reality-Check Robot Family Closure

Source: docs/reality-check-bridge-plan.md (G2). README support matrix shows 5 robot families returning robot.not_implemented and pointing to ntm: checkpoint, context, work, fleet, profile. Existing epic identifier wa-rsaf is referenced but NOT in the local beads DB.

## Sub-tasks (one per family)
- checkpoint {save, rollback, list}
- context {status, rotate, history}
- work {claim, complete, status, list}
- fleet {status, launch, stop, describe}
- profile {show, list, set}

## Methodology — contract-first, not handler-first
For each family:
1. Write a typed semantic contract (idempotency class, failure semantics, observable side-effect surface, concurrency model) at docs/robot-contracts/<family>.md
2. Build a conformance harness at tests/robot_family_conformance/<family>.rs that:
   - Generates random valid request streams via proptest
   - Asserts idempotency (replay = identical observable result)
   - Asserts atomicity under kill-switch flips
   - Asserts observable-effect bound (only declared events/storage diffs occur)
3. For families with ntm equivalents: differential test asserts zero observable divergence on a 1000-request fuzz corpus
4. THEN implement the handler

## Formal-method depth (round-3)
- TLA+ spec for state-mutating families (checkpoint, work) at docs/specs/robot-<family>.tla
- Stateright in-Rust model checking for `work` claim/release/complete: prove no double-claim, no claim leak, durable completion under crash+restart
- Schema-driven proptest generator: single source-of-truth schema feeds proptest + conformance harness + MCP tool registry

## Why
"Robot mode is supported" is a headline AI-to-AI control plane claim. 5/12 families silently degrading to "shell out to ntm" undermines the narrative. Acceptable as documented stopgap, NOT acceptable as long-term shipping state.

## Acceptance
- All 5 family contracts checked in
- Conformance harness covers all 5; tests pass on every commit
- Differential test passes for families with ntm equivalent
- Zero call sites hit build_ntm_not_implemented_response for these families
- README support matrix shows ✅ for all 5
- Each family has at least one e2e example in README
- Each family's contract attested in release bundle

title: [BR-RC-ROBOT-CONTRACT.0] Schema-driven contract infrastructure (proptest+OpenAPI generator)
description:
# Schema-Driven Contract Infrastructure

Foundation for the 5 family closures: a single source-of-truth schema feeds proptest + conformance harness + MCP tool registry.

## Actions
1. Define a meta-schema for robot-family contracts at `docs/robot-contracts/meta-schema.md` covering:
   - Idempotency class (idempotent/commutative/sequential)
   - Failure semantics (must-not-partially-mutate / can-partially-mutate-with-receipt / fire-and-forget)
   - Observable side-effect surface (events emitted, storage rows mutated, IPC sent)
   - Concurrency model (serializable / per-pane-serial / parallel)
2. Build a Rust schema-DSL crate (or extend existing) such that one declaration produces:
   - Proptest strategies for input generation
   - JSON Schema for the request envelope
   - MCP tool registration metadata
   - Conformance-harness invariants
3. Wire into existing fastmcp seam (mcp_framework.rs)
4. Skeleton harness at `tests/robot_family_conformance/` ready for per-family fillings

## Acceptance
- Meta-schema doc shipped

title: [storage-trait] set_user_version(u32) silently truncates values >= 2^31 — trait sig misrepresents SQLite contract
description:
br-cc_2 surfaced this contract gap while writing property tests for storage_backend_helpers (commit landing under br-ft-l1jgo phase-3 storage proptest sweep).

## Symptom

`StorageBackend::set_user_version(version: u32)` at
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage_backend_trait.rs:120` accepts
the full `u32` range. SQLite's `PRAGMA user_version` is internally
a signed 32-bit integer, so values `>= 2^31` are truncated by
SQLite's storage layer. Concretely:

```
set_user_version(2147483648)         // u32::from(i32::MAX) + 1
pragma_value(&backend, "user_version")  // returns Some("0"), not Some("2147483648")
```

Discovered via the property test `proptest_storage_backend_helpers_pragma_value_round_trips_user_version` — proptest shrunk to exactly `target = 2147483648` and reported `left=0, right=2147483648`.

## Why this matters

Migration code uses `user_version` to track schema version. The codebase currently lives at `SCHEMA_VERSION = 26` (storage/schema_ddl.rs:41), so the truncation isn't a live correctness risk — it's nowhere near 2^31. But the `u32` trait signature actively LIES about the safe input domain: any caller in good faith using `u32::MAX` for sentinel values would silently land at `0` and pass any "did the version land?" gate when they re-read.

## Fix shape

Two clean options:

1. **Narrow the type:** change the trait signature to `set_user_version(version: i32)`. Forces every call site to acknowledge the SQLite range. Breaking change for existing callers — they all pass `u32` today.

2. **Validate the input:** keep the `u32` signature but reject inputs `> i32::MAX as u32` with `BackendError::Other("...")`. Existing callers continue to work; rogue callers get an explicit error instead of silent truncation. Add a doc note pinning the range and the SQLite reason.

Option (2) is the lower-friction path. Recommended.

## Acceptance

- Either the trait signature narrows OR `set_user_version` rejects `>= 2^31`.
- A regression test pins the chosen contract.
- The proptest at `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_storage_backend_helpers.rs::proptest_storage_backend_helpers_pragma_value_round_trips_user_version` can drop its `1u32..=(i32::MAX as u32)` constraint and use the full input domain.

## Cross-references

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage_backend_trait.rs:117-120` (the trait surface).
- `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_storage_backend_helpers.rs::proptest_storage_backend_helpers_pragma_value_round_trips_user_version` (the proptest documenting the truncation, with a docstring noting this bead).
- ft-l1jgo (parent storage migration epic).
close_reason: Implemented StorageBackend user_version SQLite range guard and full-domain proptest; rch targeted proptest passed under /tmp/ft-cod4-target. Broader lib filter currently blocked by unrelated dirty storage.rs pane_id u64->i64 compile error.
