title: redactor.rs: redact_bytes_with_evidence + redact_chunk bytes_replaced is computed against lossy-decoded length, not original byte length
description:
## Site
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:609-626` (`Redactor::redact_bytes_with_evidence`) and `765-778` (`StreamingRedactor::redact_text_with_evidence`).

## Defect
`String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes)` replaces invalid UTF-8 sequences with the Unicode replacement character `U+FFFD`, which is **3 bytes** in UTF-8. Original 2-byte invalid sequence `[0xff, 0xfe]` becomes `\"\\u{FFFD}\\u{FFFD}\"` (6 bytes).

Then:
```rust
let pre_len = lossy.len();
let redacted = self.redact(&lossy);
let post_len = redacted.len();
let bytes_replaced = pre_len.saturating_sub(post_len) as u32;
```

`pre_len` is the LOSSY-DECODED length (post-FFFD-expansion), NOT the original byte length. Operators reading `bytes_replaced` from the evidence think \"X bytes were redacted from the input stream\" but the metric is actually computed against an inflated post-decode length.

For pure-UTF-8 input (the common case) this is fine — pre_len == bytes.len(). For mixed-encoding or binary input the metric overstates redaction work proportional to the number of FFFD substitutions.

## Impact

Cold-tier ingestion's `ColdTierPipelineHealth::record_write` consumes `bytes_replaced` to track \"how aggressive was the redactor on this segment?\". Inflated values from non-UTF-8 input misrepresent the real redaction work — a pane emitting binary noise + occasional secret looks the same in this metric as a pane emitting heavy plaintext secrets.

## Fix shape

### Option A — clamp metric semantics
Document that bytes_replaced is computed in lossy-decoded UTF-8 units, not original bytes. Update field doc-comment on `BytesRedactionEvidence`. Lightest touch.

### Option B — track raw byte length separately
Add `original_bytes: u32` to `BytesRedactionEvidence` (with `#[serde(default)]` for forward-compat). Operators get both numbers and can compute the FFFD-inflation overhead.

### Option C — saturate using bytes.len() not lossy.len()
`bytes_replaced = bytes.len().saturating_sub(post_len) as u32`. Lossless for UTF-8; for binary input, post_len (UTF-8 bytes after redaction) is compared against original byte count — direction is correct but exact value differs.

Option B is cleanest. Option A is the trivial doc fix. Recommended: A immediately, B as follow-up.

## Tests

- Input `b\"plain text\"` → bytes_replaced is 0 (no secrets).
- Input `b\"sk-1234567890abcdef...\"` → bytes_replaced > 0.
- Input `&[0xff, 0xfe]` (invalid UTF-8) → bytes_replaced is 0 but pre_len reports 6 (post-FFFD), exposing the inflation.

## Class
P3 OBS / metric correctness.
close_reason:
Fixed at 15138313f (Option A — clamp metric semantics via doc-fix). BytesRedactionEvidence::bytes_replaced is computed against String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes).len(), which expands invalid UTF-8 sequences into U+FFFD (3 bytes each). Pure-UTF-8 input is unaffected (lossy.len() == bytes.len()); mixed/binary input inflates the metric proportional to FFFD substitutions.

## Doc improvements

- Field docstring on BytesRedactionEvidence::bytes_replaced: full operator-interpretation contract including the unaffected pure-UTF-8 case, the inflation source for mixed/binary input, and the deferred-runtime-fix paragraph (option B field bump or option C bytes.len() compare).
- Inline comment at Redactor::redact_bytes_with_evidence (redactor.rs:660): pins the lossy-decoded semantic at the source so future readers don't miss it.
- Inline comment at StreamingRedactor::redact_text_with_evidence: pins the streaming-path inheritance from redact_chunk's from_utf8_lossy → self.pending.push_str pipeline.

## Why Option A (not B or C)

A is the strict subset that fixes the operator-facing contract without touching the wire format. B requires a schema bump + cold-tier integration update + audit-table column add. C changes binary-input semantics in a direction-correct but value-different way that would surprise dashboards built against existing behavior. A doesn't block B or C from landing later; the bead's recommendation is exactly 'A immediately, B as follow-up.'

## Tests

No code change → no new tests required. Pre-existing tests at redactor.rs:992-1066 (6 redact_bytes_with_evidence_* unit tests, including the dedicated _handles_invalid_utf8_lossy case) continue to assert the runtime contract.

## Defect-family closure

Three counter-naming/semantic-drift doc-pin closures via Option C analog: ft-lb5x7 (subscriber_lag_events three-source enumeration) + ft-e3wwx (events_dropped_dedup FPR conflation) + ft-r24qu (bytes_replaced lossy-decoded semantic). Plus the audit-trail bead ft-jydne also closed via Option C analog.

Verification: cargo check --lib -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features clean (193 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors). Doc-only diff; runtime behavior unchanged.

title: [review][HIGH] ft-4o5mb.1 wa.state harness expects tool-level FT-MCP-0001 but framework rejects at schema — test will fail when run
description:
commit 4e270e95 added crates/frankenterm-core/tests/wa_state_mcp_conformance.rs. Commit subject explicitly states 'verification partial - rch lane timed out after 45min'. Audit by inspection reveals a logic error that will make the test fail on first actual run.

## The bug

Test at :395-401 sends invalid args:

    json!({
        "agent": 7,
        "format": "json"
    })

Test's assertion at :274-288 expects tool-level FT-MCP-0001:

    fn assert_invalid_args_response(response: &Value) {
        assert_eq!(response["kind"], "tool_envelope");  // LINE 275
        ...
        assert_invalid_args_envelope_shape(&payload);      // asserts error_code == 'FT-MCP-0001'
    }

But fastmcp-server/src/router.rs:837 calls schema::validate() BEFORE dispatching to the tool handler, and fastmcp-protocol/src/schema.rs:211 emits 'expected type string, got integer' for type mismatches. For wa.state with {"agent": 7}, the framework will reject at schema validation with McpError::invalid_params('Input validation failed: root.agent: expected type string, got integer').

parse_invalid_args_response at :209-224 maps framework errors to {"kind": "framework_error", ...}, so response["kind"] becomes "framework_error" — the assert_eq! at :275 FAILS, test panics.

## Confirmed via

1. /dp/fastmcp_rust/crates/fastmcp-server/src/router.rs:833-849 — schema validation runs BEFORE tool dispatch.
2. /dp/fastmcp_rust/crates/fastmcp-protocol/src/schema.rs:211 — type-mismatch path emits 'expected type X, got Y'.
3. ecae6caa precedent: the mcp_conformance_core_tools.rs harness MIGRATED AWAY from type-mismatch invalid-args payloads (old: 'query': 42; new: 'limit': 0). The migration happened specifically because type-mismatch now hits framework rejection. The 4e270e95 author pattern-matched the OLD shape of ecae6caa, not the current version.
4. For wa.state specifically: all 3 schema fields (domain, agent, pane_id) are tightly typed. additionalProperties:false closes the unknown-key slip. There is NO payload that passes framework validation but fails tool-level serde for this tool — the MCP_ERR_INVALID_ARGS branch at mcp_tools.rs:912-923 is DEAD CODE for wa.state (related to wa-nu4.3.9.19).

## Concrete fix

Replace assert_invalid_args_response with a framework-level check (mirroring ecae6caa's assert_framework_invalid_params_response):

    fn assert_framework_invalid_args_response(response: &Value) {
        assert_eq!(response["kind"], "framework_error");
        assert_eq!(response["code"], "InvalidParams");
        assert!(response["message"].as_str().is_some_and(|m| m.contains("root.agent") && m.contains("expected type")));
        assert!(response["data"].is_null());
    }

Keep the invalid_args_response payload as {"agent": 7, ...} — this does trigger framework rejection, which is what we test. No golden regeneration needed if assert_matches_golden is still called (the golden content changes but ToolGoldenCapture structure stays the same).

Alternatively use boundary-violation payload {"pane_id": -1} (violates minimum:0) — cleaner intent-reveal.

## Severity

HIGH because:
- Test fails deterministically on first real run (not a flake).
- Blocks the test suite for any agent running wa_state_mcp_conformance.
- Lands during release readiness epic — a broken conformance test is a ship blocker.
- Commit subject admits 'verification partial'; this is exactly the risk that caveat was flagging.

Discovered during reviewer audit round 12, 2026-04-23. Tag: review, mcp, conformance, test-logic-error.
close_reason: Fixed in 4865b1b7: wa.state harness now expects framework InvalidParams for schema-rejected invalid args and ships the matching wa_state golden.

title: workflow cancellation leaves mid-wait execution resumable
description: Cancellation during workflow retry backoff, WaitFor pauses, or SendText verification waits returns WorkflowExecutionResult::Aborted after recording only a terminal action. It does not mark the persisted execution failed or mark the trigger event handled, so the DB can keep the workflow in running/waiting state and restart recovery can resume or replay a canceled workflow, including duplicate SendText side effects.

title: PaneWorkflowLockManager: no telemetry counters — force_release abuse + runaway-recovery rate invisible to doctor
description:
Quality review of workflows/lock.rs surfaced an operational gap: PaneWorkflowLockManager has zero telemetry. Operators cannot see:

1. How often force_release fires (recovery path or abuse signal)
2. How often try_acquire_with_limit hits the concurrency cap
3. Total acquisitions / releases lifetime counters
4. Mutex poisoned-recovery occurrences (currently silently swallowed via unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()))

force_release in particular is documented 'use with caution' but there's no observable signal when it fires repeatedly. A buggy or malicious code path could force-release every workflow lock and only emit warn-level traces.

Fix: add LockManagerTelemetry inner struct + atomic counters + health() snapshot accessor for doctor surface. Additive, non-breaking, doesn't conflict with the in-flight ft-haa2b RAII-migration.
close_reason: PaneWorkflowLockManager now ships LockManagerHealth telemetry surface with 7 counters + is_safe() predicate (mutex poisoning OR >5% force-release rate = unsafe). Wired into try_acquire/release/force_release call sites. +9 tests, 45 total pass.

Continuation of ft-t9a6q.1.

ft-t9a6q.1 shipped a syn-based stable-Rust analyzer at lints/cx_propagation/ with 23 tests on the rule shape. This follow-up migrates the analyzer to a real cargo-dylint LateLintPass plugin so the lint runs at compile time.

## Scope
1. Add a [lib] crate-type=["cdylib"] target alongside the existing lib in lints/cx_propagation/.
2. Pin nightly toolchain via lints/cx_propagation/rust-toolchain.toml (matches dylint's host requirement).
3. Implement cx_propagation_lint::dylint_plugin::LateLintPassImpl using clippy_utils + rustc_lint.
4. Walk hir::Item::Fn with sig.header.asyncness == Async; check parameter types via TyKind::Ref / TyKind::Path; check generic bounds.
5. Reuse the existing allow_list.rs module — same EXEMPT_FILES + WRAPPER_EXEMPTIONS lists.
6. Smoke-test against the real frankenterm-core src via cargo dylint.

## Acceptance
- Plugin builds + loads via cargo dylint.
- Same finding count against frankenterm-core/src as the syn analyzer.
- rust-toolchain.toml documented in docs/runtime/cx-propagation-lint.md.

## Cross-references

title: session_restore + snapshot_engine open_conn helpers omit foreign_keys PRAGMA — cleanup paths leak orphan rows
description:
ft-s4myu fixed StorageHandle::with_config to enable foreign_keys on every connection open. But two OTHER SQLite writers in frankenterm-core have their own open_conn helpers that set journal_mode and busy_timeout but skip foreign_keys:

  - crates/frankenterm-core/src/session_restore.rs:254 — used by delete_session, load_checkpoint_by_id, list_sessions, show_session, session_doctor, and 5+ other production paths.
  - crates/frankenterm-core/src/snapshot_engine.rs:1293 — used by cleanup_sync which does 'DELETE FROM session_checkpoints WHERE checkpoint_at < ?1' and 'DELETE FROM session_checkpoints WHERE id IN (...)'. The mux_pane_state → session_checkpoints FK with ON DELETE CASCADE at schema line 646 is supposed to cascade the child deletion. With FKs OFF, cleanup silently leaves orphan mux_pane_state rows.

Fix: add 'PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON' to both open_conn helpers. Regression test: run snapshot_engine::cleanup against a populated DB, assert no orphaned mux_pane_state rows remain.

Scope: same shape as ft-s4myu (compare session_retention.rs:287 which correctly issues the pragma).
close_reason: done

title: Migrate wezterm-client and frankenterm-mux-server-impl from direct smol to asupersync
description: Both crates have direct smol::Async<T>, smol::channel, smol::future::or, and async_io::IoSafe usage that needs asupersync equivalents. Key challenge: smol::Async<T> wraps blocking FDs with reactor - asupersync uses capability-based IoCap model instead. Needs design work for the I/O wrapping layer. Blocked by: understanding asupersync IoCap API and creating an Async<T>-like adapter.
close_reason: Completed direct Smol removal in wezterm-client and frankenterm-mux-server-impl; remaining debt tracked in ft-xbnl0.2.1 verification finish-line work

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: TopazHarbor research: asupersync uses IoRegistration (per-type, not generic Async<T>). TcpStream/UnixStream each embed Option<IoRegistration> directly. To build generic Async<T>: wrap T:AsRawFd + IoRegistration + implement AsyncRead/AsyncWrite with rearm pattern. Alternative: add feature-gated conditional compilation (async-smol vs async-asupersync) like SSH crate, keeping smol path until native mux replaces these legacy crates.

comments.author: OliveDesert
comments.text:
Code-grounded execution split after validating current sources and Asupersync primitives on 2026-04-03.

What the code says now
- `frankenterm/client` and `crates/frankenterm-mux-server-impl` are the direct Smol entrypoints.
- Support crates already partially know about native Asupersync:
  - `codec` defaults to `async-asupersync` and only stays on Smol when callers force `async-smol`.
  - `frankenterm-ssh` defaults to `async-asupersync` and already exposes a runtime shim (`runtime::block_on`, channel/io reexports).
  - `frankenterm-uds` and `async_ossl` default to `async-asupersync`, but today they only expose blocking `Read`/`Write` wrappers plus optional `async_io::IoSafe`.
- The hard blockers are therefore not abstract runtime folklore; they are concrete call sites and wrapper gaps:
  1. local Unix / mux-server dispatch path
  2. SSH proxy / pipe path
  3. TLS/OpenSSL path

Important design correction
- The first idea in this bead description about creating an Async<T>-like generic adapter should NOT be the default architecture.
- Asupersync's native pattern is per-type `Option<IoRegistration>` plus `rearm(...)` on `WouldBlock`, as seen in its own `net::unix::UnixStream` and `process` pipe wrappers.
- The finish-line-safe approach is: use concrete per-type native adapters where the project owns the type, and only fall back to a narrow local adapter when there is no better owned boundary.

Recommended implementation slicing
1. Local Unix + mux-server dispatch first.
   files: `frankenterm/uds/src/lib.rs`, `crates/frankenterm-mux-server-impl/src/dispatch.rs`, `frankenterm/client/src/client.rs`, relevant `Cargo.toml` files.
   plan: add native Asupersync `AsyncRead`/`AsyncWrite` + readiness registration to `frankenterm-uds::UnixStream`; stop forcing `codec`/`uds`/`async_ossl` into Smol mode from client and mux-server manifests; replace `smol::Async` + `smol::channel` + `smol::future::or` in dispatch and the local client path with native Asupersync-shaped loops.

2. SSH proxy / pipe path second.
   files: `frankenterm/client/src/client.rs`, possibly `frankenterm/ssh/*` only if needed.
   plan: remove direct `smol::block_on` in favor of the SSH runtime shim immediately; then decide whether `SshStream` should gain a small local Asupersync pipe-registration adapter or reuse an existing process-pipe pattern from Asupersync. This path is not the same problem as Unix sockets and should not be conflated with them.

3. TLS/OpenSSL path third, coordinated with finish-line networking work.
   files: `frankenterm/client/src/client.rs`, `frankenterm/async_ossl/src/lib.rs`.
   plan: either give `AsyncSslStream` a native Asupersync readiness wrapper using the same `IoRegistration`/`WouldBlock` pattern, or deliberately hand this slice to the broader native-network/TLS lane if the correct answer is to stop using this wrapper entirely. Do not hide TLS behind another executor-neutral shim.

Immediate low-risk cleanup opportunities once the first slice starts
- direct `smol::block_on(sess.exec(...))` in `client.rs` should route through `frankenterm-ssh`'s runtime shim rather than calling Smol directly.
- `smol::Timer::after(...)` in `client.rs` should move to a native timer path (`asupersync::time` or a repo-local native shim) rather than survive as a stray holdout.

This bead should now be read as: concrete per-transport native cutover, not "invent a new generic Async<T> compatibility layer".

title: [ARCH] integrate PhiAccrualFailureDetector into headless_mux_server::check_peer_health (br-ft-nll8a follow-up)
description:
[ARCH] integrate PhiAccrualFailureDetector into headless_mux_server::check_peer_health (br-ft-nll8a follow-up)

Substrate ft-nll8a shipped the φ-accrual failure detector as crate::phi_accrual_failure_detector. This bead tracks the production-side migration from the current hard-threshold timeout to the adaptive accrual approach.

Current code (crates/frankenterm-core/src/headless_mux_server.rs:518):
```rust
pub fn check_peer_health(&mut self) {
    let now = epoch_ms();
    let timeout = self.config.peer_timeout_ms;
    for peer in self.peers.values_mut() {
        if peer.status == PeerStatus::Connected
            && now.saturating_sub(peer.last_heartbeat_at) > timeout
        {
            peer.status = PeerStatus::Unreachable;
        }
    }
}
```

Migration shape:
1. Add `failure_detector: PhiAccrualFailureDetector` field to PeerInfo (struct at line 68).
2. On heartbeat receipt (locate sites: search for assignments to `peer.last_heartbeat_at`), call `peer.failure_detector.record_heartbeat(now_micros)`.
3. In check_peer_health, replace the hard threshold check with:
   `peer.failure_detector.is_unreachable(now_micros, self.config.suspicion_threshold)`
4. Add `suspicion_threshold: f64` to ServerConfig (default DEFAULT_SUSPICION_THRESHOLD = 8.0).
5. Update tests that exercise check_peer_health to drive heartbeats through record_heartbeat first.

Rollback: keep peer_timeout_ms field for one release as fallback; gate on suspicion_threshold being Some.

Acceptance:
- check_peer_health uses PhiAccrualFailureDetector::is_unreachable.
- Regression test confirms a peer with steady-state 1s heartbeats followed by 30s silence transitions to Unreachable.
- Regression test confirms a peer with high-variance heartbeats (1s±500ms jitter) does NOT flip Unreachable on a single 5s gap (false-positive rate down).
- All ServerConfig defaults documented; default threshold matches Akka/Cassandra (8.0).

Why P3:
- Substrate is shipped; this is integration only.
- Current hard-threshold behavior is functionally correct for the common case; this improves correctness in variance-prone topologies.
- No active SEC or correctness incident; soft win.

Cross-references:
- Substrate: ft-nll8a (closed in same commit).
- Substrate code: crates/frankenterm-core/src/phi_accrual_failure_detector.rs.
- Production callsite: crates/frankenterm-core/src/headless_mux_server.rs:518 (check_peer_health).
- Heartbeat-receipt sites to wire (TBD by integrator): grep `last_heartbeat_at` in headless_mux_server.rs and any RemoteRequest handler.
notes: Shipped this commit. PhiAccrualFailureDetector wired into PeerInfo (#[serde(skip)] field) + ServerConfig (suspicion_threshold f64, default 8.0). check_peer_health now uses peer.failure_detector.is_unreachable(now_micros, threshold) instead of fixed timeout vs elapsed. Heartbeat handler + JoinFederation handler call record_heartbeat. Legacy peer_timeout_ms field retained for serde back-compat but no longer consulted. Regression test check_peer_health_phi_accrual_tolerates_variance_ft_roacq drives 200 bursty heartbeats (alternating 0.5s/2s) and confirms 5s gap does NOT flip Unreachable (suspicion < 8.0). Existing check_peer_health_marks_timeout test preserved by seeding detector with one heartbeat at last_heartbeat_at = 0 — saturated suspicion still trips threshold. server_config_serde + server_config_roundtrip tests updated to include suspicion_threshold field. cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features clean in 22s.

title: [reality-gap] README tx examples target a top-level CLI that the shipped ft binary does not expose
description:
README.md documents top-level `ft tx ...` commands in the command matrix and troubleshooting examples, but the shipped binary at `FrankenTerm.app/Contents/MacOS/ft` rejects `ft tx --help` with `error: unrecognized subcommand 'tx'`.

Observed reality:
- `./FrankenTerm.app/Contents/MacOS/ft --help` has no top-level `tx` command.
- `./FrankenTerm.app/Contents/MacOS/ft robot --help` advertises `tx plan|run|rollback|show` under robot mode.
- `./FrankenTerm.app/Contents/MacOS/ft mission plan --contract mission.json` also fails because the live flag is `--mission-file`, not `--contract`.

Impact: an operator following README examples gets an immediate parse failure from the shipped binary.

Expected fix:
- Update README tx examples to the live robot surface (`ft robot tx ...`).
- Use the live flag spelling (`--contract-file`) where a contract path example is shown.
- If a top-level human tx surface is intended, ship it and re-verify the binary before documenting it.
close_reason:
AS-VERIFIED, no README edit needed. The bead's two concrete gaps were already closed by commit 3b9838ce (docs(readme): correct tx and config examples, same-day):

(1) bare 'ft tx ...' → 'ft robot tx ...' at README:158 (Quick Example tx run), :161 (tx show), :225 (Safety Guarantees bullet), :1230 (FAQ section). Current grep for bare 'ft tx ' matches zero lines.

(2) '--contract' → '--contract-file' at the matching lines. Current grep for '--contract' (not '--contract-file') matches zero lines. Cross-checked against the clap wiring: RobotTxCommands::Plan/Run at crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs:3173-3184 bind '#[arg(long)] contract_file', matching the README.

Note on bead context: the bead cited './FrankenTerm.app/Contents/MacOS/ft --help' showing no top-level 'tx' subcommand, but the live source at main.rs:430-443 actually defines a top-level 'Tx { command: TxCommands }' variant — that app bundle was stale. title: [SEV] CommandBuilder env_map_serde silently collides duplicate keys after to_string_lossy
description: frankenterm/pty/src/cmdbuilder.rs env_map_serde (added in 803356bf) maps BTreeMap<OsString, EnvEntry> -> JSON via OsString::to_string_lossy for keys. Two distinct OsString keys whose non-UTF-8 bytes differ but collapse to the same String under lossy conversion will (1) produce a JSON map containing duplicate keys during serialize (most JSON parsers keep last, silently dropping one entry), and (2) on deserialize the BTreeMap::insert loop overwrites on collision, again silently dropping entries without returning an error. The adapter offers no detection or rejection of this case — a corrupted env set roundtrips to a smaller env set with no diagnostic. Metamorphic property: |deserialize(serialize(m))| == |m| — currently violated for any m with keys that collide under to_string_lossy. Conformance concern: the commit message asserts 'POSIX env names are ASCII-only' but setenv(3) on Linux accepts non-ASCII bytes (LC_*=ja_JP.UTF-8 etc.), and libc-level execve passes raw bytes. Fix by either (a) erroring on lossy conversion in both directions, or (b) serializing as an array of [key_bytes, value] pairs via serde_bytes / base64 so the roundtrip is lossless. At minimum add a proptest that asserts roundtrip preserves map size when two synthesized OsString keys share a lossy-equivalent representation.
close_reason: Fixed in 7a452b96: replaced map adapter with sequence-of-pairs adapter so every distinct OsString key survives serde roundtrip losslessly (via OsString's native byte/UTF-16-preserving enum encoding in value position). Added 2 regression proptests: one generates arbitrary byte keys (many non-UTF-8) and asserts all distinct keys roundtrip with paired values intact; the other injects two different invalid-UTF-8 sequences that both lossy-render to U+FFFD and asserts both survive. Test-binary run is blocked by pane6-target lock contention; fix is structurally complete and compiles clean at my previous build pass.

title: [ft-q4udk follow-up] PooledReadConn lacks hit-rate counter; add for regression-test verifiability
description:
ft-q4udk acceptance criterion #3 asked for a regression test that 'asserts the pool's hit-rate stays > 80% after migration.' That requires PooledReadConn to expose hit-rate telemetry. Today the pool has no per-acquire hit/miss counters — only the silent LIFO recycle path.

## Substrate gap

`PooledReadConn::acquire` (storage.rs:8485) takes the recycled connection from the LIFO if present, else opens a fresh one. The branch is taken silently — no AtomicU64 counter increments, no tracing event, no exposed metric.

## Fix shape

Add to PooledReadConn module:
- `static POOL_HITS: AtomicU64` (or per-db_path map) bumped when `recycled` is Some.
- `static POOL_MISSES: AtomicU64` bumped when fallthrough to `open_read_storage_conn`.
- `pub fn pool_telemetry_snapshot() -> (u64, u64)` for tests + diagnostics.
- New regression test in tests/storage_pool_regression.rs: spawn N concurrent reader tasks against same db, assert hits/(hits+misses) > 0.80 after migration.

## Why follow-up not blocker

The structural regression ft-q4udk identified is FIXED by ft-3twzm (61ce1883a) + ft-ir23j (47b1b9cd8). Hit-rate counters are a verification mechanism, not a fix. Filing as P3 because the underlying pool contract is already restored.

Cross-refs: ft-q4udk (parent), ft-3twzm + ft-ir23j (the actual fixes), ft-bhyxz (original pool substrate).

title: headless_mux_server: JoinFederation has no peer-count cap (unbounded DoS) + clobbers first_seen_at on rejoin
description:
crates/frankenterm-core/src/headless_mux_server.rs:402-416 RemoteRequest::JoinFederation blindly inserts into self.peers without checking a cap, and overwrites the existing PeerInfo entirely on every re-join — losing first_seen_at. Two distinct defects:

1. **Unbounded peer-map growth (DoS)**: ServerConfig has max_connections (for clients) and max_panes, but NO max_peers. A hostile or buggy counterparty spamming JoinFederation with distinct node_ids grows self.peers without bound, eventually OOM'ing the mux server. prune_unreachable_peers only fires after peer_timeout_ms + an external caller — a burst of N spurious JoinFederation requests can bloat the map before any prune runs. Parallel shape to ft-kfy99 (tmux_cc line cap), ft-phz7x (codec oversize tagged_len), ft-8ihuz (scrollback unbounded read).

2. **first_seen_at lost on rejoin**: Every JoinFederation fully replaces PeerInfo at line 404-414, including setting first_seen_at to epoch_ms(). A peer that legitimately rejoins (e.g. partition heal after the Heartbeat ft-lekgj path tells it to re-JoinFederation) loses its original first_seen_at — making 'how long has this peer been federated' observability lie.

Fix: add max_peers: u32 to ServerConfig (default 512, twice max_connections as headroom). In JoinFederation, if the node_id is NEW and self.peers.len() >= max_peers, return RemoteResponse::Error { code: "peer_registry_full" }. If the node_id already exists, preserve first_seen_at from the existing entry and only update the re-join-time fields (node, status, last_heartbeat_at, capabilities). Regression tests: (a) 512-peer cap rejects the 513th distinct JoinFederation with peer_registry_full; (b) a rejoin keeps first_seen_at of the original insert.
close_reason: Landed in 78721403 (fix(headless_mux_server): cap JoinFederation peer registry + preserve first_seen_at on rejoin). Added ServerConfig.max_peers (default 512) + JoinFederation rejects new peers past cap with peer_registry_full; re-joins of known node_ids still succeed (they don't consume a slot). Also preserves existing first_seen_at on rejoin. Two regression tests pin both contracts. Verification blocked by pre-existing frankenterm-core build blockers (ft-kqidb/uigpj/s2u51/zv3u9).

title: [audit] chaos.rs: NaN probability silently disables fault, unbounded delay_ms DoS, probability=1.0 has 1/2^32 false-negative
description:
Audit findings in crates/frankenterm-core/src/chaos.rs:

(A) NaN probability silently disables fault injection. FaultMode::fail_with_probability calls .clamp(0.0, 1.0) which propagates NaN unchanged. Then 'if rand_val < probability' with NaN probability is always false — tester thinks they configured fault injection but no faults fire. Detection masquerade. Fix: sanitize NaN to 0.0 in the builder + the constructor.

(B) Unbounded delay_ms in FaultMode::Delay / DelayThenFail. delay_ms: u64 → std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(u64::MAX)) freezes the worker thread for ~584M years. Effective DoS via fault config; trivially set via set_fault. Cap at sane bound (e.g., 300_000ms = 5min) — fault injection legitimately needs delays measured in seconds, not hours.

(C) FaultMode::FailWithProbability uses 'rand_val < probability' strict inequality. With probability=1.0 and rand_val=1.0 (occurs when hash >> 32 == u32::MAX, ~1/2^32 of the time), the fault does NOT fire. Subtle false-negative when tester uses FailWithProbability(1.0) instead of AlwaysFail. Fix: special-case probability>=1.0 → always fail.
close_reason: All 3 findings landed in d06ef64d1. NaN probability sanitization (sanitize_probability) + delay_ms cap (MAX_DELAY_MS = 5min) + probability=1.0 short-circuit. Builder + evaluator both apply guards (defense against struct-init bypass). 7 regression tests added; all 62 chaos lib tests green.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.4.4.cont] Status-bar GUI integration — StatusTile trait + 8 built-in tiles + refresh scheduler + plugin loader + AT-tree announcements
description:
# Continuation: status-bar GUI integration

## Context
ft-mpc9b.4.4 retired at substrate scope (commit 5019aabbb):
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/status_bar.rs ships TileAlignment + TileSpec + RenderedTile + validate_tile_specs (3 invariants) + layout_status_bar engine (overflow/underflow + priority-truncation + 3-alignment packing + deterministic id tie-break) + LaidOutBar + hit_test.
- 27 inline tests passing including 8 built-in tiles default config + narrow-bar truncation + full pipeline.

## What this bead carries

### StatusTile trait + WIT bindings
- New `frankenterm-gui/src/status_bar/mod.rs`:
  - `pub trait StatusTile: Send + Sync` with the bead's API: `render(&self, ctx) -> RenderedTile`, `on_click(&mut self, x_in_tile) -> Option<TileAction>`, `on_hover(&self, x_in_tile) -> Option<String>`, `min_width / max_width / priority / accessibility_label`.
  - WIT plugin bindings (cross-link ft-mpc9b.4.3 WASM plugin system) so plugin tiles implement the same trait via wasmtime.
- The trait's `min_width / max_width / priority / accessibility_label` getters drive `TileSpec` construction at registration time.

### 8 built-in tiles
1. **ft.mode** — Normal / Copy / Visual indicator. OnEvent refresh.
2. **ft.session** — Active session name. OnEvent refresh.
3. **ft.panes** — Pane count + active-pane indicator (e.g. "3/8"). OnEvent refresh.
4. **ft.agents** — Agent state breakdown (cc/cod/gmi green/yellow/red counts). EveryMs(250) refresh.
5. **ft.fleet_memory** — Fleet memory tier (Normal / Elevated / Critical / Emergency). EveryMs(1000) refresh.
6. **ft.cost** — Per-agent / per-session cost meter. EveryMs(5000) refresh.
7. **ft.network** — PTY bytes/sec aggregate. EveryMs(1000) refresh.
8. **ft.clock** — Local + UTC. EveryMs(1000) refresh.

### Refresh scheduler
- The gui's tick loop maintains a `LastRendered { tile_id, last_render_at }` map.
- Per-tile: if `now - last_render_at >= TileRefreshHint::EveryMs`, re-render and update.
- OnEvent tiles: re-render only when an explicit signal fires (e.g. mode change, session rename).
- Layout recomputed on any change to (specs, renders, bar_width).

### Layout caching
- Cache `LaidOutBar` per (specs, renders, bar_width) hash.
- Invalidate when any tile's RenderedTile changes or bar_width changes.
- Hot-path optimisation: hash_cell_grid-style FNV-1a over the layout inputs.

### Painter integration
- After layout, walk `LaidOutBar.placements` left-to-right and render each tile at `x_start..x_start + width`.
- Tile content lives in a row of `Cell` records; status bar occupies one row at the bottom of the window.

### Mouse handler
- Mouse-move over status bar: `bar.hit_test(x)` → if `Some(hit)`, call `tile.on_hover(hit.x_in_tile)` for tooltip.
- Mouse-click: `tile.on_click(hit.x_in_tile)` → `Option<TileAction>` (e.g. ToggleMode, OpenAgentList, ShowCostBreakdown).

### A11y / screen-reader integration
- On tile render-content change: post `accessibility_label` via NSAccessibility / AT-SPI.
- Cross-link a11y_tree.rs / ft-mpc9b.10.

### frankenterm.toml config
- `[[status_bar.tile]]` array: id, alignment, min_width, max_width, priority, source = "builtin:ft.mode" | "plugin:cost".
- Operator can rearrange / hide tiles by editing config (no rebuild).

### Plugin discovery
- Plugin tiles loaded from `~/.config/ft/plugins/*.wasm` via wasmtime.
- Cross-link ft-mpc9b.4.3.

### docs
- Author docs/status-bar/truncation-rules.md per the bead.

## Acceptance per the original bead
- 8 built-in tiles shipped + plugin trait surface
- Truncation rules documented + deterministic
- A11y labels mandatory; screen-reader announces tile content changes
- Operator config in frankenterm.toml

## Cross-references
- Substrate: commit 5019aabbb (status_bar.rs, 27 tests)
- Compositor: ft-mpc9b.4.1 / ft-hk8f2 (status bar lives in Layer 3 = StatusTiles)
- WASM plugin system: ft-mpc9b.4.3
- A11y: ft-mpc9b.10 cross-cutting epic
- Truncation spec doc: docs/status-bar/truncation-rules.md

title: retry::RetryPolicy::delay_for_attempt panics on NaN backoff_factor or jitter_percent (no fail-closed)
description: RetryPolicy::delay_for_attempt computes base_ms = initial_ms as f64 * backoff_factor.powi(exp); then jitter_range = base_ms * jitter_percent; then rng.random_range(-jitter_range..=jitter_range). If backoff_factor or jitter_percent is NaN (from a malformed config, a fuzz harness, or a direct struct-literal construction bypassing new()), base_ms / jitter_range become NaN, and rng.random_range(NaN..=NaN) panics. Matches the fail-closed pattern already applied to disk_pressure (ft-761tz), continuous_backpressure (ft-yskcu), telemetry::Histogram (ft-b4l62). Fix: sanitize backoff_factor and jitter_percent inside delay_for_attempt — if either is not finite or out-of-range, substitute a safe default and return a non-NaN delay. Add proptest: any RetryPolicy with any f64 in backoff_factor/jitter_percent must produce a finite, non-panicking Duration for any attempt in 0..=63.
close_reason: done

title: storage: foreign_keys PRAGMA not applied on connection open for up-to-date DBs — CASCADE deletes silently skip
close_reason: Withdrawn — premise was wrong. The bundled SQLite that libsqlite3-sys builds compiles with `-DSQLITE_DEFAULT_FOREIGN_KEYS=1` (libsqlite3-sys-0.36.0/build.rs:127), so every rusqlite Connection::open starts with foreign_keys=1 by default. Empirically confirmed by running the reopen test: conn2 had PRAGMA foreign_keys returning 1 (not 0). The PRAGMA statement inside SCHEMA_SQL is redundant-not-missing. CASCADE deletes DO fire on fresh connections even when initialize_schema short-circuits. Reverted the uncommitted storage.rs edit. Note: if frankenterm ever switched to non-bundled SQLite or moved off libsqlite3-sys, this defense would be needed — but under the current Cargo.toml ('rusqlite = { features = ["bundled", ...] }' at Cargo.toml:246) there is no live defect.

title: [testing-fuzzing] pin match_rule_glob invariants under proptest (empty patterns, star-wildcards, length preservation)
description:
# Gap

events.rs:1121 `pub fn match_rule_glob(pattern, value) -> bool` —
a hand-rolled glob matcher with `*` (any sequence) and `?` (any
single char) support. 19 inline example tests at events.rs:2827+ cover
specific cases. No proptest / property-based coverage exists.

# Risk

Hand-rolled glob matchers are classic defect surfaces — backtrack
state machines have edge cases that example tests routinely miss:

1. Empty-pattern vs empty-value semantics (false positives here
   would break exclude rules)
2. Pattern of N `?`s must match exactly N-char values (length-
   preservation invariant that's easy to regress with an off-by-one)
3. `"*"` alone must match every value (including empty) — this is
   the "allow-everything" escape hatch operators rely on
4. Exact patterns (no wildcards) must be length-preserving: only
   match same-length values with same bytes
5. Idempotence: `match_rule_glob(x, x) == true` for any exact pattern x

# Fix

New proptest suite in events.rs test module with 5 invariant properties,
each bearing the domain check the hand-rolled state machine is supposed
to guarantee. Runs under the existing module's test harness — no new
test file or feature-gate.

# Catches

- Backtrack-reset off-by-one at events.rs:1144 (p_star assignment
  wrong-side) would fail invariant #1/#3
- Wildcard-in-early-exit regression at :1122 would fail #4
- Star-at-end (`"a*"`) improperly requiring trailing chars would
  fail #3 on pattern="a??" value="abc"

Shipping as a net-positive guard, not a known-bug fix.
close_reason: Landed in f3e3f68c (test(events): add proptest coverage for match_rule_glob invariants). Pinned 5 properties covering exact-pattern self-match, star-matches-everything, N-questions length preservation, empty-pattern empty-value only, and reflexivity over wildcard-free values. Verified: 8 passed / 0 failed (5 proptests × default cases + 3 example tests) on cargo test --lib --features asupersync-runtime match_rule_glob, 0.09s. EXIT=0.

title: [review][LOW] release.yml SLSA attestation covers binary archives but not SHA256SUMS manifest
description:
release.yml:147-149 subject-path covers dist/*.tar.xz and dist/*.zip — the binary archives attested by actions/attest@v4 (SLSA build provenance). Not covered: SHA256SUMS combined manifest (created at :137-138 as `cat *.sha256 > SHA256SUMS`) and individual .sha256 sidecar files.

Scenario: release uploads dist/* so downloaders get both ft-linux-amd64.tar.xz + SHA256SUMS. A verifier who trusts SHA256SUMS to key the right .tar.xz and only attests the .tar.xz, never re-checksums. An attacker who compromised the release step (not the attestation step) could re-write SHA256SUMS to misname the manifest entries without breaking the .tar.xz attestation signature.

Practical impact: minimal for verifiers who use gh attestation verify on the .tar.xz directly. But users following the 'download SHA256SUMS, verify, then download binary' pattern get no provenance coverage on the manifest they trust.

Fix: extend subject-path to include SHA256SUMS (and possibly *.sha256 sidecars). Minor YAML edit:

    subject-path: |
      dist/*.tar.xz
      dist/*.zip
      dist/SHA256SUMS

Severity: LOW. Audit round 6. Verifying 325054be.
close_reason: Fixed in 9ed9c7c6: release.yml attest step subject-path extended from {dist/*.tar.xz, dist/*.zip} to also cover dist/*.sha256 (per-archive sidecars) and dist/SHA256SUMS (combined manifest). Closes the attacker-compromises-release-but-not-signing-key scenario where a rewritten SHA256SUMS could re-point verifiers to a different archive with an original valid attestation. Comment added documenting the rationale.

title: [fuzzing] ft CLI argv parser (clap-based): no fuzz target despite being the AI-to-AI control surface
description:
## Attack surface

`crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs` defines the entire `ft` CLI via
clap (Parser/Subcommand derives at line 72 onward). It is the
principal control surface AI agents use to drive other AI agents
through `ft robot ...`, plus the human entry point.

When an agent runs `ft robot send <pane> "<text>"`, the `<text>`
is attacker-controlled (another agent's output passed as command
input). When `ntm` or operator scripts invoke `ft` with constructed
argv, the argv contents are similarly under indirect attacker
control.

Existing fuzz coverage: zero. `grep -lE "argv|Cli::try_parse|clap"
fuzz/fuzz_targets/*.rs` returns no hits.

## Why fuzzing finds real defects here

clap is generally robust, but the SHIM layer between argv parsing
and the command-dispatch body is not. Concrete risks:

- **Panic in subcommand argument validation** — every `--flag value`
  is parsed by clap's value parser; custom value parsers (e.g.,
  `parse_pct_arg` in tests, `parse_severity_override` in main.rs)
  may panic on malformed input rather than returning Err.
- **OOM via argument repetition** — `clap::Arg::action(Append)` with
  no upper bound lets `--include` be repeated 1M times; downstream
  collection in `Vec` allocates unbounded.
- **String parsing overflow** — `--timeout-secs 99999999999999999`
  parses through `u64::from_str` but downstream `Duration::from_secs`
  may saturate or overflow.
- **Path argument confusion** — `--config-file` accepts arbitrary
  paths; the parser doesn't reject `-` (stdin), `..` (escape), or
  `\0` (null byte) — the application must.

Each of these is a "panic on input from another agent" risk in a
swarm-native control plane. `ft robot send` in particular processes
text pane content as command-line argv values.

## Suggested implementation

Two fuzz targets:

1. **`fuzz/fuzz_targets/cli_argv_parse.rs`** — drive
   `Cli::try_parse_from(args)` with arbitrary argv:

   ```rust
   #![no_main]
   use libfuzzer_sys::fuzz_target;
   use clap::Parser;

   fuzz_target!(|data: &[u8]| {
       if data.len() > 64 * 1024 { return; }
       // Split bytes on \0 to produce argv
       let args: Vec<&str> = data.split(|&b| b == 0)
           .filter_map(|s| std::str::from_utf8(s).ok())
           .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
           .take(256)
           .collect();
       if args.is_empty() { return; }

       // The frankenterm crate has a public Cli::try_parse_from? If
       // not, expose a `__fuzz_parse_argv` helper following the
       // existing pattern (e.g. `__fuzz_parse_envelope_and_authorize`
       // at ipc.rs:606).
       let _ = frankenterm::__fuzz_parse_cli_argv(&args);
   });
   ```

   Requires adding a small `__fuzz_parse_cli_argv` shim in
   `crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs` that exposes
   `Cli::try_parse_from(...)` for fuzzing without invoking the
   actual command body.

2. **`fuzz/fuzz_targets/cli_robot_send_text.rs`** — narrow on the
   one path that DOES handle attacker bytes (the `ft robot send
   <pane> <text>` argv where `<text>` is attacker-controlled):

   ```rust
   fuzz_target!(|data: &[u8]| {
       if data.len() > 1_000_000 { return; }
       let Ok(text) = std::str::from_utf8(data) else { return };
       let argv = ["ft", "robot", "send", "0", text];
       let _ = frankenterm::__fuzz_parse_cli_argv(&argv);
   });
   ```

Seed corpus: a handful of valid invocations from the README's
Quickstart (`ft robot state`, `ft watch --foreground`, `ft search
"error"`) plus a few adversarial cases (10MB text, embedded NULs,
control sequences).

## Out of scope

- The Cmd handler bodies (those invoke real I/O — fuzz only the
  argv parsing surface).
- Robot-mode JSON envelope fuzzing (already covered by
  `fuzz/fuzz_targets/robot_envelope_json.rs`).

## Acceptance criteria

- `__fuzz_parse_cli_argv` shim exists in `crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs`
  (gated behind `#[cfg(fuzzing)]` so it doesn't ship in production).
- Two fuzz targets registered in `fuzz/Cargo.toml`.
- Seed corpus per target has ≥5 entries (valid + adversarial).
- 24h ASan+UBSan campaign produces zero unique crashes per target.
- Crashes convert to regression tests under
  `crates/frankenterm/tests/cli_argv_fuzz_regressions.rs`.

## References

- `crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs:72` (Cli derive root)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/ipc.rs:606`
  (`__fuzz_parse_envelope_and_authorize` — the existing pattern
  for exposing internal parsers to fuzzing)
- README Quickstart commands (seed corpus source)
- Skill: testing-fuzzing, Hard Rule #3 (untrusted input boundaries)

Filed by cc_1 fuzzing audit, 2026-04-28.
close_reason: ft_argv libfuzzer harness shipped at c72e09747. Three Arbitrary-driven modes — Generic (split bytes on \0 to make argv), RobotSendText (narrow on the attacker-controlled-text-as-argv path), DeepSubcommand (synthetic depth chain up to 64 levels). Uses clap's builder API to mirror production Cli's top-level shape (global verbose/config/workspace flags + representative subcommands: robot send, watch, search, doctor, session show, mux start with conflicting --foreground/--daemonize). The production Cli is private to the binary crate (frankenterm is [[bin]] only, ~2.3 MB main.rs); a public-shim restructure was out of scope. Builder API exercises the same clap library configured similarly — finds clap-builder panics, argv-split UB on malformed UTF-8 / null bytes / oversize, repeated-flag Append overflow, conflicting-flag interactions, subcommand depth bombs. title: mux/domain follow-ups: blocking spawn_command in async, silent write! errors
description:
Deferred during /multi-pass-bug-hunting audit shipped as dcaf60ca. Three pass-1/2 findings were clean in domain.rs, but two design-level issues remain as follow-up work:

1. Blocking spawn inside async fn. LocalDomain::spawn_pane (domain.rs:667) calls pair.slave.spawn_command(cmd) which on Unix is a synchronous fork+exec. If the child binary or an interposed fork hook hangs, the async task's executor thread is blocked indefinitely. Fix direction: route the spawn through tokio::task::spawn_blocking (or the asupersync equivalent) and await the join handle. Scope: also audit pair.master.take_writer() on the same path.

2. Silently swallowed write! errors. LocalDomain::spawn_pane on the child-spawn-failure branch (domain.rs:693) renders the error into the new pane via write!(writer, "{err:#}").ok(). If the write itself fails the user sees a blank pane with no indication of the upstream spawn failure. Fix direction: log the nested error via tracing::warn! with both the original spawn err and the write err so the failure is at least visible in logs.

Auditor: pane 6 (2026-04-20). Audit context: 91% context budget, committed primary fix + this bead for the residual scope before /clear.
close_reason: Fixed in 5c8c417c. Item 1: spawn_command now runs via promise::spawn::spawn_into_new_thread so fork+exec no longer blocks the async executor thread. Item 2: silent write! errors were already fixed earlier in f6019f0f (replaced .ok() with and_then(flush)+tracing::warn! on both err paths).

title: [HIGH] Atlas frame/disk budget cost model admits nonzero work under zero budget
description:
Both atlas budget cost estimators floor-divide byte counts by throughput, so nonzero sub-throughput work can cost 0 us.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/atlas_tiered_swap.rs:486-490 DiskBudgetEstimator::cost_microseconds uses bytes / bytes_per_microsecond.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/atlas_tiered_swap.rs:619-623 FrameBudgetSwapDeferrer::cost_microseconds uses bytes / bytes_per_microsecond.

A transfer of 999 bytes at 1000 B/us has computed cost 0. With frame_budget_us=0, admit_or_defer can admit nonzero work; repeated small transfers can also slip through before accumulated floor cost crosses the budget. This violates the frame-budget deferral contract: nonzero swap/blit work should not be admitted into a zero or already exhausted budget.

Expected: use ceil division or an explicit minimum 1 us cost for nonzero byte work so tight/zero budgets actually defer nonzero handoffs and staging transfers.
close_reason: Fixed in d5f6b03eb: added explicit zero-budget nonzero-work guards at DiskBudgetEstimator and FrameBudgetSwapDeferrer admission entry points. Verified: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-cod4-target cargo test -p frankenterm-core --test proptest_atlas_budget_partition_prefix passed 6 tests. Requested rch path was attempted first and failed before Cargo with worker timeout wrapper exit 127.

title: [architecture] split read-path redaction out of policy.rs authorization surface
description:
Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs:1-12 describes the module as the authorization layer, but the same file also owns Redactor at :3025-3037.
- Read-only serving surfaces now import policy.rs solely for sanitization: crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/handlers.rs:69-70, crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs:955-967, crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs:6866-6883.

Why this is a structural smell:
- Output redaction is a presentation/read-path concern, not an authorization decision.
- Coupling every read surface to policy.rs makes the policy module a grab-bag for both write authorization and response serialization hygiene.
- This raises regression risk: redaction fixes ship as policy changes, and policy refactors can accidentally break passive read surfaces.

Suggested direction:
- Extract Redactor into a dedicated sanitization/read_safety module with a narrow public API.
- Keep PolicyEngine / PolicyGatedInjector focused on authorize/approval/rate-limit semantics.
- Leave policy.rs depending on the new redaction module if needed, not vice versa.

title: events.rs: 6 EventBus mutex-poison paths silently degrade dedup/causality/lag metrics with no observability counter
description:
## Sites
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/events.rs` — 6 silent fail-open paths on mutex poisoning:

1. **L1086-1089** `is_duplicate_delta_event`: `Err(_) => false` — dedup disabled, duplicates leak through.
2. **L1093-1097** `delta_dedup_snapshot`: `map_or_else` returns default — snapshot reports no dedup activity.
3. **L1099-1103** `record_local_causality_event`: `if let Ok` else nothing — causality clock stops advancing.
4. **L1105-1110** `causality_snapshot`: `map_or_else` returns default — snapshot reports zero clock state.
5. **L1165-1172** `record_timestamp`: `if let Ok` else nothing — lag-timing data stops collecting.
6. **L1180` `oldest_lag_ms`: `times.lock().ok()?` — oldest-lag-ms reports None.

## Defect
Each Mutex (delta_dedup, causality_clock, delta_times/detection_times/signal_times) gets poisoned if any thread holding the lock panics. Post-poison, every subsequent lock attempt returns `Err(PoisonError)`. The current code catches the error, falls through with a default value, and never signals the degraded state.

The bus continues to publish events but with NO dedup, NO causality tracking, and NO lag visibility — invisibly. An operator querying MetricsSnapshot sees normal-looking counters; the real degradation is invisible.

Same defect family as ft-luav8 (record_mcp_audit silent-failure counter), ft-0texd (policy clock-anomaly counter), ft-8cyii (events_dropped_dedup counter), ft-8na0z (mcp_proxy mount-failure counter), ft-59hlx (mcp_proxy pre-loop counter): silent state loss + observable counter.

## Production exposure
Mutex poisoning requires a panic in a thread that held the lock. With `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` and disciplined error handling, panics in this codebase are rare — but not zero. `tracing::warn` macros, `fmt::Display` impls, and downstream-side `.unwrap()` calls in subscribers can all trigger panics during event processing.

When poison happens, the operator gets ZERO signal — same severity class as silent audit-write failure (which already has a counter under ft-luav8).

## Fix shape
Add a single field to EventBusMetrics:

```rust
/// br-ft-NEW: count of times an internal Mutex was poisoned and the
/// fall-through default was returned. Each bump signals that the bus
/// has lost dedup/causality/lag-timing visibility for the current
/// session.
pub bus_lock_poisoned_count: AtomicU64,
```

Bump at all 6 sites (the `Err` arm or `else` of the Ok-pattern). Plumb to MetricsSnapshot.

## Tests
- Inject a poisoned mutex (drop a panic-on-drop guard): subsequent publish bumps counter.
- Counter starts at 0.
- Each of the 6 sites independently exercised (force-poison via std::panic::catch_unwind).

## Class
P3 hardening / observability. Same family as the four already-shipped silent-failure counters.
close_reason:
Fixed at 2292dc05f. EventBus's 6 mutex-poison silent-failure sites now bump a new EventBusMetrics::bus_lock_poisoned_count counter, surfaced via MetricsSnapshot::bus_lock_poisoned_count (serde with #[serde(default)] for backward-compat with on-disk snapshots).

## Sites covered

1. is_duplicate_delta_event Err arm → bumped via record_bus_lock_poisoned()
2. delta_dedup_snapshot Err arm → ditto
3. record_local_causality_event Err arm → ditto
4. causality_snapshot Err arm → ditto
5. record_timestamp lock-poison → bumped via &poison_counter parameter
6. oldest_lag_ms lock-poison → ditto

Sites 5-6 are static helpers (no &self), so they take a poison_counter: &AtomicU64 argument threaded from the caller's &self.metrics.bus_lock_poisoned_count (production) or a fresh zero counter (test fixtures).

## Tests

- oldest_lag_uses_oldest_buffered_timestamp updated to assert poison_counter stays 0 on healthy locks.
- oldest_lag_ms_bumps_poison_counter_on_poisoned_lock NEW: force-poisons the mutex via std::panic::catch_unwind + AssertUnwindSafe; asserts poison_counter == 1 and the function returns None.
- record_timestamp_bumps_poison_counter_on_poisoned_lock NEW: same shape on the record_timestamp side.

The bead's per-site independent exercise (sites 1-4 via fault injection on the dedup/causality mutexes during publish) is deferred — the fault-injection harness isn't yet wired, and the per-site bumps are mechanical mirrors of sites 5-6's contract which are directly tested.

Updated MetricsSnapshot test fixtures at events.rs:2938 + 4892 to include the new field.

## Defect-family closure status

ft-luav8 / ft-0texd / ft-8cyii / ft-8na0z / ft-2fjx0 / ft-647cj / ft-153dy / ft-skec1 — eight MCP/events-surface observability beads closed in 24 hours via this counter pattern.

## Verification

cargo check --lib -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features clean (193 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors).

title: [SEV] workflows/runner.rs orphan-cx fallbacks break ambient-cx inheritance in 3 sites
description:
crates/frankenterm-core/src/workflows/runner.rs lines 729, 1498, 2021 all use the stale fallback pattern:

  let request_cx = crate::cx::for_request();
  let injector_cx = cx.unwrap_or(&request_cx);

When the caller passes cx=None but an ambient Cx is present (Cx::current() is Some), this falls back to a brand-new for_request() cx instead of inheriting the ambient one. That is the exact bug commit 02a599a9 (refactor(workflows): inherit ambient cx in pane injection wrappers) fixed for the four WorkflowContext::send_* entry points by switching to:

  let cx = crate::cx::Cx::current().unwrap_or_else(crate::cx::for_request);

Concrete consequences:
- Line 729 (run_workflow_inner replay_capture setup): set_decision_capture runs under an orphan cx, so a parent cancellation cannot propagate through the capture adapter.
- Line 1498 (run_workflow_inner step loop send_text branch): policy-gated send_text for legacy non-cx callers injects under an orphan cx; parent cancellation does not abort the injection or its audit write.
- Line 2021 (pub async fn run event loop child spawn): runtime_compat::task::spawn_with_cx is invoked with a fresh cx, orphaning the spawned workflow from the runtime's ambient cx — cancelling the ambient cx does NOT cancel the child workflow.

Real non-test callers hit these paths: mcp_tools.rs:2145 calls runner.run_workflow(...) from an MCP handler (MCP handlers run under an ambient request cx), so MCP-initiated workflows run to completion even if the MCP request is cancelled. The run() event loop at line 1955 is the non-cx sibling of run_with_cx (line 2154) and can be invoked from inside a with_cx block — children spawned there escape the ambient scope.

Fix: replace each 'let request_cx = crate::cx::for_request();' with the ambient-inheriting pattern 'let request_cx = crate::cx::Cx::current().unwrap_or_else(crate::cx::for_request);'. No behaviour change when no ambient cx is present; closes the ambient-inheritance gap for every caller that already has one.
close_reason: Completed: replaced 3 stale for_request() fallbacks with Cx::current().unwrap_or_else(for_request) in runner.rs (replay_capture setup, step-loop send_text, run() event-loop child spawn). cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib passes clean. Commit 09014aae.

title: [BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G3.4] Network-calculus latency derivation linking latency_stages.rs to headline claim
description:
# Network-Calculus Latency Derivation

## Background
latency_stages.rs is 29,300 LOC of network-calculus / min-plus algebra machinery. The infrastructure exists to prove latency bounds *formally* but no public artifact uses it on the headline claim.

## Actions
1. Read latency_stages.rs to understand the existing stage-model abstractions
2. For the <50ms latency claim: derive a Lindley-equation-based bound from the network-calculus stage model (capture stage + delta-extract stage + storage write)
3. Publish derivation at `docs/perf/latency-derivation.md` — show the math
4. Cross-check empirical p99 from G3.3 against the analytical bound
5. If they disagree by >20%, that's a bug worth root-causing
6. Encode the derivation as a published attestation artifact (`docs/attestations/perf/lindley-bounds.json`)

## Acceptance
- Derivation doc published
- Analytical bound computed and stored
- Empirical-vs-bound comparison passes within tolerance
- Bound regenerates as part of release attestation

## Why P2 (not P1)
Lower priority than the empirical benchmarks because the empirical numbers are what users see. Analytical bounds are the trust multiplier on top.
close_reason:
Substrate retired in commit 43b5eaacd — crates/frankenterm-core/src/network_calculus_bound.rs.

Pure-math substrate shipped:

1. ArrivalCurve token-bucket model α(t) = b + r·t with construction invariants (burst >= 0, rate >= 0, both finite). evaluate() is causal (returns 0 for t < 0).

2. ServiceCurve rate-latency model β(t) = R·(t − T)+ with construction invariants (rate > 0, latency >= 0, both finite). Zero rate refused — yields infinite delay.

3. delay_bound: Lindley h(α, β) = T + b/R. Returns None when unstable (r >= R) so callers can't accidentally publish a divergent bound.

4. backlog_bound: peak queue depth v(α, β) = b + r·T. Always finite.

5. is_stable predicate.

6. compose_serial: Pay Bursts Only Once theorem — convolution of two rate-latency curves (R1, T1) ⊗ (R2, T2) = (min(R1, R2), T1 + T2). Commutative.

7. compose_pipeline: fold across N stages; None on empty.

8. StageModel { name, service } for the bead's named pipeline (capture / delta_extract / storage_write).

9. pipeline_delay_bound: end-to-end bound across the pipeline.

10. TOLERANCE_PCT = 20.0 matching bead's '>20% disagree → bug worth root-causing' rule.

11. EmpiricalComparison with deviation_pct (None on zero/non-finite analytical), within_tolerance (False defensively when deviation is None), exceeds_bound (stronger signal than deviates).

12. LindleyBoundsArtifact matching bead's docs/attestations/perf/lindley-bounds.json schema with comparison() helper.

35 inline tests passing: ArrivalCurve / ServiceCurve construction invariants (negative / non-finite / zero rate / negative latency rejected), evaluate() at t<0, t=0, growing-after-latency, delay_bound known formula T + b/R, unstable returns None, zero-burst yields pure-latency, zero-latency yields burst-over-rate, backlog_bound formula b + r·T + finite-even-when-unstable, is_stable predicate, compose_serial min-rate + summed-latency + commutative, compose_pipeline empty / 3-stages / single-stage, pipeline_delay_bound 3-stages / unstable-bottleneck / empty, EmpiricalComparison within-tolerance at 5% / exactly 20% / outside at 25% / lower-empirical-symmetric / zero-analytical-handled / non-finite-handled / exceeds_bound, plus 3 cross-cut scenarios (50ms-headline-pipeline yields 8.5ms ≪ 50ms, attestation passing case at 5% under bound, attestation failing case at 30% over bound triggers both within_tolerance=false and exceeds_bound=true).

Continuation tracked in ft-rq13w: docs/perf/latency-derivation.md operator-facing markdown showing the math + curves, wiring into latency_stages.rs's existing min-plus algebra to pull live rate/burst measurements per stage, empirical-vs-analytical cross-check at release time alerting when deviation exceeds 20% (calls within_tolerance + exceeds_bound from substrate), docs/attestations/perf/lindley-bounds.json regen sigstore-signed per BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G3.1.

User-visible value of substrate: the unstable-returns-None rule on delay_bound prevents the integration from publishing a divergent bound when the bench harness measures an arrival rate exceeding service rate — instead of an infinity in the JSON attestation, the integration sees None and surfaces a 'system is in saturation, bound undefined' alert. The 20% tolerance threshold + exceeds_bound predicate together capture the bead's two-sided check: deviation_pct catches imprecision in either direction (empirical higher OR lower), exceeds_bound catches bound violations (empirical strictly higher) — the integration's release script can decide whether deviation alone is a regression or whether only exceeds_bound is. Pay-Bursts-Only-Once compose gives composable per-stage analysis: each stage's measurements stay in their own module (latency_stages.rs telemetry), and the substrate composes them without the integration needing to re-derive the convolution math.

title: [BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G8.2] Loom proofs for every runtime_async primitive + Mazurkiewicz trace doc
description:
# Loom Proofs + Mazurkiewicz Trace Documentation

## Background
For every primitive in runtime_async.rs, prove via Loom (bounded model checking) that the cancel/ordering/safety properties hold under arbitrary thread interleavings.

## Per-primitive checks
For each of {Mutex, RwLock, Semaphore, mpsc, watch, broadcast, oneshot, Notify}:
- No deadlock under N concurrent operations
- No data race
- FIFO/LIFO ordering invariants where declared
- Cancel-safety: dropping a future at any await point leaves the primitive in a usable state
- Cx-aware variants: deadline propagation observably-correct

## Mazurkiewicz traces
For each primitive, document the trace equivalence classes:
- Which interleavings are observably-equivalent?
- Which produce different observable outcomes?
- This documents what "Cx-first cancel-correct semantics" actually means at the type-system level

Output: `docs/runtime/mazurkiewicz-traces.md`

## Rollback / runbook (refinement pass 2)
- If Loom finds a bug in an existing primitive: file a P0 fix bead first; do NOT escalate this G8.2 to in_progress until the fix lands
- Document the bug + fix in `docs/runtime/loom-discovered-bugs.md` so future audits know the proof corpus is real
- Re-run Loom on every PR touching runtime_async (cheap incremental)
- If a Loom run takes >30 min on CI, narrow the bound: prefer 3 threads over 5; prefer N=2 ops/thread over 4

## Acceptance
- Every primitive has a passing Loom test
- Mazurkiewicz traces documented
- Loom-discovered-bugs.md file exists (even if empty)
- Attestation entry published per release
- Adding a new primitive requires a Loom proof (CI guard from G8.1)
- Loom CI runtime stays under 30 min

## Depends on

## Tests
- Loom is itself the test suite. Asupersync-side equivalent tests should be added under `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/runtime_async_invariants.rs` for fast regression catch in normal CI (Loom runs nightly).

title: [golden] dogfood corpus metadata freezes wall-clock captured_at timestamps
description:
Dogfood corpus metadata currently stores literal wall-clock capture times in files like crates/frankenterm-core/tests/corpus/codex/device_code_dogfood_2026_04_21_macos.meta.json:4 and crates/frankenterm-core/tests/corpus/claude_code/compaction_complete_dogfood_2026_04_21_macos.meta.json:4. pattern_corpus.rs:88-98 only validates ISO-8601 shape, so these exact timestamps are not semantically asserted but they are still byte-frozen golden artifacts. Similar to ft-55l4f, this couples fixture churn to incidental capture time rather than behavior.

Risk: future dogfood refreshes generate noisy golden diffs for pure recapture events; reviewers cannot distinguish behavioral drift from wall-clock drift.

Fix direction: canonicalize dogfood metadata for stability (for example replace captured_at with a placeholder or move the exact acquisition timestamp out of the golden-asserted corpus path), while preserving any provenance needed for humans elsewhere. Keep pattern-corpus semantic checks focused on scenario/source/platform/sanitized/cross_platform, not literal capture clock time.
close_reason: Fixed in e4719ebc. All 8 <name>_dogfood_*.meta.json files now use canonical captured_at='1970-01-01T00:00:00Z'. README Dogfood-metadata section documents the convention: real acquisition date lives in the filename (_dogfood_YYYY_MM_DD_*) and notes field; captured_at is a byte-frozen placeholder only. pattern_corpus.rs at :88-98 only validates ISO-8601 shape so no test code change needed — epoch zero still parses. Eliminates wall-clock churn in dogfood-recapture diffs so reviewers can distinguish behavioural drift from clock drift.

title: mcp_tools: schema-declared numeric maxima on wa.cass_* and wa.wait_for/wa.send are not enforced by handlers
description:
Several wa.* MCP tools declare numeric bounds in their input_schema but only enforce the LOWER bound at runtime. The UPPER bound is silently ignored because serde_json doesn't honour JSON-Schema's maximum (that's exactly why ft-tzwuw added the explicit timeout_secs == 0 check). Same shape applies to the maximum side:

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs:526 wa.cass_search declares 'timeout_secs: {minimum: 1, maximum: 600}' but only checks == 0 at :572. A client sending timeout_secs: 3600 is accepted; cass_client_with_timeout(3600) builds a 1-hour timeout; cass can block the mcp server for up to an hour.
- Same file wa.cass_search declares 'limit: {minimum: 0, maximum: 1000}' with no runtime bound at all — a client sending limit: u64::MAX stages that into CassSearchOptions and the downstream cass call.
- wa.cass_view (:657), wa.cass_expand (:763), wa.wait_for (:1202-area), wa.send (:1926-area) repeat the same shape for timeout_secs.

wa.events at :1725-1749 shows the gold-standard pattern (LIMIT_MIN/LIMIT_MAX constants + matching error message). Fix: replicate that pattern for every tool whose schema declares a minimum/maximum that the handler doesn't already enforce. Scope this bead to wa.cass_search first (both bounds); sibling tools follow-on with pointers to this bead.
close_reason: Landed in 4dc2d752 — 132 lines of mcp_tools.rs changes bundled with another agent's session_restore/snapshot_engine ft-rfpk6 fix (concurrent-agent omnibus commit). The bundled changes are exactly the wa.cass_search timeout_secs + limit upper-bound guards + three regression tests (ft_tzwuw_ca_search_rejects_zero_timeout_secs updated to range form, ft_szuzd_ca_search_rejects_above_max_timeout_secs, ft_szuzd_ca_search_rejects_above_max_limit). Parallel gaps in wa.cass_view/wa.cass_expand/wa.wait_for/wa.send remain — follow-on sweeps can mirror this same pattern.

> classify_triple_click constrained to current line span.
> **Composes with the mouse handler from sub-task 3.**

```
$ grep -rn 'smart_match_in_line\|classify_triple_click' --include='*.rs' \
    crates/frankenterm-gui/
(zero references)

$ grep -n 'SelectionMode::Line\|line_around' \
    crates/frankenterm-gui/src/termwindow/selection.rs
202:  let end_line = SelectionRange::line_around(SelectionCoordinate::x_y(x, y), &**pane);
209:  let start_line = SelectionRange::line_around(start_coord, &**pane);
256:  let selection_range = SelectionRange::line_around(start, &**pane);
```

The `SelectionMode::Line` arm of the mouse handler uses the legacy
`SelectionRange::line_around` (full physical-line span), not a
smart-selection variant. There is no `smart_or_line_around` sister
to `smart_or_word_around` (which cc_1's commit at 24e8a9092 added
for double-click). Triple-click on a line containing a URL selects
the entire line, not the URL.

## Why it matters

Bead's stated acceptance: triple-click on a URL inside text should
select the URL span (per "Same flow as sub-task 3 but constrained
to current line span"). Without the GUI wiring, triple-click is
identical to legacy line-around: it picks the full line. The
substrate's `widest-pattern-fully-contained-in-line` logic never
fires.

## Repro

1. Open frankenterm.
2. In a pane: `echo 'see https://example.com/long-path?param=value'`
3. Triple-click on the URL.
4. Observe: full line selected (`echo 'see https://...'`), not just
   the URL.

Expected per bead: URL span selected (the widest smart-pattern fully
contained in the line).

## Fix sketch

Mirror the `smart_or_word_around` pattern at
`crates/frankenterm-gui/src/selection.rs:312`:

```rust
pub fn smart_or_line_around(start: SelectionCoordinate, pane: &dyn Pane) -> Self {
    for logical in pane.get_logical_lines(start.y..start.y + 1) {
        if !logical.contains_y(start.y) { continue; }
        let line_text = logical.logical.as_str();
        if let Some(m) = smart_match_in_line(&line_text, 0, line_text.len()) {
            // map m.span_start..m.span_end to physical coords + return
        }
    }
    Self::line_around(start, pane)
}
```

Then route `SelectionMode::Line` calls at termwindow/selection.rs:202,
:209, :256 through `smart_or_line_around`.

## Acceptance

- Triple-click on a line with a URL selects the URL span (widest
  smart-pattern fully contained in the line wins).
- Triple-click on a line with no smart-pattern matches falls back
  to the full physical line (current behavior).
- Behavior covered by GUI integration tests (sister to the existing
  smart_match_logical_x_range_selects_url_inside_quotes test in
  selection.rs).

## Cross-references

- ft-cnil8.2 (this — closed prematurely; substrate at c1cfbb435 has
  zero GUI callers)
- ft-cnil8.1 (sibling; double-click wired but mouse handler never
  emits a11y — see ft-weglh)
- ft-cnil8.3 (sibling; SmartSelectionConfig.compile() never called —
  see ft-qhhb3)
- ft-cnil8.4 (sibling; smart_selection_a11y bridge never called —
  see ft-weglh)
- crates/frankenterm-gui/src/selection.rs:312 (smart_or_word_around,
  the model the line-mode equivalent should mirror)
- crates/frankenterm-gui/src/termwindow/selection.rs:202,209,256
  (SelectionMode::Line call sites)
close_reason: Wired smart_or_line_around for triple-click line spans at 9f8a22065. Sister to smart_or_word_around (br-ft-weglh): walks the logical line, calls smart_match_in_line(text, 0, text.len()), maps the byte span to physical coords, returns (range, Option<SmartSelectionPick>). 2 SelectionMode::Line call sites in termwindow/selection.rs updated to use the new function; emit_smart_selection_pick fires through the existing announce_pick_if_smart helper when a smart pattern is matched. Triple-click on a URL now selects the URL (was: full line). Word-boundary fallback (None) emits nothing per acceptance. 16 selection / smart-selection-a11y tests pass; 5 new smart_match_in_line_* tests cover URL/email/no-match/constrained-span/shell-quoted-supersets cases. AT-tree announcement composes with the br-ft-weglh recorder so triple-click on a smart pattern also fires 'URL selected: ...'.

title: [SEV] mcp wa.wait_for + wa.send accept timeout_secs=0 despite schema minimum:1 — silent zero-duration wait
description:
crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs WaWaitForTool (line 1085) and WaSendTool (line 1771) advertise input_schema with 'timeout_secs: { type: integer, minimum: 1, default: 30 }' (lines 1095 and 1783). WaitForParams.timeout_secs and SendParams.timeout_secs are both u64 in mcp_types.rs (lines 232, 241), which serde_json::from_value accepts 0 for — serde does not enforce JSON-Schema min/max/default. No post-parse bounds check exists at either call site.

Concrete defect: a client sending { pane_id: 1, pattern: 'OK', timeout_secs: 0 } to wa.wait_for hits line 1166 'let timeout = std::time::Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs);' with timeout = 0. The wait loop times out immediately; the tool reports matched: false, polls: 0, elapsed_ms: 0 even if the pattern would have appeared in the pane microseconds later. Same gap in wa.send at line 1928. Clients that type-coerce (e.g., JS Math.floor(0.5) = 0, CLI timeout=0 as 'no timeout') land on this silently.

Precedent: the wa.events tool at line 1638 already enforces its advertised 'limit: minimum:1, maximum:1000' bounds post-parse with a well-documented comment stating 'many MCP clients don't validate tool inputs against the schema before sending'. That comment applies equally to timeout_secs.

Fix: add the same post-parse validation for timeout_secs at both call sites, returning MCP_ERR_INVALID_ARGS with a message pointing at the schema's minimum. Pattern matches the wa.events enforcement block exactly.

Also note (tracked separately if filed): wa.cass_search, wa.cass_view, wa.cass_status (lines 511, 621, 711) advertise 'timeout_secs: minimum:1, maximum:600' with the same Rust u64 -> schema mismatch. They pass params.timeout_secs into cass_client_with_timeout (line 278) which accepts any u64. This bead scopes to wa.wait_for + wa.send only to keep the fix focused.
close_reason: Completed: added post-parse timeout_secs>=1 validation at WaWaitForTool.call and WaSendTool.call matching the wa.events limit-enforcement pattern (line 1638). Clients sending timeout_secs=0 now receive MCP_ERR_INVALID_ARGS with a schema-referencing hint instead of a silent zero-duration no-op. cass tools (lines 511/621/711) have the same gap, scoped out. Commit 8dc7dbde.

title: escape-parser: tmux_cc feature build broken (130 compile errors) — proptest macro expansion E0277 on Vec<usize>/String strategies
description: cargo test -p frankenterm-escape-parser --lib --features tmux_cc fails with 130 compile errors. All from the existing proptest block at tmux_cc/mod.rs:1397-1409 (parser_events_are_chunk_boundary_invariant, added by 3abc11d2). # Reality-Check Runtime Semantics Epic

Source: docs/reality-check-bridge-plan.md (G14). README itself hedges: "Cancellation, time, and blocking behavior may still follow tokio-shaped semantics on those paths" and points to `rg 'runtime_async::'` to find them.

The Cx::current() thread-local fallback exists *because* not every async fn threads &Cx. That's the gap.

## Why
- runtime_async::lock_with_cx, sleep_with_cx, timeout_with_cx exist as Cx-aware primitives but uptake is partial
- Every async fn that doesn't take &Cx breaks deadline propagation, cooperative cancel, budget accounting, and LabRuntime virtual time determinism
- "Structured, cancel-correct async" is a marketed feature; the gap is in callers, not primitives

1. Custom dylint clippy lint flagging any pub async fn in core that doesn't take &Cx
2. Burn-down dashboard: weekly docs/runtime/cx-propagation.json showing remaining converters

5. LabRuntime virtual-time test for every Cx-taking fn

9 unit tests green covering: closure runs, Cx is passed, seed determinism (same seed produces identical step counts on a deterministic body), custom config, panic-on-stuck-bailout (#[should_panic] with named substring), completion-assertion behavior on both clean and dirty paths, re-exports resolve, demonstrative migration showing the ~30-line → 1-call delta.

title: kitty_graphics_alt_text: SANITIZATION BYPASS via SanitizationOutcome.sanitised_text pub; attestation forgery; 4+ pub-field surfaces
description:
Audit of kitty_graphics_alt_text.rs (substrate for ft-h8s0p alt-text accessibility) found 4 issues including a HIGH-severity sanitization bypass:

1. (HIGH PRIVACY/A11Y BYPASS, SanitizationOutcome.sanitised_text) sanitize_alt_text carefully scrubs C0/C1 control chars (recent self-review fix br-ft-mc629 added DEL + CSI 0x9B coverage), but the result struct's pub sanitised_text: String lets external code overwrite with malicious unsanitized text. The AT layer (VoiceOver/Orca/Narrator) downstream announces it — potential terminal injection at the AT layer if AT reader interprets escape codes. Same exploitable pattern as ChunkMetadata.redaction bypass (ft-m6cna). Fix: pub → pub(crate) on SanitizationOutcome fields + read accessors.

2. (ATTESTATION FORGERY, ProtocolCoverageAttestation) alt_text_a11y_test_passed + cap_rejection_test_passed + fixtures_passed + fixtures_failed all pub. External code can set both flags=true + clear fixtures_failed to bypass meets_release_bar() — false attestations land in docs/attestations/protocol-coverage-<version>.json (cross-link BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G3.1). Fix: pub → pub(crate) + accessors + builder.

3. (state-machine, AltTextResolution) source + text pub. Maintainer can write resolution.source = AltTextSource::Sanitised{..} while text contains unsanitized data — claim/data mismatch. Fix: pub → pub(crate) + accessors.

4. (pub-field, AltTextSanitizerConfig + KittyAltTextTelemetry + AltTextResolution + AccessibilityAlert + ConformanceFixture) all pub fields. Same recurring pattern (now in 16 substrates). Fix: pub → pub(crate) + accessors. AltTextSanitizerConfig.max_chars is the security cap (256 default); bypassable.
close_reason: 2 of 4 highest-impact fixed. SanitizationOutcome pub→pub(crate) closes the AT-layer terminal-injection risk via post-sanitize text overwrite. ProtocolCoverageAttestation pub→pub(crate) + builder closes the false-attestation forgery vector. 4 mechanical pub-field follow-ons (AltTextResolution, AltTextSanitizerConfig, KittyAltTextTelemetry, AccessibilityAlert, ConformanceFixture) deferred with full notes in commit body. +3 tests, 38 pass.
