title: [Human command] wa stop (stop watcher in workspace safely)
description:
# Task: Human command wa stop

## Goal
Give users a safe, ergonomic way to stop a running `wa watch` for a given workspace.

Many users will run `wa watch` in the background (or via terminal multiplexers). Telling them to manually find and kill a PID is user-hostile.

## Behavior (v0)
- `wa stop`
  - resolves the workspace (flag/env/default)
  - reads the watch lock metadata (pid/started_at/host/version)
  - sends SIGTERM to the watcher pid (preferred) and waits for the lock to be released
  - prints a clear summary:
    - which workspace
    - which pid
    - whether shutdown was graceful

- `wa stop --force`
  - if graceful shutdown times out, escalates to SIGKILL (only with explicit `--force`)

## Safety
- Never kills an arbitrary PID:
  - only act if the lock metadata matches the workspace lock
  - require the process to be owned by the same user (best-effort check)

## UX
- TTY: rich panel output.
- Non-TTY: stable JSON.

## Testing
- Integration test:
  - start a watcher-like process that holds the lock
  - run `wa stop`
  - assert lock is released and process exits

- E2E:
  - `wa-4vx.10.21` validates stop+restart behavior and captures artifacts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `wa stop` reliably stops a watcher started in the same workspace.
- `wa stop` errors are actionable when no watcher is running.

title: [EPIC] Setup automation: wa setup (wezterm.lua lane, shell integration, SSH hosts)
description:
# [EPIC] Setup & configuration automation

## Mission
Make wa easy to install and hard to misconfigure.

## Why
wa’s correctness depends on:
- having sufficient scrollback / capture strategy
- prompt boundary markers (OSC 133 / user-vars)
- a forwarding lane from WezTerm to wa (wezterm.lua)

Humans should not have to hand-edit large config files or remember magic snippets.

## Scope
- Local setup (`wa setup`): idempotent modifications and installs.
- SSH host discovery for future remote support.

## Non-goals (v0.1)
- Full remote orchestration across machines (Phase 5+)

## Testing & safety (non-negotiable)
Setup is where users decide whether they trust wa. The setup path must be:
- non-destructive
- idempotent
- transparent (shows diffs / planned edits)

Test coverage must include:
- fixture-based unit tests for:
  - ssh config parsing
  - idempotent patching logic (wezterm.lua + shell)

- E2E scripts with artifacts:
  - `wa setup` run twice produces the same result (idempotency)
  - logs and patched files are captured for debugging

## Definition of done
- A new machine can get to a working capture + events pipeline with a single guided `wa setup`.

## Success Criteria
- `wa setup` provides a safe, idempotent path to install wezterm.lua lane and shell integration.
- Setup scripts avoid destructive changes and include clear rollback instructions.
- E2E/manual validation steps exist with detailed logging for troubleshooting.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All items in the following sections are satisfied: Success Criteria, Definition of Done.
- All Testing requirements pass (unit/integration/E2E) with the logging/artifacts described above.
- Any explicit dependencies for this bead are implemented and validated via tests or E2E artifacts.

title: E2E script: wa setup idempotent patching (wezterm.lua + shell) with artifacts
description:
# Task: E2E script — wa setup idempotency

## Goal
Validate that wa setup is truly safe and idempotent.

Setup commands are uniquely user-sensitive: a bug can corrupt dotfiles and destroy trust.
This E2E test provides a safety net with great logging and artifacts.

## Scenario
Run against a temporary fake "home" directory (never touch real dotfiles):
- Provide fixture files:
  - wezterm.lua (various shapes)
  - .zshrc / .bashrc / config.fish fixtures
  - optional ~/.ssh/config fixture

Steps
1) wa setup --dry-run
   - asserts: prints what it would change without writing

2) wa setup (apply mode)
   - asserts: writes only within the temp home

3) wa setup again
   - asserts: no further changes (idempotent)

## Assertions
- wezterm.lua contains exactly one wa-managed block (WA-BEGIN/WA-END) after apply.
- Running again makes zero changes.
- Shell integration is installed once and is idempotent.
- Output is verbose, timestamped, and never contains secrets.

## Artifacts
- before/after copies of each modified file
- unified diff outputs
- full command logs

## Registry
- Register this case in the E2E case registry (`wa-4vx.10.20`), including prerequisites and default inclusion status.
- Ensure `./scripts/e2e_test.sh --all` includes this case (or mark non-default with justification).

## Acceptance Criteria
- The test is deterministic and safe to run in CI.
- Failures clearly identify which patcher step is not idempotent.


## Testing
- Meta-validation:
  - Add an explicit guard that the test never writes outside the temp home (assert all modified paths are under the temp root).
  - Include at least one “hostile fixture” variant (wezterm.lua already contains a partial WA block / malformed markers) to ensure patcher behavior is safe.
close_reason: Added setup_idempotency scenario to e2e_test.sh with temp home, idempotency checks, and artifacts

- systemd user services
- installs binaries/configs)

An E2E harness helps us ship confidently.

## Approach
- Use a dockerized sshd container as the "remote host".
- Run wa setup remote against it with:
  - dry-run mode
  - apply mode
  - idempotency verification (run twice)

## Safety constraints
- The harness must guarantee it only touches the container filesystem.
- Always run with verbose logging and produce artifacts.

## Assertions
- Remote install steps are idempotent.
- systemd user service unit file is created/updated as expected.
- Logs include clear step start/end markers and show any rollback path taken.

## Artifacts
- captured stdout/stderr
- remote filesystem snapshot (or tarball of touched paths)
- systemd unit contents

## Registry
- Register this case in the E2E case registry (`wa-4vx.10.20`), including prerequisites and default inclusion status.
- Ensure `./scripts/e2e_test.sh --all` includes this case (or mark non-default with justification).

## Acceptance Criteria
- The harness runs locally and in CI (where supported) without flakes.


## Testing
- Meta-validation:
  - Assert the harness refuses to run if the "remote host" is not clearly the docker container (avoid accidental real-host modification).
  - Add a failure-injection step (e.g., simulate missing package manager) and ensure rollback reporting is captured in artifacts.

## Docker for Mac Considerations
- Docker Desktop for Mac runs containers inside a Linux VM, which introduces subtle differences:
  - **Filesystem performance**: Bind mounts from the macOS host are slower; prefer named volumes or tmpfs for artifact collection inside the container.
  - **Port mapping**: Use `host.docker.internal` instead of `172.17.0.1` when the harness needs to reach the host from inside the container.
  - **Resource limits**: Docker Desktop defaults may be too low for concurrent sshd + setup operations; document minimum resource settings (2 CPU, 4 GB RAM).
  - **Socket paths**: Docker socket is at `/var/run/docker.sock` on Linux but may be at `~/.docker/run/docker.sock` on newer Docker Desktop versions; the harness should detect and adapt.
- The harness Dockerfile should use a multi-arch base image (e.g., `debian:bookworm-slim`) to work on both amd64 and arm64 (Apple Silicon).
- CI matrix should include both a native Linux runner and a macOS runner with Docker Desktop to catch platform-specific failures early.

## Cross-references
- **wa-brc7d.6** (wezterm-ssh asupersync migration): The remote setup harness validates the same SSH connectivity and remote file operations that the asupersync migration relies on. Ensure the dockerized sshd container configuration (auth methods, shell, PATH) mirrors the assumptions made by the asupersync SSH transport layer. Test fixtures from this harness can be reused to validate asupersync remote operations.

title: Idempotent wezterm.lua patch: user-var forwarding lane to wa
description:
# Task: Idempotent `wezterm.lua` patch (user-var forwarding lane)

## Goal
Automate installation of a small `wezterm.lua` snippet that forwards wa-related `user-var-changed` events to wa.

## Why
- OSC 133 markers are good, but user-vars give us an extra deterministic channel.
- Forwarding is necessary for future features (explicit checkpoints, prompt boundaries, "agent ready" signals).
- Humans should not need to copy/paste Lua.

## Minimal forwarding lane (PLAN Appendix E.1)
This is the exact minimal Lua we must be able to install idempotently:

```lua
-- Forward user-var events to wa daemon
wezterm.on('user-var-changed', function(window, pane, name, value)
  if name:match('^wa%-') then
    wezterm.background_child_process {
      'wa', 'event', '--from-uservar',
      '--pane', tostring(pane:pane_id()),
      '--name', name,
      '--value', value
    }
  end
end)
```

Notes:
- Prefix filter: default is `wa-` (hyphen). If we later support `wa_`, the filter must remain strict and configurable.
- The background child process must be non-blocking for WezTerm UI responsiveness.

## Approach
- `wa setup` locates the active `wezterm.lua`.
- It applies an idempotent patch:
  - insert snippet if missing
  - do nothing if already present
- It creates a backup copy (non-destructive).

## Forwarding lane contract
- We only forward vars matching the configured prefix.
- The Lua code calls:
  - `wa event --from-uservar --pane <id> --name <name> --value <value>`
- wa decodes base64 payloads where applicable and emits an internal signal/event.

## Deliverables
- Lua snippet template (managed block with WA-BEGIN/WA-END markers).
- WezTerm config locator.
- Idempotent patcher.

## Testing
- Unit/fixture tests (see `wa-nu4.3.3.5`):
  - patcher inserts exactly one managed block
  - re-running is a no-op
  - backups are created and paths are reported
- E2E:
  - `wa-nu4.3.3.10` validates end-to-end idempotency in a temp HOME
  - `wa-4vx.10.14` validates user-var events flow through the forwarding lane

## Acceptance Criteria
- Re-running `wa setup` does not duplicate the snippet.
- Manual review of the file shows only the intended additions.

title: Shell integration installer: enable OSC 133 prompt markers (bash/zsh/fish)
description:
# Task: Shell integration installer (OSC 133 markers)

## Goal
Provide a guided, idempotent way to enable OSC 133 prompt markers so wa can detect:
- prompt boundaries
- command start/end
- "pane is idle/ready" reliably

## Why
We want to avoid brittle heuristics that guess prompts based on `❯`/`$`.
OSC 133 is the robust path.

## Minimal marker emission (PLAN §4.6; illustrative)
The installer should ultimately produce equivalent semantics to:

```bash
# ~/.config/wa/shell-integration.bash (sourced by user's .bashrc)
__wa_prompt_start() { printf '\e]133;A\a'; }
__wa_command_start() { printf '\e]133;C\a'; }
__wa_command_end() { printf '\e]133;D;%s\a' "$?"; }
PROMPT_COMMAND='__wa_prompt_start'
trap '__wa_command_end' DEBUG  # Simplified; real impl must be more robust
```

Notes:
- This snippet is intentionally simplified in the plan; the real implementation must avoid breaking shells.
- The key requirement is emitting the correct OSC 133 sequences so wa can deterministically infer PromptActive/CommandRunning and exit codes.

## Approach
- `wa setup --shell` detects current shell (and can accept `--shell bash|zsh|fish`).
- Install minimal shell snippets into appropriate rc files:
  - `~/.bashrc`, `~/.zshrc`, `~/.config/fish/config.fish`
- Changes are idempotent and include a clear managed marker block.
- Always create a backup copy before modifying.

## Deliverables
- Shell snippet templates.
- Detection and idempotent patching logic.

## Testing
- Unit/fixture tests (see `wa-nu4.3.3.5`):
  - inserts exactly one managed block
  - re-running is a no-op
  - backups are created
- E2E:
  - `wa-nu4.3.3.10` validates idempotent patching in a temp HOME with artifacts

## Acceptance Criteria
- After setup, a sample interactive session emits OSC 133 markers.
- wa ingest sees those markers and updates deterministic state.
close_reason: Implemented OSC 133 prompt markers for bash/zsh/fish with idempotent patching and 13 unit tests

title: Remote setup spec: wezterm install, mux server service, wa install, safety/rollback
description:
# Task: Remote setup spec (`wa setup remote`)

## Goal
Define a robust, user-friendly remote bootstrap flow that makes WezTerm domains reliable:
- install WezTerm if missing
- run `wezterm-mux-server` as a user systemd service
- enable linger so the mux survives logout
- optionally install `wa` on the remote

## Why
A core user journey in the plan is:
> “Bring a new remote host online: install matching WezTerm, set up mux server, standardize config.”

## Safety requirements
- Must be **explicit** and non-surprising:
  - default to `--dry-run`
  - require confirmation for any operation that changes the remote host
- Must be **idempotent**:
  - re-run safely
  - detect existing installs/services
- Must be **observable**:
  - verbose logging and step timing
  - clear final summary with next steps

## Plan (proposed)
1. Choose host (from SSH config or explicit `--host`).
2. Verify connectivity.
3. Detect WezTerm presence + version.
4. If missing:
   - detect package manager (apt/dnf)
   - install WezTerm (documented script)
5. Install systemd user service unit for `wezterm-mux-server`.
6. `systemctl --user enable --now wezterm-mux-server`.
7. `loginctl enable-linger $USER` (requires sudo; explain).
8. Verify service is active.
9. Optionally scp `wa` binary to `~/.local/bin/wa`.

## Deliverables
- A written contract for:
  - CLI flags
  - what remote commands we run
  - what files we create
  - what errors we surface

## Testing
- Fixture-based tests:
  - covered by `wa-nu4.3.3.9` (dry-run plan output stability, command rendering, logging)

- E2E coverage:
  - covered by `wa-nu4.3.3.11` (dockerized sshd harness + artifacts + rollback safety)

## Acceptance Criteria
- A reviewer can implement remote setup from this issue without re-reading `PLAN.md`.
- The spec includes a rollback story (how to disable service / undo).

## Mission
Make it easy to answer "Is wa healthy?" and "Why did it do that?" without guesswork, including crash-only diagnostics.

- health snapshot plumbing from the watcher
- diagnostic bundle export (sanitized)

- performance budget checks in CI

## Deferred
- Incident/reproduce workflows are deferred until demand (see wa-upg.1).

## Testing & observability (non-negotiable)
Diagnostics tooling is only valuable if it is reliable and safe.

- Unit/integration tests must verify:
  - doctor checks against fixtures (no real WezTerm required)

  - redaction: bundles/logs never leak secrets

- E2E scripts must verify:

- `wa doctor`/`wa status` provide actionable health signals (DB connectivity, queue depths, ingest lag, lock state).

- Performance budgets exist for core hot paths and regressions are visible in CI.

# Task: Metrics endpoint (Prometheus)

## Goal
Expose optional Prometheus metrics to support long-running reliability:
- ingest lag
- gaps
- queue depths
- pattern detection latency
- workflow outcomes
- DB write latencies

## Design
- Disabled by default.
- Bind address configurable (default localhost).
- Must not significantly slow down hot path.

## Safety
- Default bind is localhost-only.
- Binding publicly requires an explicit, scary flag (proposed): `--dangerous-bind-any`.
- Metrics must never include transcript contents or secrets.

## Deliverables
- `wa watch --metrics <bind>` and/or config-driven enable.
- A minimal set of stable metric names.

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - metric names are stable
  - registry can be instantiated with metrics disabled (zero overhead path)

- Integration tests:
  - start watcher with metrics enabled (bind to localhost ephemeral port)
  - fetch `/metrics` and assert:
    - response is valid Prometheus text format
    - key metrics appear (even if counts are zero)

- Safety tests:
  - default bind is localhost
  - public bind requires `--dangerous-bind-any`
  - enabling metrics does not leak secrets

## Acceptance Criteria
- When enabled, `/metrics` responds with valid Prometheus text format.
- When disabled, zero overhead on hot path.

title: Doctor tests: fixture-based checks + output stability (JSON/TTY)
description:
# Task: `wa doctor` tests

## Goal
Make `wa doctor` a **trustworthy** and **regression-resistant** diagnostic surface.

`wa doctor` is how users decide whether to trust the tool. If it flakes, lies, or leaks secrets, we lose users.

## Test scope

### Unit tests
- Path resolution rendering (workspace root, DB/log/lock paths) is correct and deterministic.
- JSON output shape is stable (fields present, naming stable, no secret leakage).
- Redaction is applied to any potentially sensitive field (even on error paths).

### Integration tests (fixture-driven; no real WezTerm required)
Run `wa doctor` in a hermetic test environment that simulates:
- A healthy system.
- Missing `wezterm` binary / `wezterm cli list` failure.
- Workspace not writable.
- DB unreadable / schema mismatch.
- Watcher not running / lock held / stale lock.
- Optional feature checks present/absent (mcp/browser/web/tui) without forcing those deps.

## Test strategy / harness design
- Prefer dependency injection where feasible (traits) so we can simulate:
  - `wezterm` CLI calls
  - storage open/migration version
  - watcher health snapshot
- If process-based stubbing is simpler, use a test harness that:
  - writes a small “fake wezterm” executable to a temp dir
  - prepends that temp dir to `PATH`
  - feeds deterministic stdout/stderr for specific subcommands

## Output stability requirements
- Non-TTY mode:
  - `wa doctor --format json` must be strictly machine-parseable and stable.
  - Tests validate JSON against a versioned schema (if/when we add a schema for doctor output).
- TTY mode:
  - Tests validate key content (not exact ANSI art); either strip ANSI or snapshot a normalized rendering.

## Logging & debuggability
- Tests must capture logs on failure and print them (bounded) to make failures diagnosable.
- Ensure logs do not leak secrets (redaction applied to any dynamic content).

## Deliverables
- Unit test module(s) for doctor output + redaction.
- Integration test harness utilities for stubbing wezterm/storage/watcher.
- A small set of golden fixtures covering the major failure modes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `wa doctor` has coverage for each major check and for each major failure mode.
- Tests do not require:
  - network access
  - a real WezTerm instance
  - a real user home directory
- Adding a new doctor check requires adding at least one test covering both success and failure paths.

## Testing
- Meta-validation:
  - Ensure the integration harness actually uses the fake `wezterm` binary (assert invocation).
  - Add an explicit assertion that `--format json` output contains no ANSI escapes and validates against schema (once added).
close_reason: done

title: DB snapshot export (safe copy, WAL handling, size checks)
description:
# Task: DB snapshot export

## Goal
Allow exporting the wa SQLite database as a portable artifact for backup/debugging.

This supports:
- user self-service bug reports
- deterministic repro bundles
- safe backups for long-running watcher instances

## Safety requirements
- Must not corrupt or block the live DB.
- Must handle WAL mode correctly.
  - Prefer SQLite backup API (consistent snapshot) or a safe `VACUUM INTO` style approach.
  - If checkpointing is used, do it intentionally and document the tradeoffs.
- Must validate output size and warn if unexpectedly large.
- Must never include secrets beyond what already exists in the DB (and DB should already be redacted where required).

## Deliverables
- A human-facing entrypoint (name flexible):
  - `wa export db-snapshot --out <path>`
  - (or `wa export --db <path>`)
- Optional compression (feature-gated) for large snapshots.
- A short metadata sidecar (optional) that includes:
  - wa version
  - schema version
  - created_at
  - workspace id/path (redacted)

## Logging / UX
- Progress logs (bounded, non-spammy):
  - starting snapshot
  - checkpoint/backup method chosen
  - bytes written
  - completion path
- On failure: actionable error + suggestion to run `wa diag bundle`.

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - output path validation (no directory traversal)
  - metadata rendering (if implemented)

- Integration tests:
  - create a temp DB with known rows
  - run snapshot export
  - open exported DB read-only and verify expected tables/rows exist
  - verify WAL handling does not leave a corrupt or partial snapshot

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exported DB can be opened read-only and contains expected tables.
- Export is safe while watcher is running (no corruption; bounded blocking).
- Failures are actionable and do not leak secrets in logs.

title: Web server hardening: localhost-only default, explicit bind, no secret leakage
description:
# Task: Web server hardening (safe-by-default)

## Goal
Ensure the optional `wa web` server is safe-by-default and hard to misuse.

## Threat model
Even “read-only” endpoints can leak:
- terminal transcripts (may contain secrets)
- tokens embedded in URLs
- hostnames, paths, and other sensitive metadata

So the web server must inherit wa’s redaction and safety conventions.

## Requirements
- **Bind defaults**
  - default bind: `127.0.0.1`
  - require an explicit, scary flag to bind publicly (proposed): `--dangerous-bind-any`
  - when binding non-localhost, print a prominent warning

- **No secret leakage**
  - all responses must be redacted using the same redaction pipeline as robot/audit/export
  - never include raw segment bytes by default

- **Hard limits**
  - request size limits
  - sensible default pagination limits

- **Surface area**
  - only GET endpoints in v0
  - no file-serving
  - no CORS-by-default (unless explicitly enabled)

## Testing strategy
- `cargo test --features web` includes cases that assert:
  - localhost bind is the default
  - public bind requires `--dangerous-bind-any`
  - redaction is applied to responses for any field that can contain secrets

## Acceptance Criteria
- A naive `wa web` run is not remotely reachable by default.
- Redaction is applied consistently (web == robot == audit == export).

title: [EPIC] Optional TUI (charmed_rust): pane picker + event feed + transcript viewer
description:
# [EPIC] Interactive TUI Dashboard

## Mission
Transform wa from an invisible background daemon into a **visible control center** with a real-time dashboard showing panes, events, workflows, and health metrics.

## Why This Is Transformative
Terminal automation is inherently opaque. Users cannot see what wa is doing. The TUI changes this fundamentally:

**Before TUI:**
- "I hope it is working"
- "I need to check logs to see what happened"
- "I do not know if the workflow succeeded"

**After TUI:**
- "I can watch everything happening in real-time"
- "I see the workflow progressing step by step"
- "I know immediately when something needs attention"

## TUI Layout Vision
```
┌─ WA Dashboard ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Panes (4 observed, 1 ignored)                                        │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ● Pane 1 [codex]     Idle ▪ PromptActive    │ Last: 2m ago          │
│ ● Pane 3 [claude]    Running ▪ CommandActive │ Last: 5s ago          │
│ ○ Pane 5 [local]     Ignored (exclude rule) │                        │
│ ● Pane 7 [gemini]    Idle ▪ PromptActive    │ Last: 30s ago         │
│ ⚠ Pane 9 [codex]     UsageLimitReached      │ Last: 1s ago          │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Events (recent)                                              [e] more │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 14:32:01 ⚠ codex.usage_limit_reached    Pane 9  → workflow started  │
│ 14:31:45 ○ session.compaction           Pane 3  → handled           │
│ 14:30:12 ○ codex.session_summary        Pane 1  → no workflow       │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Workflows                                                            │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ▶ handle_usage_limits (Pane 9)  Step 3/7: Selecting account...      │
│   [████████░░░░░░░░░░░░] 42%                                         │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Health: ● OK  │ Queue: 0  │ Lag: 12ms  │ DB: 1.2GB                   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
[q]uit [p]anes [e]vents [w]orkflows [t]imeline [s]earch [h]elp
```

## Core Views

### 1. Panes Panel
- List all panes with state indicators
- Color-coded status (green=healthy, yellow=warning, red=error)
- Filter: observed/ignored, by agent type
- Select to inspect: show recent output tail, events, actions

### 2. Events Feed
- Real-time event stream
- Severity coloring (info/warning/error)
- Filter: unhandled, by type, by pane
- Select to view details and quick-fix suggestions

### 3. Workflow Progress
- Active workflows with step-by-step progress
- Progress bars and estimated completion
- Expand to see step logs
- Cancel button for stuck workflows

### 4. Health Metrics
- Overall system status
- Queue depths and lag
- DB size and write status
- Circuit breaker states

### 5. Timeline View
- Interactive scrollable timeline
- Cross-pane event correlation
- Zoom in/out on time ranges

### 6. Search/Transcript View
- FTS query interface
- Snippet display with highlighting
- Navigate to context around matches

## Keyboard Navigation
```
Tab / Shift-Tab : Move between panels
Arrow keys      : Navigate within panel
Enter           : Select/expand item
Escape          : Back / collapse
q               : Quit
?               : Help
```

## Implementation

### Framework
Use `ratatui` (successor to tui-rs) with `crossterm` backend:
- Cross-platform (macOS, Linux, Windows)
- Full Unicode support
- Mouse support (optional)

### Architecture
```
wa tui
  ├── App (main loop)
  │     ├── EventBus subscriber (real-time updates)
  │     └── Query client (same as CLI)
  ├── Widgets
  │     ├── PanesPanel
  │     ├── EventsPanel
  │     ├── WorkflowsPanel
  │     ├── HealthPanel
  │     ├── TimelineView
  │     └── SearchView
  └── State management (Redux-like)
```

### Feature Flag
`--features tui` to keep binary size down for headless deployments.

## Testing
- Unit tests: Widget rendering with mock data
- State tests: Verify state transitions
- Integration tests: Event subscription works
- Manual tests: Keyboard navigation, responsiveness

## Success Criteria
- TUI launches with `wa tui` and shows real-time dashboard
- All panels update in real-time as events occur
- Keyboard navigation is intuitive and documented
- Performance: <50ms render time, <100MB memory
- Accessibility: Works with screen readers (basic)

## Acceptance Criteria
- TUI launches reliably behind feature flag.
- Pane picker, event feed, and transcript viewer work with live data.
- Workflow and health panels render without crashes.

title: TUI scaffolding (charmed_rust): feature flag + app skeleton + shared query client
description:
# Task: TUI scaffolding (charmed_rust, feature tui)

## Goal
Create an **optional** interactive UI entrypoint: `wa tui`, behind `--features tui`, that provides a foundation for panes/events/search views.

The purpose of this bead is the **app skeleton** and **data access architecture**, not the final UX polish.

## Architecture (critical: keep UI dumb)
- Implement a small TUI app framework layer (initial screen router + event loop).
- Define a `QueryClient` trait (exact name flexible) used by the TUI:
  - `list_panes()`
  - `list_events(filters)`
  - `search(query)`
- Provide a production implementation backed by existing wa query surfaces:
  - prefer calling the same internal query/model layer that powers `wa robot ...`
  - never query SQLite directly from UI widgets

This separation is what makes the TUI testable and prevents “UI spaghetti + DB coupling”.

## UX baseline (v0)
- Global keybindings:
  - `q` quit
  - `?` help
  - `r` refresh
  - `tab` / `shift+tab` switch views (or a visible nav)
- Clear empty/error states:
  - watcher not running
  - DB not reachable
  - permission/policy denied

## Logging & diagnostics
- Use the structured logging baseline (tracing spans) so TUI bugs can be debugged.
- Avoid logging transcript contents; log counts/ids and redacted summaries only.

## Testing strategy
- `cargo test --features tui` includes:
  - unit tests for the view-model/reducer (state transitions) using a fake `QueryClient`
  - snapshot tests for non-ANSI text render helpers (headers/rows formatting)

## Acceptance Criteria
- `wa tui` starts and shows a placeholder screen with nav + help.
- The app uses a shared query client abstraction (no direct DB calls from views).
- Basic error states render cleanly (e.g., “watcher not running”).

description:
# Task: TUI panes view

## Goal
Provide an interactive pane picker that makes it fast to answer:
- “Which pane is my agent running in?”
- “Is it at a prompt or mid-command?”
- “Which panes have unhandled events?”

This is the TUI equivalent of `wa status` + quick drill-down.

## Data contract
Back the view via the shared query layer / robot state model:
- pane id
- domain + workspace
- title + cwd
- inferred agent type (Codex/Claude/Gemini/unknown)
- inferred pane state (PromptActive/CommandRunning/AltScreen/unknown)
- last segment/event timestamp
- unhandled event count (if available)

## UX requirements
- List view:
  - stable columns and readable truncation
  - highlights for “needs attention” (unhandled events / alt-screen / gaps)
- Filtering:
  - free-text filter on title/cwd/domain
  - quick toggles: unhandled-only, agent filter, domain filter
- Selection details:
  - show a detail panel with full fields
  - show “next best actions” hints (e.g., suggest `wa workflow …` when unhandled events exist)

## Performance constraints
- Must handle hundreds of panes without lag.
- Prefer incremental updates (refresh tick) rather than re-rendering everything per keystroke.

## Testing strategy
- Unit tests (feature `tui`) using a fake `QueryClient`:
  - filtering logic correctness
  - sort order stability
  - selection state transitions
  - large list performance sanity (no quadratic behavior in reducer)

## Acceptance Criteria
- User can filter panes and select one.
- Details panel shows basic info (title/cwd/state/last_activity/unhandled_count).
- The view remains responsive with a large synthetic pane list.

title: [EPIC] Optional sync (asupersync): configs/binaries/DB snapshots
description:
# [EPIC] Optional sync (asupersync)

## Mission
Support syncing wa artifacts across machines:
- wa binary
- config files
- DB snapshots / exports

## Why
Even in single-user setups, people often have:
- desktop + laptop
- local + remote build box

Sync makes wa more practical and reduces setup drift.

## Principles
- Feature-gated (`--features sync`).
- Prefer explicit sync operations (no surprise background rsync).
- Treat DB snapshots as immutable artifacts.

## Definition of done
- `wa sync push` and `wa sync pull` can sync a configured set of paths.


## Success Criteria
- Sync spec defines what may be synced (configs/binaries/db snapshots) and what is forbidden; defaults are safe.
- Sync operations are opt-in, transparent, and produce clear logs/artifacts.
- Tests validate path selection rules and prevent accidental secret exfiltration.


## Testing
- Safety tests:
  - Ensure forbidden paths are never synced by default (e.g., credentials).

- Dry-run output stability:
  - `wa sync --dry-run` must produce deterministic output so users can trust it.

- E2E (optional):
  - Use a local temp “remote dir” or container to simulate push/pull and validate artifacts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All items in the following sections are satisfied: Success Criteria, Definition of Done.
- All Testing requirements pass (unit/integration/E2E) with the logging/artifacts described above.
- Any explicit dependencies for this bead are implemented and validated via tests or E2E artifacts.

title: Sync spec: what to sync, safety rules, remote targets (asupersync)
description:
# Task: Sync spec (asupersync)

## Goal
Define a safe, explicit sync contract.

## What to sync (initial)
- `wa` binary (optional)
- `~/.config/wa/` (config)
- exported DB snapshots (not live DB)

## Safety rules
- No overwriting without explicit confirmation.
- Prefer versioned snapshot filenames.
- Never sync secrets (or redact before sync).

## Deliverables
- Config fields for sync targets.
- Documented rules for push vs pull.



## Acceptance Criteria
- The sync contract clearly defines:
  - what may be synced (binary/config/snapshots)
  - what must never be synced (live DB, secrets)
  - push vs pull semantics
  - safety prompts/confirmation requirements
- Config fields exist to express sync targets and safety defaults (schema + examples).
- Threat model / safety rules are explicit enough that implementers can build `wa sync` without ambiguity.
- Tests (for the eventual implementation) are called out explicitly: path selection rules, redaction enforcement, and "no overwrite without confirmation" semantics.


## Testing
- Spec-to-implementation tests to require:
  - Path allow/deny lists are enforced.
  - Dry-run output is stable.
  - Overwrite attempts require explicit confirmation and are logged/audited.

title: [Human command] `wa sync` scaffolding (feature sync, asupersync wiring)
description:
# Task: `wa sync` scaffolding (feature sync)

## Goal
Introduce a **safe-by-default** `wa sync` command surface behind `--features sync`, wired to `asupersync`, without committing us to any risky behavior.

This bead is intentionally about **CLI contract + wiring**. The actual file movement logic (configs/binaries/snapshots) lives in follow-on beads.

## CLI surface (v0)
- `wa sync status`
  - show configured targets
  - show what categories are enabled (config, binary, snapshots)

- `wa sync push [--target <name>] [--dry-run] [--apply]`
- `wa sync pull [--target <name>] [--dry-run] [--apply]`

## Safety & UX principles
- `push`/`pull` should be **non-destructive by default**.
  - Prefer `--dry-run` as the default behavior, or require `--apply` to actually change files.
  - When changes would overwrite local/remote files, require an explicit confirmation gate.

- Output modes:
  - TTY: human plan view (tables/panels, clear warnings)
  - non-TTY: stable JSON plan output (sorted, schema-stable)

- Explicitly explain what is *not* synced:
  - live SQLite DB (only exported snapshots)
  - any secret material

## Integration details
- Feature-gate all code (`cfg(feature = "sync")`).
- Load sync configuration via the normal config system (do not invent a parallel config loader).
- Implement a minimal abstraction around the transport so tests can run offline:
  - local directory backend for integration tests
  - (future) SSH backend

## Acceptance Criteria
- `wa sync status` runs and shows configured targets and enabled categories.
- `wa sync push --dry-run` and `wa sync pull --dry-run` run end-to-end and print a plan without making changes.
- The command surfaces a clear warning that live DB files are never synced (snapshots only).


## Testing
- Integration tests:
  - Use a local-dir backend to simulate push/pull and assert:
    - `--dry-run` makes no changes
    - `--apply` makes only the intended changes
    - overwrite attempts require explicit confirmation

- Output tests:
  - `--format json` plan is schema-stable and sorted.

title: Sync push/pull for config + binary (explicit, non-destructive)
description:
# Task: Sync push/pull for config + binary (feature sync)

## Goal
Implement the core sync operations for:
- `~/.config/wa/**` (config)
- optional `wa` binary (explicit opt-in)

The intent is to make it easy to keep multiple machines consistent **without ever surprising the user**.

## Design principles
- **Explicitness over magic**: no background sync; only `push`/`pull`.
- **Plan-first**: always compute and display a plan; require `--apply` for real changes.
- **No silent overwrites**: overwriting requires confirmation and clear diff metadata.
- **Secret-aware**: never sync forbidden paths; never print secret contents.

## Path selection rules
- Config root is the canonical wa config directory.
- Include only known-safe config artifacts.
- Exclude patterns like:
  - `**/.env*`
  - `**/*token*`
  - `**/*secret*`
  - keychains/SSH keys

(Exact allow/deny rules are authored in the sync spec bead; this bead implements them.)

## Conflict semantics
When both sides changed:
- classify as `Conflict` and refuse to apply automatically
- provide remediation:
  - show which file conflicted
  - suggest manual resolution steps
  - (future) offer an interactive merge/choose-side mode

## Binary sync
- Treat binary sync as a separate category:
  - opt-in in config
  - prefer syncing from a trusted build machine to others
- Validate binary integrity (hash/size) before replacing.

## Testing
- Covered by `wa-nu4.3.8.5` (sync tests):
  - offline push/pull planning and dry-run output stability
  - conflict classification (no silent overwrite)
  - secret/path deny rules

## Acceptance Criteria
- `wa sync push/pull` computes a deterministic plan for config + binary categories.
- `--dry-run` never modifies local or remote files.
- Applying changes requires `--apply` and refuses to overwrite without explicit confirmation.
- Conflicts are detected and surfaced as `Conflict` items (no auto-overwrite).

title: Sync exported DB snapshots (immutable artifacts, versioned filenames)
description:
# Task: Sync exported DB snapshots (immutable artifacts)

## Goal
Make it easy to move **database snapshots** between machines for debugging or continuity, without ever touching the live DB file.

## Safety model
- Only sync snapshots created via `wa export` / `wa diag bundle` (explicit export paths).
- Never sync the live DB file or WAL/SHM.
- Treat snapshots as immutable artifacts:
  - versioned filenames
  - no in-place overwrite
  - optional compression (if/when supported by export)

## Naming & versioning
- Filenames should encode enough metadata to be self-describing:
  - wa version
  - created timestamp (UTC)
  - workspace key (hashed/short)
  - optional host

## Push/pull behavior
- `push` uploads snapshot(s) to the target under an artifacts directory.
- `pull` downloads snapshots and places them under a local artifacts directory.
- Default behavior is additive (no overwrites).

## UX expectations
- Plans should clearly distinguish:
  - “syncing snapshots” (safe)
  - “syncing live DB” (forbidden; should never appear)

## Testing
- Covered by `wa-nu4.3.8.5` (sync tests):
  - live DB paths are rejected
  - snapshot filenames are stable and never overwritten
  - push/pull round-trips via local-directory backend

## Acceptance Criteria
- `wa sync push` can push an exported snapshot to a target without overwriting existing files.
- `wa sync pull` can pull the same snapshot back and preserves the filename.
- Attempts to sync live DB paths are rejected by the planner.

title: Sync tests: config diffing + dry-run output stability (feature sync)
description:
# Task: Sync tests (feature sync)

## Goal
Make `wa sync` safe and boring by locking down:
- **path selection rules** (what may sync vs must never sync)
- **plan generation** (what would happen)
- **dry-run output stability** (humans + automation can trust it)

Sync is inherently risky: it touches configs and binaries, and can easily become a secret-exfiltration or accidental-overwrite footgun. Tests are the safety net.

## Scope
- Unit + integration tests that run **offline** and **deterministically**.
- No real SSH, no real remote machines, no real secrets.

## Test strategy
### 1) Pure unit tests (no filesystem required)
- **Path allow/deny rules**
  - allow: `~/.config/wa/**` (except explicit denylist)
  - allow (optional): `wa` binary (explicit opt-in)
  - deny: any known secret file patterns (tokens, keyrings, `.env`, etc.)
- **Target resolution**
  - parse configured sync targets
  - explicit “default target” selection rules
  - stable ordering (targets and files are sorted deterministically)
- **Planning semantics**
  - classify changes as `Add` / `Update` / `Skip` / `Conflict`
  - ensure “would overwrite” requires an explicit confirmation gate

### 2) Filesystem integration tests (temp dirs)
- Build a temp “local” tree and a temp “remote” tree (local-directory transport backend).
- Exercise:
  - `push --dry-run` produces a plan but changes nothing
  - `pull --dry-run` produces a plan but changes nothing
  - “same content” yields a minimal/no-op plan
  - “different content” yields Update items (but still requires confirmation in non-dry-run)

### 3) Golden tests for dry-run output stability
- Snapshot the **dry-run plan output** (both modes):
  - TTY-ish human format (no ANSI in tests; use the plain renderer)
  - machine JSON format (stable schema + stable ordering)
- The golden tests should assert:
  - stable ordering of files/targets
  - stable wording for safety warnings
  - redaction is applied to any values that might contain secrets

## Logging & debuggability requirements
- Tests should capture and assert a few critical log lines:
  - which target selected
  - how many items in plan
  - whether an overwrite would have occurred
- Log output must never include file contents or secret values.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `cargo test --features sync` includes deterministic tests that cover:
  - path selection allow/deny rules (including a “secret-ish” fixture)
  - plan generation for push + pull (no-op, update, conflict)
  - dry-run output stability (goldens/snapshots)
- Tests are fully offline (no SSH/network), fast, and reproducible.
- A regression that would accidentally sync a forbidden path fails loudly.


## Testing
- Meta-validation:
  - Add an explicit assertion that no files are modified in dry-run tests (e.g., hash trees before/after).
  - Include at least one fixture that resembles a secret and ensure it is denied and never appears in output.

title: [EPIC] Ship readiness: docs, CI checks, release workflow, versioning
description:
# [EPIC] Ship readiness (docs + CI + release)

## Mission
Make v0.1.0 shippable:
- clear docs
- reliable CI signals
- predictable version/build metadata

## Why
A tool that controls terminals needs high trust and clear operator UX.

## Definition of done
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo test` pass in CI.
- README + quickstart lets another engineer install and run wa.
- Version/build metadata is visible (`wa --version`).

## Success Criteria
- CI runs fmt/clippy/tests/e2e reliably and preserves artifacts on failure.
- Release workflow/versioning produces reproducible binaries with build metadata.
- Docs/README/quickstart are sufficient for a new contributor to install and run wa.

## Testing
- CI verification:
  - CI must run the full quality gate (fmt/clippy/tests) and E2E, and upload artifacts on failure.

- Release smoke tests:
  - After packaging, run `wa --version` and `wa --help` and a minimal `wa doctor --format json` scenario to ensure the binary is functional.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All items in the following sections are satisfied: Success Criteria, Definition of Done.
- All Testing requirements pass (unit/integration/E2E) with the logging/artifacts described above.
- Any explicit dependencies for this bead are implemented and validated via tests or E2E artifacts.

## Cross-references
- **wa-vv3h** (Rename project): Ship readiness depends on the final project name being settled. CI workflows, binary names, crate names, and documentation must all reflect the chosen name. Coordinate timing so that the rename lands before or as part of the v0.1.0 release to avoid publishing under a temporary name. README, quickstart, and `wa --version` output must use the canonical project name.

## CI: macOS + Linux Coverage
- CI matrix MUST include both macOS and Linux runners for the full quality gate:
  - `cargo fmt --check` (platform-independent, but verify).
  - `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` on both platforms to catch platform-conditional compilation warnings.
  - `cargo test` on both platforms to catch any `#[cfg(target_os)]` divergences.
  - E2E tests on Linux (Docker-native) and macOS (Docker Desktop) where Docker is required.
- Release binaries must be built for both `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `aarch64-apple-darwin` (Apple Silicon) at minimum, with `x86_64-apple-darwin` as a stretch target.
- Platform-specific smoke tests: verify `wa setup` handles launchd (macOS) vs systemd (Linux) correctly in CI for each platform.

title: release build.rs: honor SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH for FT_BUILD_TS / FT_GIT_DIRTY so release.yml reproducibility env actually works
description:
## Bug

release.yml:65 sets `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH: "0"` to signal reproducible builds, but crates/frankenterm/build.rs:32-39 calls `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` which reads wall-clock and ignores the env var. Same commit built on two different days produces different `FT_BUILD_TS` → different binary hashes → SHA256SUMS diverge for identical source state.

`FT_GIT_DIRTY` (build.rs:17-29) has a similar issue: depends on working-tree state, not commit content.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `git checkout <tag>`
2. `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0 cargo build --release -p frankenterm`
3. Wait a second. Repeat.
4. `sha256sum target/release/ft` — hashes differ.

## Fix path

In crates/frankenterm/build.rs:

- If `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` is set, format that epoch as UTC ISO8601 for `FT_BUILD_TS` instead of calling `date -u`.
- Either skip `git status --porcelain` entirely in reproducible mode, or gate `FT_GIT_DIRTY` on commit-level truth only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Two back-to-back builds from the same commit with `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0` produce identical `ft` binaries on the same host/toolchain.
- `ft version --full` still shows a meaningful timestamp (the SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH-derived one).

## Testing

- Add a one-shot check script or CI step that builds twice with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0 and diffs the resulting binary hashes.

## Scope note

Requires editing crates/frankenterm/build.rs which is outside the current release-plumbing agent's scope — flagging for a code-scope agent. Surfaced by wa-nu4.3.9.15 release workflow audit (commit 83acd334).
close_reason: build.rs now honors SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (landed in 4d251588). When set: FT_BUILD_TS is derived from the epoch via GNU 'date -d @<e>' / BSD 'date -r <e>' with a 4-digit-year sanity check and epoch:<n> fallback; FT_GIT_DIRTY is forced empty regardless of working-tree state. Preserves the existing YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ format so main.rs consumers and tests are unaffected. Added cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH. Verified: rustc --edition 2024 standalone parse=0, runtime sanity on macOS showed correct ISO8601 conversion for 0/1700000000/1735689600 and safe fallback for invalid input. Full cross-build verification (two builds produce identical binaries) is an acceptance item for a separate CI gate.

title: release.yml: add SLSA build provenance attestation for published artifacts
description:
## Gap

AGENTS.md §Release Profile (L136-147) does NOT currently require signing, so strictly there's no DoD miss. But the wa-nu4.3.9 mission says 'A tool that controls terminals needs high trust.' Release artifacts currently ship with SHA256 checksums (release.yml:89/99/136) but no cryptographic provenance — a user can't verify an artifact was actually produced by this repo's workflow vs tampered in transit.

## Fix path (in-scope for workflow-only agent)

Add to `.github/workflows/release.yml` `release` job:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: write
  id-token: write        # for sigstore OIDC token
  attestations: write    # for provenance upload
```

Add a step after download-artifact, before softprops/action-gh-release:

```yaml
- name: Generate SLSA build provenance attestations
  uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@v2
  with:
    subject-path: |
      dist/*.tar.xz
      dist/*.zip
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- `gh attestation verify <artifact> --owner Dicklesworthstone` succeeds against a post-change release.
- No change to artifact naming, checksum publishing, or release notes.

## Testing

- `workflow_dispatch` the release workflow against a sacrificial tag; confirm attestations appear under the Releases page sigstore bundle and `gh attestation verify` passes.

## Why P3

Nice-to-have, not in AGENTS.md Release Profile DoD. Surfaced by wa-nu4.3.9.15 audit.
close_reason: Landed 325054be to add GitHub artifact build provenance attestation in release.yml: release job now has id-token/attestations permissions and runs actions/attest@v4 over dist/*.tar.xz and dist/*.zip before publishing. Verified with YAML parse and git diff --check; live workflow_dispatch/gh attestation verify remains follow-up runtime proof.

title: CI: version-smoke job asserts ft --version + ft version --full output shape (ubuntu + macos)
description:
## Gap

README Quickstart (bcc668a0) claims `ft --version` emits semver+short-git and `ft version --full` emits commit/built/rustc/target/features. Without a CI assertion on the actual binary output, a future build.rs change or clap wiring edit can silently break that claim — exactly the regression ft-b4mif surfaced.

release.yml:68-80 runs those commands at tag time but doesn't assert their output; ci.yml runs unit tests on build_meta functions but never exercises the real binary.

## Deliverable

New `version-smoke` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that:

1. Depends on `build` (reuses the release binaries it already produces).
2. Downloads the `ft-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `ft-aarch64-apple-darwin` artifacts on matching runners.
3. Asserts `ft --version` output contains semver and a commit hash in parens.
4. Asserts `ft version --full` output contains semver header, `commit:` (7-40 hex or `unknown`), `built:` (ISO8601 / `epoch:<n>` / `unknown`), and `rustc:`/`target:`/`features:` fields.

Matrix over `ubuntu-latest` + `macos-14` to catch platform-conditional regressions.

## Acceptance

- New job visible in Actions tab under ci.yml.
- Runs in < 2min (no rebuild, only download + execute).
- No `continue-on-error`.
- Fails loudly with a specific error pointer when any assertion misses.
close_reason: version-smoke CI job landed in 176d89b6. Reuses release binaries from the existing build job (ft-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu on ubuntu-latest, ft-aarch64-apple-darwin on macos-14) via download-artifact@v4, locates the binary with a find step that tolerates upload-artifact path-preservation behavior, then runs both 'ft --version' and 'ft version --full' with specific ::error:: assertions for semver / commit-in-parens / header / commit field / built field (ISO8601|epoch:n|unknown) / rustc / target / features. fail-fast:false across the 2-platform matrix. All regexes verified locally against the expected output shape. Protects the README Quickstart claim (bcc668a0) and the ft-b4mif fix from future drift.

title: [follow-up ft-tczj7] Find serde-reject slip payload that reaches FT-MCP-0001 tool envelope
description:
## Context

ft-tczj7 fixed (in commit TBD): added `assert_tool_invalid_args_envelope_shape` to mcp_conformance_core_tools.rs that fences the FT-MCP-0001 tool-level envelope contract, plus a synthetic unit test that exercises the helper against a reference envelope.

What's still missing: a LIVE test that feeds a real-world payload through `harness.client.call_tool(...)`, slips past framework schema validation, triggers the serde_json::from_value failure at mcp_tools.rs:1025/1216/1387/1940, and lands on the helper assertion.

## Two acceptable outcomes

1. **Slip exists.** Add one regression test per tool (wa.search / wa.get_text / wa.send / wa.wait_for) that calls `assert_tool_invalid_args_envelope_shape` on the real framework response. FT-MCP-0001 fenced live.
2. **No slip exists.** Framework schema validation supersedes the tool-level serde-reject path for all four tools. Remove the defensive branches in mcp_tools.rs (:1025, :1216, :1387, :1940 — and any other tools with the same pattern) as dead code. Update the helper doc-comment to reflect that FT-MCP-0001 is now only emitted by intra-handler paths, not the top-level serde guard.

## Candidate slip payloads to try

- JSON integer > u64::MAX — whether serde_json parses it as f64 and whether the framework's JSON Schema `type: integer` validator catches that depends on which schema lib fastmcp uses.
- Integer-valued float (`1.0`) where a field is `type: integer` — some validators accept, some don't.
- Null for an optional field typed `Option<T>` where T deserialize itself rejects default — unlikely.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Either a merged test that exercises assert_tool_invalid_args_envelope_shape against a live framework response,
- OR a merged diff that removes the dead defensive branches in mcp_tools.rs with the helper doc-comment updated to match.
close_reason: Committed in 8d1e93dc with partial verification only: removed dead core-tool serde guards and updated the synthetic FT-MCP-0001 helper docs after live framework InvalidParams probes.

title: Docs: README/quickstart + architecture + CLI/robot/MCP reference
description:
# Task: Documentation for v0.1

## Goal
Make the project approachable for a new contributor and operable for users.

This bead is intentionally self-contained and mirrors PLAN Appendix A + F so contributors don’t need to dig through planning docs.

## Deliverables
### 1) README (operator-first)
- What wa is (WezTerm mux “terminal hypervisor” for agent fleets).
- Quickstart:
  - install wa
  - `wa setup`
  - `wa watch`
  - `wa status`
  - `wa query` / `wa events`
- Safety guarantees:
  - observe vs act split
  - no silent gaps
  - policy-gated sending + approvals

### 2) Architecture doc
- Ingest → Storage (SQLite+FTS5) → Pattern engine → Workflow engine → Robot/MCP.
- Deterministic state via OSC 133.
- Explicit GAP semantics.

### 3) CLI reference (PLAN Appendix A)
Human-oriented commands (rich output by default via `rich_rust`):
- `wa status` — panes + inferred agent state
- `wa watch` — run daemon (foreground/background)
- `wa stop` — stop watcher in workspace safely
- `wa events` — recent/unhandled events
- `wa query` — FTS search
- `wa send` — guarded send to a pane
- `wa reserve` — reserve a pane for exclusive use
- `wa reservations` — list active reservations
- `wa approve` — grant allow-once approvals
- `wa workflow` — run a workflow manually (guarded)
- `wa audit` — audit trail of actions (redacted)
- `wa history` — action timeline + undoability
- `wa undo` — undo supported actions (with confirmation)
- `wa rules` — list/test rule packs, show matching traces
- `wa accounts` — list/refresh accounts, show rotation picks
- `wa setup` — canonical WezTerm configuration (local/remote)
- `wa doctor` — environment checks (wezterm presence, DB health)
- `wa diag bundle` — sanitized diagnostic bundle export
- `wa export` — export slices/history/audit
- `wa web` — optional HTTP server (`fastapi_rust`) if enabled
- `wa tui` — optional TUI (`charmed_rust`) if enabled
- `wa sync` — optional sync (`asupersync`) if enabled

Robot mode commands (stable JSON envelope; token-efficient):
- `wa robot state [--domain <name>] [--agent <type>]`
- `wa robot get-text <pane_id> [--tail N] [--escapes]`
- `wa robot send <pane_id> "<text>" [--no-newline] [--wait-for "<pat>"] [--timeout-secs N]`
- `wa robot wait-for <pane_id> "<pat>" [--timeout-secs N]`
- `wa robot search "<fts query>" [--pane-id <id>] [--since <iso8601>] [--limit N]`
- `wa robot events [--unhandled] [--pane-id <id>] [--type <event>] [--limit N]`
- `wa robot workflow <name> <pane_id> [--force]`
- `wa robot reserve <pane_id> --ttl <secs> --reason <text>`
- `wa robot release <pane_id>`
- `wa robot reservations`
- `wa robot accounts [--service <openai|anthropic|google>]`
- `wa robot accounts refresh [--service <openai|anthropic|google>]`
- `wa robot rules list [--pack <name>]`
- `wa robot rules test "<text>" [--agent <type>]`
- `wa robot quick-start`

### 4) MCP reference (PLAN Appendix A)
Tools (names are short and obvious):
- `wa.state`
- `wa.get_text`
- `wa.send`
- `wa.wait_for`
- `wa.search`
- `wa.events`
- `wa.workflow_run`
- `wa.accounts`
- `wa.accounts_refresh`
- `wa.rules_list`
- `wa.rules_test`
- `wa.reserve`
- `wa.release`
- `wa.reservations`

Resources:
- `wa://panes`
- `wa://events`
- `wa://accounts`
- `wa://workflows`
- `wa://rules`
- `wa://reservations`

### 5) Library integration map (PLAN Appendix F)
| Library | Role in `wa` |
|---------|--------------|
| `cass` (`/dp/coding_agent_session_search`) | Correlation + session archaeology; used in status + workflows |
| `caut` (`/dp/coding_agent_usage_tracker`) | Usage truth + selection; used in accounts + `handle_usage_limits` |
| `rich_rust` | Human-first CLI output (tables/panels/highlight) |
| `charmed_rust` | Optional interactive TUI (pane picker, event feed, transcript viewer) |
| `fastmcp_rust` | MCP tool surface for agent control (mirrors robot mode) |
| `fastapi_rust` | Optional HTTP server for dashboards/webhooks (read-only first) |
| `asupersync` | Remote bootstrap/sync layer (configs, binaries, DB snapshots) |
| `playwright` | Automate device auth flows with persistent profiles |
| `ast-grep` | Structure-aware codebase scans in “unstick agent” workflows |

## Testing / doc correctness
Docs must not drift.

- The quickstart commands shown in README should be validated regularly:
  - either by referencing existing E2E scripts, or
  - by adding a small “docs smoke” CI step that runs the exact commands from the docs in a controlled environment (tracked by `wa-nu4.3.9.9`).

- Robot mode docs should match the schema contract:
  - reference the versioned JSON schemas and keep field names consistent.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A new engineer can get to a running watcher and see events with no oral tradition.
- CLI/robot/MCP references match implemented command surfaces and schemas.
close_reason: Added docs/cli-reference.md with human/robot/MCP command matrix, feature-gated/planned notes, and MCP tool/resource list

title: [wa-nu4.3.9 blocker] CI concurrency cancel-in-progress makes green CI on main unobservable during swarm sessions
description:
## Problem
.github/workflows/ci.yml declares:
```
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```
With swarm sessions producing 1+ pushes/min to main and CI taking 15-30+ min, every run is cancelled before completion. Workflow_dispatch uses the same `github.ref` (refs/heads/main), so manually triggered runs are also cancelled by subsequent swarm pushes.

## Evidence (collected for wa-nu4.3.9.22)
- Last 100 CI runs on main (gh run list --workflow=CI --branch=main --limit 100):
  * 97 cancelled
  * 1 failure (databaseId 24973856126, headSha e549b5e2, 2026-04-27T02:34:59Z)
  * 2 in progress (then cancelled)
  * 0 success
- Workflow_dispatch test (databaseId 25033837579, ref main, headSha 11e22da0, 2026-04-28T04:25:25Z) was cancelled within 30 seconds by push 25033845055 at 04:25:42Z (commit 2b718f84).
- All 30 jobs in cancelled-run sample 25033710902 ended in conclusion=cancelled (no partial success bypass).

## Why it matters
wa-nu4.3.9 acceptance requires green CI on main. As long as the swarm is active, no run can finish, so the epic cannot be observed-green even if all underlying gates would pass. The earlier run that survived to a verdict (24973856126) was a failure — proof that uncancelled completion is the prerequisite for any further work, including triaging the underlying gate bugs.

## Suggested fix (smallest surface)
Option A — exempt manual dispatches from cancellation:
```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.event_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' }}
```
Allows operators to fire and observe a CI run on a stable SHA without push-cancel.

Option B — group by SHA so each commit gets its own slot:
```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
```
Higher cost but yields a verdict for every push.

Option A is the smaller diff and meets the immediate need (operator-driven proof of green).

## Acceptance
- ci.yml updated so a workflow_dispatch run on main can complete during swarm activity without being cancelled by subsequent pushes.
- A successful run on main is observed (databaseId/headSha/conclusion=success cited).
- Evidence appended to wa-nu4.3.9.

## Out of scope
- Fixing any underlying gate bugs that the run may surface (those should be filed as their own beads — including triage of e549b5e2's E0432/E0433 errors at HEAD if they persist).
- Tuning CI cost beyond the minimum needed to observe green.
close_reason: Tuned ci.yml concurrency in 05c6ff4c: group now includes github.event_name and cancel-in-progress is false for workflow_dispatch, so manual main CI proof runs no longer share the push cancel-in-progress group. Verified syntax with ruby YAML parse. Pushed main and main:master. Triggered manual ci.yml run on main at head 05c6ff4c: workflow_dispatch run 25033983588 (https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankenterm/actions/runs/25033983588), alongside separate push run 25033978961 (https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankenterm/actions/runs/25033978961). Parent epic wa-nu4.3.9 has the evidence comment; final green/failure verdict is now observable by the CI proof bead once GitHub runners complete the manual run.

title: Version/build metadata: `wa --version` shows semver + build info + enabled features
description:
# Task: Version/build metadata (`wa --version`)

## Goal
Make it easy to know exactly what build of wa is running when debugging bugs, comparing machines, or filing issues.

This becomes non-optional once we span multiple machines and (optionally) a vendored WezTerm build.

## Output contract
- `wa --version` prints a **single, stable** line by default (human-friendly, scriptable).
- `wa --version --verbose` prints a multi-line block with detailed metadata.
- Output must not require a TTY.

## Fields to include (when available)
- `wa` semver
- build timestamp (UTC)
- git commit hash (if built from a git checkout)
- rustc version
- target triple
- enabled cargo features (mcp/web/tui/sync/browser/vendored/etc.)

Vendored mode (PLAN Appendix H):
- when `--features vendored` is enabled, include:
  - vendored WezTerm commit hash (the pinned commit)
  - any compatibility/version string we can reliably extract

## Why this matters
When automation spans multiple machines, “what version is running?” is the first diagnostic question. Vendored mode adds an additional critical dimension (which WezTerm commit?).

## Testing
- Unit tests for `--version` output:
  - non-empty
  - contains semver
  - stable (no ANSI, no random ordering)

- Verbose output tests:
  - includes the detailed fields and feature list

description:
# Task: Docs smoke tests (quickstart stays executable)

## Goal
Prevent docs drift by ensuring the README/quickstart instructions remain executable and safe.

This is a user-trust feature: if the quickstart breaks, new users churn.

## Scope
- Focus on commands that docs will recommend for a fresh install:
  - `wa --help`
  - `wa --version --verbose`
  - `wa robot quick-start`
  - `wa setup --dry-run` (in a temp HOME)
  - `wa doctor` (in a minimal environment; may be expected to warn but must be actionable)

- For commands that require a real WezTerm environment, docs should point to the E2E scripts as the canonical tested path rather than embedding fragile “just run this” snippets.

## Deliverables
1) A small docs-smoke runner (CI-friendly)
- Runs in a temp HOME + temp workspace.
- Captures stdout/stderr to artifacts.
- Never modifies real user dotfiles.

2) A mapping from “docs claims” → “test coverage”
- For each quickstart step, link to either:
  - a docs-smoke command, or
  - an E2E script case (e.g., `wa-4vx.10.7`, `wa-nu4.3.3.10`).

3) CI integration
- Add a CI job/step that runs docs smoke and uploads artifacts on failure.

## Logging & artifacts (must match the E2E philosophy)
- Artifacts directory contains:
  - `env.txt` (OS, rustc, cargo, enabled features)
  - `commands.txt` (exact commands executed)
  - `stdout.txt` / `stderr.txt` per command (or per step)
  - `summary.json` (pass/fail + durations)

- Logs must never contain secrets (even if users have real configs on their machine).

## Testing
- Unit-ish tests:
  - if docs smoke is implemented as a Rust subcommand, validate output schemas and deterministic ordering.
  - if implemented as a shell script, include at least one self-test that verifies it creates artifacts and returns correct exit codes.

- CI tests:
  - docs smoke runs on every PR and fails when a quickstart command regresses.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Docs smoke runs in CI and fails when a referenced quickstart command breaks.
- Failures are diagnosable from artifacts without rerunning locally.


## Testing
- “Tests for the tests”:
  - include one intentionally-failing step under a special flag (or a dedicated CI mode) to ensure artifact capture + summaries are working.

title: [EPIC] Phase 5: Advanced — vendoring, streaming, distributed mode, coordination
description:
# Phase 5 — Advanced Features

## Objective
Push wa from "solid local orchestrator" into "fleet-grade system":
- Selective WezTerm vendoring (feature-gated) for streaming output / lower overhead.
- Real-time output streaming (reduce polling and gaps).
- Optional distributed mode: `wa-agent` near mux servers + central aggregator.
- Multi-agent coordination helpers.

## Why this phase exists
The core system can ship without this. These features are justified only when they deliver measurable wins:
- latency, correctness (fewer gaps), or usability.

## Deliverables
- Vendored client prototype + benchmarks vs CLI.
- If ROI confirmed: ship `--features vendored` with strict version checks.
- Distributed protocol design + first implementation.

## Acceptance criteria
- Benchmarks show clear advantage for vendored/streaming modes.
- Distributed mode can ingest deltas from at least one remote domain without stalling the central watcher.



## Success Criteria
- Advanced capabilities (vendoring, streaming, distributed mode, coordination) remain optional and do not compromise core safety.
- Each advanced feature has clear boundaries, tests, and safe defaults.


## Testing
- Performance ROI validation:
  - Benchmarks must prove vendored/streaming modes are meaningfully better than CLI polling for target workloads.

- Safety/regression:
  - Optional features must compile-gate cleanly and have their own unit/integration tests.

- E2E (when distributed mode is implemented):
  - Distributed E2E tests must validate persistence, ordering, and secret-safe artifacts (`wa-nu4.4.3.5`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- All items in the following sections are satisfied: Success Criteria, Deliverables.
- All Testing requirements pass (unit/integration/E2E) with the logging/artifacts described above.
- Any explicit dependencies for this bead are implemented and validated via tests or E2E artifacts.

## Cross-references
- **wa-e34d9** (asupersync epic): Advanced features in this phase — especially streaming and distributed mode — depend heavily on a mature async runtime. The asupersync migration establishes the `tokio`-based async foundation that streaming subscriptions, agent-to-aggregator connections, and coordination protocols build upon. Ensure asupersync migration is complete (or at least the core async runtime layer is stable) before implementing streaming or distributed features. Backpressure, cancellation, and graceful shutdown patterns from asupersync should be reused here rather than reinvented.

# [EPIC] Selective WezTerm vendoring

## Mission
Unlock capabilities not available via `wezterm cli`, while preserving a CLI-first default:
- zero-copy scrollback access
- real-time output streaming (enables true subscription vs polling)

## Default posture
- CLI-first remains the foundation.
- Vendoring is an **optional acceleration lane** behind `--features vendored`.

## Key risks
- Upstream API churn
- Version compatibility problems
- Larger binary / more complex build

## Definition of done
- `--features vendored` builds successfully.
- wa can detect local WezTerm version compatibility and surface it in `wa doctor`.
- Unified client picks best available backend (vendored when compatible, otherwise CLI).


## Success Criteria
- Vendored WezTerm components are minimal, clearly version-pinned, and do not break upstream compatibility expectations.
- CI validates vendor build and ensures core features still work without vendoring enabled.


## Testing
- Feature-gate tests:
  - Ensure `--features vendored` builds and unit tests run, and `--no-default-features` (or default) still works without pulling vendored deps.

- Compatibility tests:
  - Fixture-based tests for version/commit matching logic (supported/unsupported versions).
  - `wa doctor` should surface compatibility deterministically.

- RPC smoke tests:
  - Basic mux RPC framing tests with fixtures so failures are diagnosable without a live WezTerm.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All items in the following sections are satisfied: Success Criteria, Definition of Done.
- All Testing requirements pass (unit/integration/E2E) with the logging/artifacts described above.

title: DirectMuxClient: connect to mux socket + basic RPC framing (vendored)
description:
# Task: DirectMuxClient (vendored)

## Goal
Implement a direct mux client that can connect to the WezTerm mux socket and perform RPCs using vendored protocol types.

This is the foundation for vendored scrollback reads and real-time subscriptions.

## Socket discovery
- Discover mux socket path via:
  - WezTerm defaults
  - wa config override (must exist for unusual setups)
- Support multiple platforms (macOS/Linux) as needed.

## Connection + framing
- Implement:
  - connect with timeout
  - request/response framing with bounded reads
  - graceful close

## Robustness
- Never allow unbounded reads from the socket.
- Return structured errors that can be surfaced in `wa doctor` and `wa status`.
- Treat protocol decode errors as “incompatible version” signals (and fall back to CLI where appropriate).

## Testing strategy
- Offline unit tests:
  - frame encode/decode round-trips
  - truncated/invalid frames handled without panics

- Optional manual smoke:
  - on a machine with a running mux server, connect and perform a simple request (e.g., list panes)

## Acceptance Criteria
- In vendored mode, wa can connect to a running mux server and perform a simple request (e.g., list panes).
- Decode errors are handled gracefully and do not panic.

title: UnifiedClient: use vendored scrollback when available; fallback to CLI
description:
# Task: UnifiedClient backend selection

## Goal
Expose a single WezTerm client API that:
- uses vendored direct access when available and compatible
- falls back to `wezterm cli` otherwise

The rest of wa (ingest/workflows/robot/MCP) should not care which backend is used.

## Selection rules
- Prefer vendored backend only when:
  - feature `vendored` enabled
  - version compatibility checks pass
  - mux socket discovery succeeds

- Otherwise, fall back to CLI client.
- Selection decision should be observable:
  - log which backend was chosen and why (no secrets)
  - optionally expose via `wa doctor` / `wa status`

## API constraints
- Maintain a stable high-level API across backends:
  - list panes
  - read scrollback/text
  - send text / ctrl sequences

- Normalize semantics:
  - error types are consistent
  - timeouts behave similarly

## Performance expectations
- Vendored mode should be measurably faster for large scrollback reads.
- Add (or reuse) benchmarks to quantify the improvement.

## Testing strategy
- Unit tests:
  - selection logic chooses the expected backend under different synthetic conditions
  - compatibility gating behavior

- Integration tests:
  - ensure the same call (`get_text`) works in both modes (fixtures where possible)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Same high-level call (`get_text`) works in both modes.
- Vendored mode is measurably faster on large scrollback reads.
- Fallback behavior is correct and observable.

# Task: Vendoring ROI decision (go/no-go)

## Goal
Decide whether WezTerm vendoring delivers enough value to justify the maintenance cost.

description:

Without explicit maintenance infrastructure, vendored mode becomes a “rotting optional feature”.

title: [EPIC] Real-time output streaming: subscribe to pane deltas (vendored)
description:
# [EPIC] Real-time output streaming

## Mission
Move from polling-based capture to subscription-based capture when vendored WezTerm is available.

## Why
- Lower latency
- Less CPU
- Eliminates missed scrollback windows under heavy load

## Scope
- Subscribe to pane output events and feed them into the existing ingest/event bus.
- Preserve current polling path as fallback.

## Definition of done
- Vendored mode can stream deltas for a pane.
- Ingest can switch between polling and streaming based on capabilities.


## Success Criteria
- Real-time streaming of pane output is optional, performant, and does not regress ingest correctness.
- Backpressure and resource limits prevent runaway memory/CPU usage.
- Tests validate correctness under streaming and non-streaming modes.


## Testing
- Correctness tests:
  - Streaming mode must preserve the same seq/gap invariants as polling.
  - Compare streaming vs polling capture on the same fixture transcript (when possible) and assert equivalence.

- Backpressure tests:
  - Simulate slow consumers and ensure bounded queues drop/slow appropriately without unbounded memory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All items in the following sections are satisfied: Success Criteria, Definition of Done.
- All Testing requirements pass (unit/integration/E2E) with the logging/artifacts described above.
- Any explicit dependencies for this bead are implemented and validated via tests or E2E artifacts.

## Test Framework Requirements
- **LabRuntime DPOR** (Dynamic Partial Order Reduction): Use LabRuntime's DPOR scheduler to test streaming concurrency invariants. Key scenarios:
  - Multiple panes streaming concurrently into the event bus — verify no interleaving corrupts per-pane sequence ordering.
  - Polling-to-streaming mode switch mid-capture — verify no gaps or duplicates at the transition boundary.
  - Backpressure activation under concurrent producers — verify bounded queue invariants hold regardless of scheduling order.
- **Criterion benchmarks** for stream throughput:
  - `bench_stream_ingest_throughput`: Measure bytes/sec for streaming ingest of a synthetic pane output (1 KB, 64 KB, 1 MB chunks).
  - `bench_stream_vs_poll_latency`: Compare end-to-end latency from pane output emission to event bus delivery for streaming vs polling modes.
  - `bench_backpressure_overhead`: Measure throughput degradation when backpressure engages (slow consumer scenario).
  - All benchmarks must run in CI and regressions >10% should trigger warnings.

## Cross-references
- **wa-283h4.5** (Reactive dataflow graph): The streaming subscription model in this epic feeds into the reactive dataflow graph's input nodes. Ensure the stream event format (PaneDelta, GAP, detection events) is compatible with the dataflow graph's expected input schema. Backpressure signals from the dataflow graph should propagate back to the streaming layer to avoid unbounded buffering between the two systems.

title: Streaming design: event types, backpressure, integration with existing seq/gap model
description:
# Task: Streaming design

## Goal
Specify how streaming output integrates with wa’s segment/seq/gap invariants.

## Key constraints
- We must preserve monotonic per-pane `seq`.
- We must still emit explicit GAP events when discontinuities occur.
- Streaming must not overwhelm storage/event bus.

## Deliverables
- Definition of the streamed unit (bytes, lines, or “delta string”).
- Mapping to `OutputSegment` + seq assignment.
- Backpressure strategy:
  - bounded channels
  - drop policy (prefer emitting GAP over silent drop)

## Testing
- Property/invariant tests:
  - given an input stream with drops/out-of-order events, we either:
    - re-order safely, OR
    - emit a GAP deterministically (explicitly choose and lock down)

- Integration tests with a fake stream:
  - slow consumer behavior
  - bounded channel behavior
  - cancellation/reconnect paths do not leak resources

## Acceptance Criteria
- A reviewer can implement streaming ingestion from this issue alone.
- The design includes an explicit plan for invariant testing (seq monotonicity + gap semantics).
close_reason: done

title: Implement subscribe_output (vendored): stream pane output events as deltas
description:
# Task: Implement `subscribe_output` (vendored)

## Goal
In vendored mode, subscribe to pane output events and expose a stream of deltas that integrates with wa’s existing seq/gap model.

Polling scrollback works, but subscriptions enable:
- lower latency
- lower CPU
- better fidelity (fewer missed segments)

## Deliverables
- Vendored mux subscription wiring (connect → subscribe → receive events).
- Stream adapter that yields a typed event (proposed: `PaneDelta`).
- Cancellation/shutdown handling:
  - dropping the stream unsubscribes
  - process shutdown closes cleanly

## Backpressure & robustness
- The stream must not allow unbounded buffering.
  - bounded channel
  - drop policy or slow-consumer handling (explicitly choose and document)

- Handle reconnects/timeouts gracefully:
  - transient errors → reconnect with backoff
  - permanent errors → surface a structured error and fall back to polling (if caller chooses)

## Integration with seq/gap
- Define how subscription events map to:
  - seq numbers
  - gaps (if the stream reports dropped events)

## Testing strategy
- Offline unit tests with fixtures:
  - decode/encode subscription messages
  - simulate event stream and ensure adapter produces ordered deltas
  - simulate dropped/out-of-order events and ensure we emit a GAP or diagnostic

## Acceptance Criteria
