title: Recording format spec: .war file structure, delta encoding, metadata schema
description:
# Recording format specification

## Purpose
Define the .war (wa recording) file format for storing terminal sessions with efficient delta compression and rich metadata.

## Background
A good recording format must:
- Be space-efficient (delta encoding)
- Preserve timing accurately
- Include metadata for context
- Be forward-compatible (versioned)
- Be parseable without wa

## Format Structure

### File Header
```rust
pub struct WarHeader {
    magic: [u8; 4],        // "WAR\x01"
    version: u16,          // Format version
    created_at: i64,       // Unix timestamp
    pane_info: PaneSnapshot,
    metadata: RecordingMetadata,
    compression: Compression,
}

pub struct RecordingMetadata {
    title: Option<String>,
    description: Option<String>,
    agent_type: Option<AgentType>,
    tags: Vec<String>,
    total_duration_ms: u64,
    frame_count: u64,
}
```

### Frame Format
```rust
pub struct Frame {
    timestamp_ms: u64,      // Relative to recording start
    frame_type: FrameType,
    payload: Vec<u8>,
}

pub enum FrameType {
    Output(OutputFrame),    // Terminal output delta
    Resize(ResizeFrame),    // Terminal size change
    Event(EventFrame),      // wa detection event
    Marker(MarkerFrame),    // User annotation
    Input(InputFrame),      // Optional: captured input (redactable)
}

pub struct OutputFrame {
    delta: DeltaEncoding,   // Compressed diff from previous
    raw_bytes: usize,       // Original size for stats
}
```

### Delta Encoding
Use rolling hash + LZ4 for efficient storage:
```rust
pub enum DeltaEncoding {
    Full(Vec<u8>),              // Full frame (first or after discontinuity)
    Diff { base: u32, ops: Vec<DiffOp> }, // Delta from frame N
    Repeat(u32),                 // Same as previous (common for idle)
}
```

### Index Section
For fast seeking:
```rust
pub struct FrameIndex {
    keyframes: Vec<(u64, u64)>,  // (timestamp_ms, file_offset)
    events: Vec<(u64, EventId)>, // Event timestamps for annotation
}
```

## File Layout
```
[Header: 256 bytes]
[Metadata: variable, JSON]
[Frames: compressed stream]
[Index: variable]
[Footer: checksum + offsets]
```

## Versioning
- v1: Initial format
- Header includes version for forward compatibility
- Readers should reject unknown versions gracefully

## Testing
- Unit tests for encode/decode roundtrip
- Property tests for delta encoding correctness
- Fuzz tests for malformed file handling

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Format spec documented
- [ ] Header structure defined
- [ ] Frame types enumerated
- [ ] Delta encoding specified
- [ ] Index structure for seeking
- [ ] Version handling documented
- [ ] Tests for format parsing

# Recording CLI commands

## Purpose
Provide user-friendly CLI commands for recording and replaying terminal sessions.

## Commands

### wa record start
```bash
wa record start [--pane <ID>] [--title "Session name"] [--auto-stop <duration>]

# Examples
wa record start --pane 0 --title "Debugging usage limit"
wa record start --pane 0 --auto-stop 30m
```

Output:
```
Recording started for pane 0
Recording ID: rec-2026-01-18-001
Press Ctrl+C or run `wa record stop` to end
```

### wa record stop
```bash
wa record stop [--pane <ID>] [--all]

# Examples
wa record stop --pane 0
wa record stop --all
```

Output:
```
Recording stopped
Duration: 5m 23s
Frames: 1,234
Size: 256 KB (compressed from 1.2 MB)
Saved: ~/.local/share/wa/recordings/rec-2026-01-18-001.war
```

### wa record list
```bash
wa record list [--limit <N>] [--format json|table]

# Output
ID                      Duration  Size    Pane  Title
rec-2026-01-18-001      5m 23s    256KB   0     Debugging usage limit
rec-2026-01-17-003      12m 45s   512KB   1     Codex workflow test
```

```bash
wa replay <recording-id-or-path> [options]

Options:

wa replay rec-2026-01-18-001 --speed 2 --from 2m
wa replay ./my-recording.war --tui
```

### wa record info

wa record info <recording-id-or-path>

# Output

Title: Debugging usage limit

description:
# Recording export and sharing

## Purpose
Enable users to share recordings with others, including an HTML player for those without wa installed, and privacy controls for sensitive content.

## Export Formats

### Standalone HTML Player
```bash
wa record export <id> --format html --output recording.html

# Creates self-contained HTML file with embedded player
# Uses asciinema-player or custom player
# No server required - opens in any browser
```

HTML player features:
- Terminal-accurate rendering
- Speed control (0.5x, 1x, 2x, 4x)
- Pause/seek/play
- Event annotations as clickable markers
- Responsive design

### Asciinema Format
```bash
wa record export <id> --format asciinema --output recording.cast

# Compatible with asciinema.org and asciinema-player
```

### GIF Export
```bash
wa record export <id> --format gif --output recording.gif

# For documentation and quick sharing
# Configurable size, frame rate, quality
```

## Privacy Redaction

### Redaction Rules
```rust
pub struct RedactionConfig {
    patterns: Vec<RedactionPattern>,
    mode: RedactionMode,
}

pub enum RedactionMode {
    Mask,       // Replace with ***
    Remove,     // Delete entirely
    Placeholder(String), // Replace with custom text
}

pub struct RedactionPattern {
    pattern: Regex,
    description: String,  // "API keys", "passwords"
}
```

### Built-in Patterns
- API keys (sk-*, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, etc.)
- Passwords (password=*, --password)
- Tokens (Bearer *, token=*)
- Personal info (email patterns, IP addresses)

### Usage
```bash
wa record export <id> --redact-secrets --output safe-recording.war
wa record export <id> --redact-pattern "CUSTOM_SECRET_\w+" --output safe.war
```

## Sharing Workflow
```bash
# Export with redaction
wa record export rec-001 --redact-secrets --format html --output debug-session.html

# Share the file
# User opens in browser - no wa installation needed
```

## Testing
- HTML player renders correctly in major browsers
- Redaction removes sensitive content
- Export/import roundtrip preserves non-redacted content
- GIF export produces valid files

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] HTML export creates self-contained player
- [ ] HTML player works in Chrome, Firefox, Safari
- [ ] Asciinema format compatible with player
- [ ] GIF export produces reasonable quality
- [ ] Redaction removes secrets from output
- [ ] Custom redaction patterns work

}
\`\`\`

title: Coordination primitives: multi-pane selection, group locks, safe broadcast semantics
description:
# Task: Coordination primitives

## Goal
Define the primitives required for safe multi-pane workflows ("swarm" behavior) without turning wa into a chaos machine.

Multi-pane automation is powerful but risky: we need deterministic selection, locking, and per-pane auditing.

## Concepts
### Pane groups
- Define grouping strategies:
  - by domain
  - by inferred agent
  - by project (cwd-based)
- Group selection must be deterministic and explainable.

### Group locks
- Build on per-pane workflow locks to support multi-pane coordination:
  - lock acquisition across N panes is all-or-nothing (or explicitly partial with clear reporting)
  - timeouts and deadlock avoidance

### Safe broadcast semantics
- Observe each pane first.
- Only act on panes that pass preconditions (prompt state, no gap, not alt-screen, etc.).
- Execute actions with policy gating + rate limiting.
- Record per-pane results:
  - allowed/denied
  - verification success/failure
  - timing

## Testing strategy
- Unit tests with synthetic panes:
  - group selection and determinism
  - lock acquisition behavior
  - partial failure reporting

## Acceptance Criteria
- A workflow can target N panes and produce an auditable per-pane outcome.
- Preconditions prevent “spray and pray” broadcasting.

title: Performance benchmarks and budgets: Criterion suite with regression guards
description:
# Performance benchmarks and budgets (Criterion)

## Goal
Establish benchmarks for all performance-critical paths and prevent regressions with explicit, documented budgets.

This system sits on the hot path of “every command the user runs” (watch loop, pattern matching, policy checks). Performance regressions are user-visible.

## Benchmark suite (Criterion)
Benchmarks must target *real* hot paths and be runnable locally:

```rust
// benches/pattern_engine.rs
criterion_group!(
    pattern_benchmarks,
    bench_bloom_check,
    bench_aho_corasick_match,
    bench_full_pattern_pipeline,
);

// benches/ingest.rs
criterion_group!(
    ingest_benchmarks,
    bench_delta_extraction,
    bench_segment_persistence,
    bench_fts_indexing,
);
```

## What we benchmark (minimum set)
- Quick reject / prefilter:
  - `memchr`/bloom/no-match fast paths
  - worst-case “near match but reject” path
- Pattern pipeline:
  - no-hit text (must be very fast)
  - one-hit typical text
  - extraction path with captures
- Ingest/deltas:
  - delta extraction on typical scrollback
  - gap detection path
- Storage:
  - write queue throughput (bounded queue)
  - FTS indexing cost for typical segment sizes
- Query surfaces:
  - typical FTS query latency (scoped)
  - worst-case query guardrails (bounded)

## Performance budgets (absolute ceilings)
Budgets are set as “this must feel snappy to users” ceilings. Exact numbers may be tuned after first implementation, but budgets must exist before optimization work is called done.

| Operation | Budget (target ceiling) | Notes |
|-----------|--------------------------|-------|
| Bloom filter check | < 1µs | hot path prefilter |
| Pattern match (no hit) | < 10µs | must be cheap for most text |
| Pattern match (with hit) | < 100µs | includes extraction |
| Delta extraction | < 1ms | per pane per tick typical |
| FTS insert (single) | < 5ms | typical segment size |
| FTS query (typical) | < 50ms | scoped query; “feels instant” |
| Startup (no patterns) | < 100ms | CLI responsiveness |

## Regression detection strategy (CI realities)
Perf measurement is noisy on shared runners. The plan must be robust:

- Local dev loop:
  - `cargo bench` is the source of truth for tuning.
  - Provide a short “budget check” summary line per benchmark so developers can self-serve.

- CI loop (two-tier):
  1) **PR job (warn-only by default)**
     - Run benches and upload `criterion` output + a short summary artifact.
     - Fail only on catastrophic regressions (e.g., >2x slower OR exceeding a hard ceiling by a large margin).
  2) **Main/perf job (enforce budgets)**
     - Prefer a stable environment (self-hosted runner if available).
     - Enforce budgets strictly and record historical trend artifacts.

- Baselines:
  - Store a baseline artifact from main (or a tagged commit) and compare PR results against it.
  - Comparisons must ignore obviously-noisy fields and focus on timing deltas.

## Reporting
Example (desired UX):
```
$ cargo bench --bench pattern_engine

bloom_check         time:   [0.8 µs 0.9 µs 1.0 µs]  ✓ (budget: 1µs)
aho_corasick_match  time:   [8.2 µs 8.5 µs 8.8 µs]  ✓ (budget: 10µs)
full_pipeline       time:   [45 µs 48 µs 51 µs]     ✓ (budget: 100µs)
```

On regression, the report must include:
- which benchmark regressed
- old vs new timings
- which budget was exceeded (if any)
- where to find the artifacts (CI URL/path)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Criterion benchmarks exist for the minimum hot paths listed above.
- [ ] Budgets are documented and checked by an automated “budget check” step.
- [ ] CI produces artifacts for every run (raw criterion + summarized results).
- [ ] CI regression detection works (warn-only on PR; enforced on stable perf job).

## Testing
- Benchmark harness self-checks:
  - benches compile and run on supported platforms.
  - the budget-checking logic is covered by unit tests (parsing/threshold evaluation).
- CI regression guard tests:
  - include a small synthetic “known regression” fixture in test mode to verify:
    - the budget checker fails when it should
    - output includes the expected summary fields

title: Connection pooling for WezTerm: reuse mux connections when available
description:
# Connection Pooling for WezTerm

## Purpose
Reduce overhead of WezTerm CLI calls by pooling connections to the mux server.

## Current Behavior
Each WezTerm CLI call spawns a new process, connects to mux, executes, and disconnects.

## Proposed Behavior
When using vendored mode (direct mux protocol):
```rust
pub struct WezTermPool {
    connections: Vec<MuxConnection>,
    max_size: usize,
    idle_timeout: Duration,
}

impl WezTermPool {
    pub async fn execute<T>(&self, cmd: MuxCommand) -> Result<T> {
        let conn = self.acquire().await?;
        let result = conn.execute(cmd).await;
        self.release(conn);
        result
    }
}
```

## Benefits
- Avoid process spawn overhead (~10ms per call)
- Reduce socket churn
- Enable connection keepalive
- Batch multiple operations efficiently

## Prerequisites
- Requires vendored mode (bd-nu4.4.1)
- Direct mux protocol access

## Fallback
CLI mode: No pooling possible, but can batch commands.

## Benchmark Targets
- With pooling: ~1ms per operation
- Without pooling: ~10-20ms per operation
- 10x improvement for high-frequency operations

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Connection pool implemented for vendored mode
- [ ] Idle connection cleanup
- [ ] Graceful fallback for CLI mode
- [ ] Benchmark proves improvement

## Testing
- Criterion benchmarks with budgets and baseline comparison.
- Microbenchmarks for the specific optimization.
- CI regression guard with perf logs.

title: E2E script: dry-run mode (wa send/workflow --dry-run previews)
description:
# E2E script: dry-run mode (previews for wa send / wa workflow / robot)

## Goal
Validate end-to-end that `--dry-run` produces accurate previews **without mutating anything**:
- correct target resolution (pane/domain/cwd/agent)
- correct policy evaluation (allow/deny/require-approval)
- correct “what would happen” step plan for workflows
- deterministic, schema-valid JSON output for machines

This is the integration proof for the dry-run epic (`wa-1pe`) using the shared E2E harness.

## Why this matters
Dry-run is the primary trust-building UX feature:
- users can explore safely
- robots can plan before acting
- reduces mistakes and support burden

## Key constraints
- **Zero side effects**:
  - must not send input to panes
  - must not acquire workflow locks
  - must not mark events handled
  - must not create workflow executions
  - may optionally write an audit entry tagged as a *dry-run evaluation* (explicitly non-action)
- **Deterministic**: no fixed sleeps; use bounded waits/quiescence.
- **Machine-stable**: tests should prefer `--format json` outputs (avoid scraping rich/TTY output).
- Uses the standard harness contract (`wa-4vx.10.6`) and runner (`wa-4vx.10.11`).

## Test setup
- Start a WezTerm mux server and spawn dummy panes that:
  - can echo any received input to prove whether a send occurred
  - can deterministically emit patterns to create events for workflow previews
- Run `wa watch` in an isolated E2E workspace.

## Scenarios

### 1) `wa send --dry-run` preview quality
- Run: `wa send --pane 3 --dry-run "hello" --format json`
- Assert preview includes:
  - resolved pane info (pane_id, title, cwd, agent)
  - policy decision + reasons (capabilities, safety gate)
  - an explicit “would send” description (bytes/line endings/control codes)
  - an explicit “would wait-for” plan if applicable

### 2) `wa send --dry-run` on a denied state
- Create a deterministic unsafe state (fixture / dummy alt-screen).
- Run: `wa send --pane 3 --dry-run "hello" --format json`
- Assert:
  - decision is deny/require-approval as expected
  - the preview explains remediation (e.g., exit AltScreen)
  - **no text was sent** (dummy pane echo confirms)

### 3) Preview vs actual: stable-field match
Goal: the preview’s *decision* and *target* must match the actual path.
- Capture preview JSON: `wa send … --dry-run --format json > artifacts/send_preview.json`
- Execute actual send: `wa send … --format json > artifacts/send_actual.json`
- Compare only stable fields:
  - `target.pane_id`
  - `policy.decision` + `policy.rule_id` (if present)
  - `action_kind`
  - (ignore timestamps, durations, correlation ids)

### 4) `wa workflow run --dry-run` step plan preview
- Ensure a deterministic unhandled event exists (dummy pane emits marker).
- Run: `wa workflow run handle_compaction --pane 3 --dry-run --format json`
- Assert preview includes:
  - step list in order (with step ids/names)
  - per-step policy checks (or a summarized policy gate)
  - expected waits/verifications
  - explicit note that no locks will be acquired and no DB state will change

### 5) Robot dry-run output (schema + no mutation)
- Run: `wa robot send --pane 3 --dry-run "hello" --format json`
- Run: `wa robot workflow handle_compaction 3 --dry-run --format json` (or the canonical robot workflow invocation)
- Assert outputs validate against the dry-run JSON schemas and include:
  - `decision` / `would_execute=false`
  - `steps_preview` (for workflows)

## Registry
- Register this case in the E2E case registry (`wa-4vx.10.20`) with prerequisites and default inclusion status.

## Artifacts
- `send_preview.json`
- `send_actual.json`
- `workflow_preview.json`
- `dry_run_vs_actual.json` (comparison result)
- `wa_watch.log`
- `events.jsonl`
- `audit_slice.jsonl` (to prove “no action” vs “action”)

## Logging contract
Log per scenario:
- command invoked (redacted)
- timeout settings
- comparison summary (stable fields)

Example:
```
[DRYRUN_E2E] scenario=send_preview pane=3
[DRYRUN_E2E] decision=allow would_execute=false
[DRYRUN_E2E] scenario=preview_vs_actual stable_match=true
```

## Testing
- Determinism:
  - no fixed sleeps
  - every wait has a timeout and emits actionable failure output
- No-mutation proofs (pick at least two independent signals):
  - dummy pane did not echo received input
  - no new `send_text` audit action exists (only optional `dry_run` audit)
  - no `workflow_executions` row was created on dry-run
- Schema:
  - JSON outputs validate against the documented dry-run schema(s)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Dry-run output is informative (target + policy + plan).
- [ ] Dry-run never mutates panes/locks/handled state.
- [ ] Preview decisions match actual decisions on stable fields.
- [ ] Robot dry-run output is schema-valid and deterministic.
- [ ] Artifacts/logging make failures easy to debug.

title: Policy tests: capability gates, rate limiting, redaction, approval behavior
description:
# Task: Policy tests

## Goal
Prevent regressions in safety-critical logic.

Policy regressions are high-impact because they either:
- block safe operations (user-hostile), or
- allow unsafe operations (trust-destroying)

## Testing
Unit tests must cover:
- Capability gates
  - deny SendText in AltScreen
  - deny SendText when recent_gap is true
  - require prompt_active (or RequireApproval if configured)

- Rate limiting
  - per-pane/per-action budgets
  - no runaway loops

- Redaction
  - inputs and secrets never appear in logs/audit summaries

- RequireApproval + allow-once approvals
  - RequireApproval returns a scoped allow-once payload
  - approval enables ONLY the matching action fingerprint
  - TTL expiry works
  - Deny decisions cannot be overridden via approval

- **Reservations**
  - non-owner actions are denied/require-approval per config
  - owner actions are allowed
  - expired reservations are treated as no reservation

## Acceptance Criteria
- Tests fail loudly on any policy behavior change.
- Adding a new policy rule requires adding/adjusting tests.


LABELS: area-safety, area-tests, phase-1

DEPENDS ON
  → ○ bd-4vx.8: [EPIC] Safety & policy engine (capability gates, rate limits, redaction) ● P0
  → ○ bd-4vx.8.1: Define policy model: ActionKind, PolicyDecision, authorize() API (capabilities provided separately) ● P0
  → ○ bd-4vx.8.3: Secret redaction for audit logs (tokens, api keys, passwords) + safe logging conventions ● P0
  → ○ bd-4vx.8.8: PaneCapabilities derivation: PromptActive/CommandRunning/AltScreen/RecentGap (deterministic first, safe fallback) ● P0
  → ○ bd-4vx.8.9: Approval tokens (allow-once): ergonomic override for RequireApproval decisions ● P0
  → ○ bd-4vx.8.2: Rate limiting: per-pane, per-action-kind (avoid spam / runaway loops) ● P1
  → ○ bd-4vx.8.4: Policy rules loaded from config (allow/deny/require approval) + robot-safe errors ● P1
  → ○ bd-nu4.1.6.2: Enforce reservations in PolicyEngine + send paths ● P2

title: Consistent help patterns: examples, cross-references, unified style
description:
# Consistent Help Patterns

## Purpose
Make help text comprehensive, consistent, and genuinely helpful.

## Help Structure
Every command has:
1. One-line description
2. Usage synopsis
3. Options with descriptions
4. Examples (most important!)
5. See Also (related commands)

## Template
```
wa <command> - <one-line description>

USAGE:
    wa <command> [OPTIONS] [ARGS]

OPTIONS:
    -o, --option <VALUE>  Description [default: X]

EXAMPLES:
    wa <command> arg              Basic usage
    wa <command> --opt val arg    With option
    wa <command> --dry-run arg    Preview mode

SEE ALSO:
    wa related-cmd    Related functionality
    wa another        Alternative approach
```

## Implementation
```rust
#[derive(Parser)]
#[command(
    about = "Send text to a pane",
    long_about = None,
    after_help = SEND_EXAMPLES,
)]
struct SendCmd { ... }

const SEND_EXAMPLES: &str = r#"
EXAMPLES:
    wa send --pane 3 "hello"
    wa send --pane 3 --dry-run "hello"
    wa send --pane 3 --wait-for ">>>" "continue"

SEE ALSO:
    wa status       List available panes
    wa why          Explain send failures
"#;
```

## Validation
CI check ensures:
- All commands have help text
- All commands have examples
- No broken cross-references

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All commands follow consistent help template
- [ ] All commands have at least 2 examples
- [ ] See Also references are accurate
- [ ] CI validates help text completeness

## Testing
- Unit tests for completion/alias generation and help formatting.
- Integration tests for help output snapshots and no-ANSI guarantees.
- CI smoke tests for completions and help stability.

title: [Human command] `wa workflow` (run workflow manually; show step logs/progress)
description:
# Task: Human command wa workflow

## Goal
Allow humans to manually run a workflow against a pane for debugging/recovery.

## Command examples
- wa workflow run handle_compaction <pane_id>
- wa workflow run handle_usage_limits <pane_id> --force
- wa workflow show <execution_id>

## Workspace/config
- --workspace / WA_WORKSPACE
- --config (optional)

## UX
- TTY: show step-by-step progress as it runs (or tail step logs if running asynchronously).
- Non-TTY: stable JSON.

## Safety
- Same policy gates as workflows run automatically.
- Surface policy decisions clearly.

## Testing
- CLI contract tests:
  - covered by `wa-nu4.3.2.11` (args/exit codes/JSON stability)

- E2E coverage:
  - core workflow behaviors are validated by E2E scripts under `wa-4vx.10.*` (compaction, usage limits, resume-after-restart).

## Logging & debuggability
- The command output must always include (TTY or JSON):
  - `workflow_execution_id`
  - final outcome (success/aborted/denied) + reason
  - a short per-step summary (waits/sends) with redaction

This makes “what happened?” answerable without digging in DB tables.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A human can run a workflow and see a clear, minimal summary of:
  - steps executed
  - waits/timeouts
  - sends performed (redacted)
  - final outcome
